output: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany has criticized UEFA's Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, arguing that they are designed to protect the elite clubs instead of preventing bankruptcies. Last year, City was fined £50 million and required to limit their spending to £49 million this season for breaching FFP regulations. Kompany believes the regulations stifle competition and prevent smaller teams from challenging the established clubs, like Manchester United, who can spend substantially more than the FFP-regulated clubs.

Bath has signed England Sevens international Jeff Williams for the upcoming season. The 26-year-old, who has bypassed 36 tries on the World Series circuit, will join the team from the Recreation Ground. Williams, a South Africa native whose father is English, previously played for the Hamiltons club in Cape Town and had a stint in France. Bath's head coach, Mike Ford, is excited about Williams' dynamism and high-tempo playing style, which will fit the team's attacking ethos. England Sevens head coach Simon Amor lauds Williams' contributions to the squad, including his physicality and development as a player.

1. On Friday, director David Ayer unveiled the first full image of Jared Leto as the Joker in the upcoming film "Suicide Squad", with the character set to make his big-screen debut since the death of Heath Ledger.
2. The film, which is slated for release on August 5, 2016, also stars Will Smith, Margot Robbie, and a diverse ensemble of villains and anti-heroes.
3. Interestingly, Joker by Leto will appear in "Suicide Squad" without Batman as a character, marking a departure from the traditional dynamic of these DC Comics characters.

Three Florida corrections officers and a former trainee have been charged by Florida's Attorney General's office for allegedly plotting to murder a former inmate upon his release. An FBI informant, infiltrating the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, claimed that one of the officers, Thomas Jordan Driver, had a personal grievance with the targeted ex-inmate. The FBI conducted a staged murder scene to implicate the suspects, with the men showing satisfaction when presented with the photos of the fake crime scene. If convicted on one count of conspiracy to commit murder, they face up to 30 years in prison, with Florida's Attorney General Pam Bondi stating firm stance against such acts of hatred and violence.

The conference call between Manny Pacquiao and Floyd Mayweather, scheduled to discuss their upcoming boxing fight, was abruptly cancelled due to technical difficulties caused by a high number of participating boxing writers and broadcasters. Pacquiao was only able to answer one question before the call was cut short, and the event was rescheduled for another time. American boxer Mayweather is due to address the media in a conference call on Wednesday.

The Miami Open has seen a trend of celebration cakes for notable tennis victories, with Serena Williams receiving one for her 700th career win and Andy Murray for his 500th. Williams advanced to the semi-finals by defeating Sabine Lisicki in three sets, avenging her 2013 Wimbledon loss to the German player. Simona Halep defeated Sloane Stephens to set up a semi-final match against Williams.

1. Beijing International Airport is set to open the world's largest terminal, Terminal 1, in 2018, covering 700,000 square metres and designed to accommodate 45 million passengers annually.

2. The design of Terminal 1, a collaboration between architect Zaha Hadid and airport developers ADPI, aims to provide spacious, open areas, minimizing customer walking distances and increasing connectivity.

3. The massive terminal at Daxing Airport is intended to reflect a harmonious blend of Chinese culture and landscape, serving as a significant gateway for international travelers while accommodating the growing number of Chinese tourists on the world stage.

1. Manchester United manager Louis van Gaal revealed that Wayne Rooney sustained a knee injury during their defeat by Everton on Sunday; the England international was replaced by Robin van Persie in the closing stages of the game.
2. The severe nature of Rooney's injury remains uncertain, with Van Gaal stating they would have to wait and see.
3. United's loss to Everton, their first back-to-back league defeats since Van Gaal took over, leaves them fourth in the race for automatic Champions League qualification and has potentially allowed Liverpool to put more pressure on United in the race for fourth.

Jack Wilshere, despite being on Manchester City's transfer list, is recovering from ankle surgery and preparing to return to Arsenal's first team. During a day off, he shared a photo on Instagram of his shopping haul, which included various food items like cereals, eggs, baked beans, and corn on the cob. Wilshere expressed the challenge of unpacking his shopping and sought help from his followers, humorously mentioning his post-shopping exhaustion.

A Venezuelan woman, Marleni Olivo, threw a mango at President Nicolas Maduro during a rally, hoping to get his attention for her housing issue. To her surprise, Maduro not only acknowledged the incident but also promised to resolve her housing issue. The mango-throwing incident has sparked controversy, with some critics labeling it as an attempted assassination, while Olivo has insisted she had no ill intentions. Olivo's dream of owning a home before she dies may now become a reality as a result of her unusual approach.

Carlos Tevez, a former striker for Manchester United and City and currently playing for Juventus in Serie A, claims it is harder to score goals in Italy than in the Premier League. He criticizes the Premier League midfields as 'non-existent' and suggests that defending is better on the continent. Despite sitting out a game against Parma, Tevez maintains that scoring for Juventus is now "much more difficult." Tevez, who won the Champions League with Manchester United in 2008 and scored 84 Premier League goals, believes Juventus is more rounded than his previous teams and could replicate such success.

Jamie Carragher, a Sportsmail columnist, accused Yaya Toure of ducking out of a defensive wall during a free-kick situation in a Manchester City game against Crystal Palace. Carragher felt Toure, who is paid £200,000-a-week, did not do enough to prevent the winner. This incident occurred when Jason Puncheon took a free-kick that ultimately sealed Palace's victory, effectively ending City's chances of a comeback at Selhurst Park. The defeat left City nine points behind Chelsea, who also have a game in hand. Carragher criticized Toure for shying away from his defensive responsibilities during the Premier League match.

A 50-year-old Australian man, believed to be from Seymour in Victoria, died suddenly on Wednesday while on holiday in Kuta, Bali. He collapsed in the Rooftop Restaurant at the 101 Legian Hotel after telling a waitress he wasn't feeling well. Kuta, a popular destination for Australian tourists, is known for its long sandy beach, varied accommodations, and numerous restaurants and bars. An autopsy is pending to determine the exact cause of death, but external examinations suggest it was likely a heart attack.

Richie Benaud, a former Australia cricket captain and commentator, died last week at the age of 84 from skin cancer complications. His private funeral service was held on Wednesday in Sydney and was attended by ex-players Shane Warne and Ian Chappell, as well as close family and friends. Despite an offer of a state funeral from Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott, Benaud's family opted for a smaller service at the Eastern Suburbs Memorial Park. Benaud was renowned for his career in the commentating booth and was loved around the world for his distinctive voice and commentary style. Tributes were paid to him from various cricket teams and fans worldwide.

A 16-year-old named Isobel Attwood has been missing for two days. She is believed to be with a man in his twenties, and her friends have posted on social media suggesting she is in Southampton. Police are concerned for her welfare and are appealing for information to locate her. Isobel wrote a message on Facebook stating she was safe but needed to get away for a while.

Manchester City faces a £12 million pay cut for players if they fail to qualify for the Champions League this season, due to their incentivized contracts designed to meet financial fairplay requirements. After the recent Manchester derby loss to Manchester United, they are currently in fourth place, four points ahead of Liverpool who have a game against Newcastle United on Monday. Pellegrini acknowledges that City's season has disintegrated, losing seven times since the start of 2015, including early exits in the FA Cup and Champions League. Both City and United are looking to attract top-tier talent, with Paul Pogba being a potential transfer target for both clubs.

Martin Skrtel, Liverpool defender, has denied rumors of a move away from the club, stating he won't be leaving despite links to Wolfsburg and Napoli. His agent confirmed Skrtel is finalizing a new contract with Liverpool, and there's no offer from Wolfsburg on the table. Skrtel has made over 200 league appearances for Liverpool since joining in 2008.

A CEO named Cheryl Rios, from Texas, has received criticism for stating on her Facebook page that biology prevents a woman from being president due to hormones. The remark was made in reference to Hillary Clinton's announcement of her presidential run. Rios, who runs Go Ape Marketing, has defended her stance by citing "old biblical sound reasoning," but she did not reference a specific verse. Social media users have labeled Rios as a misogynist and a hypocrite for her comments. Rios has since defended her position by stating she is entitled to her opinions, despite drawing criticism. She clarified that she supports equal rights for women but believes the position of president may not be suitable for them due to their hormones.

In the Champions League quarter-final first leg between Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid, striker Mario Mandzukic was injured due to physical altercations with defenders Sergio Ramos and Dani Carvajal. Despite the bruises, Mandzukic is expected to play in the return leg at the Bernabeu on Wednesday. Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid drew 0-0 in the first leg, notable for a second half altercation. Coach Diego Simeone expects Mandzukic, favored over Fernando Torres, to line up alongside Antoine Griezmann, who has been in form with 20 goals in La Liga.

1. Jose Mourinho, Chelsea's manager, had spent the week preparing his team to counteract Manchester United's Marouane Fellaini, only to find out from a hotel doorman that it was Fellaini's twin brother (Mansour) who was present, not the actual player.
2. Mourinho's plan involved player Kurt Zouma man-marking Fellaini, with Ruben Loftus-Cheek playing the part of Fellaini in training.
3. Despite the initial confusion, Fellaini (the actual player) did indeed start the game at Stamford Bridge, and was marked by Zouma, as Chelsea won 1-0. The victory moved Chelsea within two more wins of winning the Premier League title.

A New Jersey woman named Dawn Milosky was rescued from her overturned and smoking car just before it caught fire, following a tip-off about erratic driving in Kinnelon. Officers Mark Ehrenberg and Ricky Ferriola arrived on scene, found Milosky unconscious, and managed to pull her from the vehicle in less than 3 minutes. The car was engulfed in flames approximately 30 seconds later. Milosky has been charged with driving while intoxicated, having an open container of alcohol in the vehicle, reckless driving, and failure to stay in the right lane. She was airlifted to Morristown Medical Center but is reportedly doing okay.

A farmer in eastern China, Xiao Qibin, has a six-legged goat that has been born and is growing healthily. The goat, nicknamed the 'spider goat', was born with four forelegs and two hind legs, and has become a national sensation. Xiao, who runs a goat farm in Chaohu, Anhui Province, expressed surprise at the mutation and plans to let the goat grow naturally without medical intervention.

1. West Ham United are considering a move for Javier Hernandez, the Mexican striker currently on loan at Real Madrid from Manchester United, who scored the winning goal against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League quarter-final.

2. Hernandez, 26, is unlikely to be a part of Louis van Gaal's plans at Manchester United after returning at the end of this season, making him available for around £7 million.

3. West Ham have a list of primarily young transfer targets ahead of their final season at Upton Park, including Pedro Obiang of Sampdoria, Moussa Konate of FC Sion, and Fabian Schar of Basle.

Stuart McCall, the manager of Scottish football club Rangers, has dismissed any speculation about his future being decided before the end of the season. He has been credited with restoring a positive atmosphere at the club, with three consecutive wins, including victories over Hibs and Hearts. McCall believes his side has not yet achieved anything, even though they are currently on a winning streak. Shane Ferguson, a Northern Ireland international and part of a controversial loan deal with Newcastle United, is finally set to join Rangers next week, but McCall is unsure about his readiness to play due to a long-term knee injury.

In a crucial match, Werder Bremen defeated Hamburg SV 1-0 with a late penalty by Franco Di Santo, keeping their hopes for a Europa League spot alive. Di Santo converted the penalty in the 84th minute, and Hamburg's Valon Behrami received a red card for bringing down Zlatko Junuzovic. Hamburg remains in last place, while Werder moved up to seventh position. Meanwhile, second-placed VfL Wolfsburg aims to reduce Bayern Munich's lead to 10 points when they take on Schalke 04 later on the same day, with Bayern currently at the top after their 2-0 win over Hoffenheim. Bayer Leverkusen is in third place following their 4-0 triumph over Hanover 96.

A two-year-old boy fell about 10-12 feet into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after his parents dangled him over the railing. The child was rescued by his parents before emergency services arrived and sustained minor injuries. The zoo plans to press child endangering charges against the family, with the exhibit being closed following the incident.

A Russian TV channel gave Hillary Clinton's campaign video a mature audience rating due to fears it may violate the country's anti-gay propaganda law. The rating was given due to a scene featuring a gay couple holding hands in the video. The anti-gay propaganda law, enacted in 2013, prohibits dissemination of information about gay rights to minors. There have been concerns about the law's vague language and potential infringements on free speech and human rights.

Dutch midfielder Siem de Jong returned from a collapsed lung to play 45 minutes for Newcastle Under 21s, but his comeback was cut short at halftime in a 2-0 loss to Derby County. De Jong has seen limited playing time since his transfer from Ajax last summer. Despite the setback, he might have a chance to appear in the final six matches this season. Derby's victory was secured by goals from Alefe Santos and Farrend Rawson in the second half.

A chef named Ally Lees from Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham created a giant omelette containing 12,000 calories and 945g of protein (16 times the recommended daily amount for a man) for Easter. Measuring three feet in circumference, he advises a group of no fewer than five people to attempt eating it. The massive omelette was made using 150 fresh eggs and took an hour to cook in a giant paella pan.

This summer, the Sainsbury's Anniversary Games will feature three Olympic gold medalists: Jessica Ennis-Hill (heptathlon), Mo Farah (10,000 meters), and Greg Rutherford (long jump). These athletes won their gold medals during the Super Saturday event at the 2012 London Olympics, and Ennis-Hill will be making her first appearance since giving birth last summer. The event will take place at the Olympic Stadium, from July 24-26, and is expected to be one of the biggest events in the summer sports calendar. Tickets are now available for purchase online.

A snack bar in Rio de Janeiro was found to be using the meat of slaughtered stray dogs as a filling for traditional Brazilian pastries, called pastels. The owner, Chinese Van Ruilonc, admitted to this practice and claimed to have sourced the animals from the streets of Rio. During the investigation, police discovered evidence of slave-like working conditions, including a worker being imprisoned and forced to work for 18 hours a day without pay, in a room filled with the stench of dead dogs. The public prosecutor described the conditions as among the worst he had ever seen.

The article discusses the case of Ebony Dickens, who posted violent threats against white police officers on Facebook under a fake name, Tiffany Milan. The threats lead authorities to arrest Dickens, who was charged with disseminating information related to terrorist acts. During the arrest, a firearm and three computers were found in her residence. Dickens was given a $10,000 bond and banned from social media.

PSV Eindhoven won the Dutch championship for the first time in seven seasons after a 4-1 victory over Heerenveen, with striker Luuk de Jong scoring two headed goals in the opening period. The win secured PSV's 22nd league title, second only to Ajax's 33 titles in the Netherlands. In other matches, Dordrecht moved closer to relegation following a 3-0 loss, while AZ Alkmaar ensured Europa League playoff participation with a 3-1 home win.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva was reportedly beaten to death by his school headteacher, Lalit Verma, for stealing a pencil and eraser in Railamau village, India. Verma has been charged with culpable homicide not amounting to murder and is currently in custody for questioning. This incident marks another instance of severe corporal punishment leading to a student's death in India. Previous cases include a nine-year-old boy dying after a private tutor beat him with a stick, and a young boy being thrown out of a window onto a busy road in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, following late school fee payments.

A gastrointestinal illness has affected over 100 passengers and crew on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship, with symptoms including vomiting and diarrhea. The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) is investigating the cause of the illness and plans to meet the ship in San Diego on Monday. The Celebrity Infinity has previously experienced similar outbreaks in 2006 and 2013.

A Boston Terrier named Gizmo has gained popularity online by performing a unique trick known as paw-stand walking, where he walks on his front legs while his back legs are elevated in the air. This trick was recorded at home by his owner Loren Mathieson after Gizmo tried on new black boots, and the video shows Gizmo taking several steps forward and performing graceful sidesteps. The origin of the trick was explained as Gizmo being uncertain about walking in his new boots, leading to this unexpected and entertaining performance. The video has garnered more than 80,000 views.

New Orleans, known for its lively nightlife and celebrations, implemented a city-wide smoking ban on bars, casinos, and restaurants, effective midnight on Tuesdays, as reported by the New Orleans Times-Picayune. The decision was unanimous among the city council. Bar owners have expressed concerns about potential revenue loss, while some smokers have lamented the loss of their smoking spots. A lawsuit challenging the ban has been filed by Harrah's New Orleans and other bar owners, with a hearing scheduled in a month. Despite the ban, popular tourist attractions such as Treme tours and beignet spots remain unaffected.

Manchester United's Under 21 team, captained by Adnan Januzaj, secured a 3-1 victory against West Ham United to go four points clear at the top of the Under 21 Premier League. West Ham took an early lead through Reece Oxford but responded quickly with Josh Harrop scoring twice by capitalizing on poor goalkeeping from the opposition. Despite some pressure from West Ham, the young Red Devils held on to claim all three points.

1. Brisbane's Anglican Archbishop, Phillip Aspinall, has joined a local Catholic priest in advocating for the removal of Queensland's 'gay panic' homicide defense, which reduces a murder charge to manslaughter if the defendant claims the victim made a sexual advance.

2. In a statement after an Easter Sunday mass, Archbishop Aspinall expressed his support for this initiative, emphasizing that self-defense should not condone murder under any circumstance, including sexual advances.

3. Beyond this issue, Dr. Aspinall also appealed for peace and resistance to violence in response to fear, addressing incidents of violence at anti-Islam rallies and church vandalism in Melbourne, and urging followers to rise above mistakes and honor the spirit of resurrection in daily life.

Sandra Bullock, aged 50, has been named the world's most beautiful woman of 2015 by People magazine, joining a list that includes Lupita Nyong'o (2014) and Gwyneth Paltrow (2013). Bullock, in a humble response, calls the whole notion "ridiculous" and links real beauty to being a good person, good mother, and not striving for a superficial appearance. The cover story discusses Bullock's family life with her son, Louis, 5, and her approach to fitness and aging gracefully. The choice of Bullock as the oldest woman to ever receive this honor is celebrated by some as an affirmation that beauty knows no age. Other individuals on the 2015 list include Gabrielle Union, Ariana Grande, and Laverne Cox.

An improvised bomb exploded near a U.N. vehicle in Garowe, northeastern Somalia on Monday, killing six people, including four UNICEF aid workers. The terrorist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack, which also left four UNICEF workers in serious condition. This event followed a separate incident where three African Union troops died in an ambush in Lower Shabelle region the day before. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and international representatives have strongly condemned these attacks.

A wildlife park operator named Gary Saurage, resembling a modern-day Crocodile Dundee, was called to capture a 400-pound, 11-foot alligator from a family's backyard pond in Beaumont, Texas. The image captured during the capture shows Saurage approaching the aggressive creature with bare hands, looking directly into the alligator's eyes. After successful removal, Saurage revealed the alligator, estimated to be between 35 to 40 years old, was later confirmed male and brought to his park, where it joined over 400 other alligators. Saurage emphasized that while alligators can be dangerous, they are manageable as long as people maintain a safe distance and refrain from feeding them, given their speed and hunting abilities.

In a clash in eastern Turkey, five Kurdistan Workers' Party militants were killed and another wounded, while four Turkish soldiers were wounded. The violence occurred in Agri, with the Kurds reportedly initiating the conflict while securing an area ahead of a spring festival. Both Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan strongly condemned the attack, with Erdogan viewing it as an attempt to intervene in ongoing peace talks with Kurds. Notably, the longtime leader of the Kurdistan Workers' Party, Abdullah Ocalan, has recently called for an end to violence from within prison walls. The ongoing conflict between Turkish forces and Kurdish separatists has resulted in an estimated 40,000 lives lost over more than three decades, with many seeing it as a bid for Kurdish independence or a guerrilla war with terrorist acts.

Two 18-month-old twin boys were pronounced dead at a hospital following an accident where they fell in a canal in Yuma, Arizona. The incident occurred at 9.45am on Friday, and the area is commonly used for walks and jogging. Although the exact circumstances leading to the toddlers entering the canal are unclear, investigators do not suspect foul play. Rescue efforts included the Yuma Fire Department, U.S. Border Patrol, and U.S. Marine Corps, with the boys being airlifted to the hospital after being found in the water and receiving immediate life-saving efforts.

Orlando City, an MLS team with a significant Latin-American fanbase, have shown interest in signing Javier Hernandez, a Mexican international who is currently on loan at Real Madrid but has faced struggles. Meanwhile, Manchester United are looking to retain midfielder Andreas Pereira, as several European clubs express interest in signing him, if he chooses not to agree to new terms with United.

Joel Burger, 24, and Ashley King, 23, got engaged, favoring a humorous nickname given to them in fifth grade as "Burger King." They plan to celebrate their marriage with a creative twist, using personalized Burger King cups for drinks at their wedding. The couple met in kindergarten, became more than friends during college years, and are fond of the persistent teasing they receive from their friends.

A hit band from the 1960s, unnamed in the article, is linked to a notorious paedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London, along with the disgraced BBC star Jimmy Savile. This information is from a secret police intelligence report from 1964, with no confirmation if they attended the brothel at the same time. The brothel was investigated in 2013 by Detective Superintendent David Grey when it was mentioned in another police report, but there is no clear evidence suggesting a direct connection between the band and Savile. Savile was a regular visitor to the brothel in the 1970s.

A six-year-old German Shepherd named Sadie, once rescued from a shelter, has been filmed playing an electric keyboard at home in Alberta, Canada. She demonstrates her musical skill by positioning her front paws on the keyboard and sitting on a piano stool, appearing to perform a minimalist, unconventional piece. Footage of the unusual performance has garnered over 12,000 views online, with many viewers praising Sadie's performance. Her owner notes that Sadie enjoys learning new tricks and recently mastered piano playing skills.

A 22-year-old man named Ivan Balashov, while shopping for phones in Novokuznetsk, Russia, took a selfie with a phone he found unappealing, then stole another one. He was caught when the shop identified him from the selfie. He denied being at the shop but was later found guilty and given a three-month suspended sentence.

The first trailer for a documentary titled "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name" about the life and music of late British singer Amy Winehouse was released, set for UK release on July 3. Winehouse, known for her struggle with drugs and alcohol, discusses her ambivalence towards fame in the trailer, expressing concern about the potential impact it could have on her. The documentary has been endorsed by Winehouse's family, featuring extensive unseen archive footage and previously unheard tracks, and has been produced by the team behind the award-winning documentary "Senna." A U.S. release date for the film has yet to be announced.

This week, "The Big Bang Theory" (Thursday 8 p.m. ET, CBS) is a must-watch with the return of Christine Baranski and Laurie Metcalf as the mothers of Leonard and Sheldon. "Saturday Night Live" (Saturday May 2 at 11:30 p.m., NBC) features Scarlett Johannsson as host. "Mom" (Thursday 9:30 p.m., CBS) is concluding its season with Allison Janney delivering Emmy-worthy performances. "Backstrom" (Thursday 9 p.m., Fox) is ending its season, with potential for renewal in the fall. "Blue Bloods" (Friday 10 p.m., CBS) is concluding its two-part season finale, although its future is uncertain. "Younger" (Tuesday 10 p.m., TV Land), a charming comedy, has been renewed for a second season, making this a great time to tune in.

The Downton Abbey character Violet, Countess of Grantham, played by Dame Maggie Smith, may return in a new series created by Julian Fellowes called The Gilded Age, set in the high society of New York in the late 19th century. The potential return of Robert, Earl of Grantham, and his wife Cora, who is American-born, is also hinted at, with Violet appearing as a younger character. NBC is currently excited about the production of The Gilded Age, aiming to recreate the atmosphere of the Downton Abbey period, focusing on the wealthy industrialists of the time. The new series is expected to air as early as September.

Steven Gerrard, who is nearing the end of his tenure with Liverpool, is set to start in their FA Cup semi-final against Aston Villa at Wembley. This will mark his 36th and potentially final game at Wembley. Gerrard has been out for a month due to a three-match ban, but he is now back in the starting lineup. Manager Brendan Rodgers has praised Gerrard, referring to him as a "special player" who has consistently delivered significant moments and goals in major matches.

A new, original Dr. Seuss book titled "What Pet Should I Get?" is set to be released on July 28, with pre-orders exceeding expectations. The book, featuring the spirited siblings from "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish," was penned between 1958 and 1962, and its manuscript and illustrations were found in Geisel's home shortly after his death in 1991. Random House Children's Books anticipates releasing more books from discovered materials.

Jessica Carey drove three hours to surprise her grandmother with a surprise tattoo, which was a portrait of her grandmother as a younger woman. The tattoo was made by her husband Aaron, and it brought about a heartwarming emotional reaction from Patty Lawing. The special moment was captured on video, which was later shared online.

Annegret Raunigk, a 65-year-old mother-of-13 from Berlin, is preparing to give birth to quadruplets in a matter of weeks, making her the oldest woman in the world to have quadruplets. Despite undergoing 18 months of fertility treatment and approaching retirement, Raunigk feels fit and not overly concerned about the upcoming birth. The father's identity remains unknown, and Raunigk previously made headlines in Germany for giving birth to her youngest daughter at the age of 55.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, has announced plans to launch an unmanned rover on the moon by 2018, joining an exclusive group of nations with lunar exploration. The mission, called SLIM (Smart Lander for Investigating Moon), is expected to cost between $83.4 million and $125 million. Its purpose includes perfecting soft-landing technologies and utilizing face recognition software for surface navigation. This mission could be Japan's response to Chinese and Indian successes in recent years, with the landing site determined by data gathered by Japan's previous lunar orbiter, SELENE (Kaguya), launched in 2008.

1. Brazilian football clubs have imposed precautions amid a surge of dengue fever cases, as three players have been diagnosed with the mosquito-borne illness, including Corinthians striker Paolo Guerrero, forcing some players to miss crucial matches.
2. Three Brazilian football players have contracted dengue fever, with Paolo Guerrero of Corinthians and Leo Cittadini of Santos being the most notable, and the health ministry reported over 460,000 cases in the country this year, accounting for nearly 5,000 cases daily.
3. Players from affected clubs have resorted to using insect repellent during practice sessions, avoiding short sleeves and pants, and training facilities have been inspected for mosquito breeding sites. Brazilian clubs, such as Corinthians and Sao Paulo, have responded proactively to the outbreak, in a bid to maintain player health and prevent further infections.

James Wilson, a 19-year-old striker for Manchester United, has expressed his admiration for teammate Wayne Rooney's free-kick ability, emphasizing Rooney's daily practice and consistent accuracy. Wilson also appreciates Robin van Persie's movement and Radamel Falcao's predatory instincts in the penalty box, hoping to emulate these qualities in his own game. Wilson has scored one Premier League goal this season and previously stated his desire to learn from these three experienced forwards.

A 2-year-old child was struck and killed by a van in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The driver, identified as Archie Brown Jr., was then shot dead at the scene, potentially as an act of revenge. A 15-year-old boy also died from gunshot wounds, though the connection to the initial accident is unclear. The police are still investigating the incidents and have not yet identified any suspects.

A minor boy from Memphis, Tennessee, has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers with posts featuring him posing with guns, drugs, and explicit language, prompting criticism from community members. Despite the backlash, the boy defends himself, claiming he's had a tough year and the criticism is stressing his mother. Ongoing concerns exist about the use of Twitter for perpetuating gang culture, with approximately half of organized gangs in the U.S. maintaining a social media presence.

1. Former Redgum frontman John Schumann firmly denounced anti-Islam protesters for using his song "I Was Only 19" during a Reclaim Australia rally, stating that the song promotes messages of compassion, tolerance, and inclusiveness.

2. Saturday's Reclaim Australia protests, which aimed to oppose 'sharia law, halal tax, and Islamization', led to violence, clashes with anti-racism groups, and arrests across multiple locations, including Melbourne and Brisbane.

3. Federal Opposition Leader Bill Shorten expressed his disapproval of the violence at the protests, stating that there is no place for violence in any protests or expressions of freedom of speech, while also discrediting the claims that Muslims were planning to bring Sharia law to Australia.

Emmanuel Adebayor, Tottenham striker, has publicly stated his intention to stay with the team and fight for his place, disregarding transfer speculation. Despite an underwhelming performance against Sheffield United and a significant decline in form since his 2011 arrival, highlighted by Harry Kane's rise, Adebayor remains committed to his contract with Tottenham. He has made limited appearances this season, scoring only twice.

1. Manuel Pellegrini, the manager of Manchester City, is being urged by Stuart Pearce to be given more time to turn around the club's struggling fortunes, despite a faltering title challenge and a battle to secure a top-four finish.

2. Former City player and manager Pearce believes City should maintain stability, with Pellegrini, and is advocating for a more measured approach to managerial changes, citing the club's expectation to consistently contest the Champions League and win the Premier League.

3. Yaya Toure, a key player for City, has been cited by Pearce as a significant factor in the team's poor performance this season, with his inconsistent form and frequent absences for African Nations tours impacting negatively on the team.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce remains optimistic about keeping Hull City in the Premier League despite a 2-0 loss to Southampton, targeting 8-9 wins to secure safety. Hull have struggled with long-term injuries to key players, including Mohamed Diame, James Chester, Michael Dawson, Nikica Jelavic, and Robert Snodgrass. Southampton moved up to fifth place, but manager Ronald Koeman had to intervene after Sadio Mane tried to take a penalty not given to James Ward-Prowse, causing him to remind his squad about team rules.

A terror alert was triggered in Reading, UK after a dummy wearing a balaclava and holding a fake missile launcher was spotted on a boat sailing down the Thames. Thames Valley Police and an Army bomb disposal team were called, but after inspecting the missile, they determined it was purely ornamental. A local resident condemned the prank as reckless and potentially alarming, given the current state of global terrorism.

Tiger Woods suffered a bizarre injury during the Masters tournament on Sunday, hitting a tree root with his club, causing a painful yelp, and briefly popping a ligament in his right wrist. He managed to finish the competition at 5-under-par, despite the injury. Despite ending 13 strokes behind the winner, 21-year-old Jordan Spieth, Woods' finish was his best in over a year.

Iker Casillas, a long-time goalkeeper for Real Madrid, has stated his intention to remain at the club despite potential competition from David de Gea. Casillas, who has been at Real Madrid since his breakthrough at 16, wants to fulfil his contract and compete for the number 1 jersey. Prior to focusing on the Champions League, Casillas aims to help Real Madrid defend their title, having recently progressed to the semi-finals.

A video has surfaced of a failed S300 missile launch in Russia, where the rocket barely lifts off and plummets back down, followed by a loud explosion. This incident, which occurred in an unknown location, is believed to involve Russian-backed militia and may have happened near Donetsk in Ukraine. After the initial explosion, a second missile was successfully launched from the wreckage, potentially aimed at government forces. This incident could be an embarrassment to Russian President Vladimir Putin, who has significantly increased the Russian defense budget over the past year.

James Faulkner, the Australian World Cup-winning all-rounder, has signed to join Lancashire for the majority of this summer. He will replace Peter Siddle, who will initially play in Lancashire's first four LV= County Championship matches before joining the Australia squad. Faulkner is enthusiastic about joining Lancashire, citing the club's rich history and the benefits of playing in English conditions for his career. Lancashire's head coach, Ashley Giles, is equally excited about the addition, emphasizing Faulkner's international pedigree and his impressive first-class cricket record.

Mary Kay Letourneau Fualaau, once a 34-year-old teacher who engaged in a scandalous relationship with her 13-year-old student, is now happily married to her former student Vili Fualaau and they are parents of two teenage girls. In an upcoming interview with ABC's "20/20," the couple, who will celebrate their 10th wedding anniversary on May 20, will discuss what keeps their relationship strong, Mary Kay's plans to return to teaching, and her efforts to have her status as a registered sex offender lifted. Vili Fualaau will also share his experiences with alcoholism, depression, and his beliefs about how the system failed him as a minor.

Jamie Carragher, a former Liverpool player and current sports pundit, travelled to Girona, Spain to watch his son James play in the Under 12s edition of the Mediterranean International Cup. The tournament features over 200 clubs from 36 countries. Carragher bystanded the Liverpool U12s match against CE Mercantil, where they drew 1-1, and also posed for a picture at the opening ceremony. Notable alumni of the tournament include Lionel Messi, Cesc Fabregas, and Philippe Coutinho.

A Seattle-based filmmaker, Gabriel Ng, utilized a drone to capture breathtaking footage of Thailand's visual wonders, showcasing the country's stunning coastline, religious sites, and everyday life. His six-minute video, predominantly filmed on Ko Samui, presents breathtaking scenes such as the Big Buddha Temple, fishermen preparing their nets, and calm river landscapes. The visually engaging video, featuring a diverse mix of sceneries, has been popular among YouTube viewers, receiving praise for its Discovery Channel-like quality.

1. Despite a past conflict with Michael Vaughan, Peter Moores has expressed willingness to work with Vaughan if he becomes England's new director of cricket.

2. Moores has stated that he is uncertain about the necessity of another voice in the England dressing room for the new director.

3. The departure of Paul Downton, who brought Moores back as coach, has been confirmed, with Vaughan firmly in contention for the position of managing director of England cricket. Moores remains committed to his coaching role and is eager to focus on the upcoming Test series.

Nottingham Forest plans to renew its bid for £10million-rated Blackburn striker Jordan Rhodes this summer, having failed to sign him on loan in March. Rhodes, who has scored 70 goals in the last three seasons, has been a target for Forest, Derby, Norwich, and Middlesbrough by Blackburn, who have so far resisted all bids. Meanwhile, Blackburn manager Gary Bowyer anticipates interest in Rhodes' strike partner Rudy Gestede, who scored 19 goals this season, with Hull, Crystal Palace, West Brom, and Southampton reportedly considering a move.

A three-dog band consisting of a Husky named Sky, two Springer Spaniels named Sadie and Marshall, harmoniously performed a melodious ensemble by howling and barking in their North Carolina home. The performance began with Sadie barking, which triggered Sky's howling, leading Sadie to follow suit. Meanwhile, the third Springer Spaniel wagged its tail in excitement. The climax of the performance featured all three dogs howling together in unison, with the Husky adding a deep, growl-like sound to their harmony. The owner interrupted the performance, and the dogs stopped howling in surprise.

The French Spiderman, Alain Robert, completed a daring climb of Dubai's twisting 75-storey Cayan Tower without the use of a safety harness or other equipment, using only sticky tape and chalk. The 52-year-old climber, who has survived falls during previous climbs, took approximately an hour and a half for the ascent, with hundreds of spectators watching. Robert is known for his illegal ascents and has been previously arrested, imprisoned, and banned from locations worldwide. The climb was captured on video and shows him struggling to find footing on the narrow ledges, as well as waving a flag as a tribute to the Cayan Group for permitting the climb. In 2011, Robert climbed the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest tower, with a harness and rope in compliance with regulations.

An experimental cancer drug, AZDO5030, developed by Astra Zeneca and initially discarded due to poor cancer results, has shown potential in reversing the effects of Alzheimer's. The drug works by blocking a process that breaks nerve connections in the brain used for memory storage. Researchers at Yale University are now conducting human trials on Alzheimer's patients to assess its effectiveness. Dr James Pickett of the Alzheimer's Society expresses optimism about the drug's repurposing for Alzheimer's treatment, noting its potential to lead to clinical trials and new treatments sooner.

1. In the upcoming "Avengers: Age of Ultron," Paul Bettany will play the android character Vision, a member of the superhero group in the comics. This was confirmed by a poster released by Marvel Studios.
2. Thursday saw the reveal of the real Daredevil suit from the Netflix series starring Charlie Cox, a new character announcement for "X-Men: Apocalypse" with Ben Hardy playing Angel, and a disclosure on Jamie Bell's character The Thing in the "Fantastic Four" reboot.
3. The widespread release of new superhero-related images over 24 hours indicates that the superhero trend in media remains strong and continues to capture public interest.

Kenny Bayless, a highly-regarded referee with experience overseeing both Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao's fights, has been selected to officiate their upcoming boxing match, considered historic and financially significant. This appointment has raised concerns, as Oscar De La Hoya, a past Mayweather opponent, believes Bayless' officiating style may give an unfair advantage to Mayweather, suggesting it could influence close decisions in their favor. De La Hoya won the WBC light middleweight title against Mayweather in a split decision loss in 2007.

Harry Kane's participation in the Under 21 European Championship in June is uncertain due to Tottenham's planned friendly match in Malaysia, scheduled for May 27. Mauricio Pochettino, Spurs manager, has expressed concerns about Kane's potential burnout, possibly preventing him from representing England's Under 21 team. Kane, who scored 79 seconds into his England debut last month, has been told he will not be required for senior international matches against the Republic of Ireland (June 7) and Slovenia (June 14), but has shown interest in playing for Gareth Southgate's Under 21 side.

The California Department of Public Health declared an end to a measles outbreak that affected over 130 people since December, after 42 days without a new case. The outbreak began with visits to two Disney theme parks, and most of the patients were unvaccinated, accounting for 70% of those for whom vaccine status was known. Two new cases with a different measles genotype were identified in April. Measles is a highly contagious respiratory disease that causes fever, red eyes, runny nose, cough, and a rash, and can lead to severe health complications like pneumonia and encephalitis. The disease is spread through contact with an infected person via coughing or sneezing, and can remain in the air and on surfaces for up to two hours.

A family-of-six, comprising two adults and four children, has been sought by police in Argentina after they were photographed riding without helmets on a single motorbike in the city of San Miguel de Tucuman. The children sat on the petrol tank while the man gripped the handlebars, and the woman sat behind them. This case follows a similar incident where a family of seven was spotted riding on one motorbike in the city of Junin just weeks prior. Both incidents have been widely condemned on social media for being irresponsible and dangerous. Police are urging anyone who recognizes the families to come forward.

Andrea McVeigh, a 44-year-old social media manager, was seriously injured after being knocked down by a cyclist riding on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London. The cyclist fled the scene, initially stopping and appearing to lock his bike up before speeding off. McVeigh sustained significant facial injuries, including two three-inch gashes to her forehead, and is currently off work due to her injuries. Police have issued CCTV footage of a cyclist they want to speak to in connection with the incident and are appealing for witnesses.

In the Washburn Street Cemetery in Scranton, Pennsylvania, the headstone of Hillary Clinton's father, Hugh Rodham, was found tipped over on Monday, just two days after Clinton announced her run for the White House. Local resident Paul McGloin, who tends to Rodham's grave, found the headstone in this state and is not sure if it was a case of vandalism or weather-related damage. Police are investigating the incident and suspect vandalism as the most likely cause, with funeral director Neil Regan sharing similar sentiments. Local resident McGloin questions if this occurrence was a coincidence, given its timing with Clinton's presidential announcement.

A California woman, Beatriz Paez, claims a U.S. Marshal broke her phone and interrupted her recording of a police incident in South Gate, California. Paez has filed a complaint and is considering a lawsuit. The police department does not have authority over U.S. Marshals, complicating Paez's official complaint. U.S. Representative Janice Hahn wants a federal investigation into the Marshall's actions, arguing they were illegal as Paez was not hindering an investigation or arrest.

Max, a husky-corgi hybrid, stands at 18.5 inches tall and was abandoned in Essex, sought refuge at the Dogs Trust. Despite his small stature, Max is a fully-grown canine. His unique origin stems from a stray corgi and a Siberian husky, possibly belonging to the explorer Sir Ranulph Fiennes. With a gentle, intelligent, and big-hearted nature, Max is currently seeking a new home. The increased popularity for huskies, such as Max, is partly due to shows like Game of Thrones. However, owners often underestimate the specific care requirements for these breeds, leading to abandonment. There are currently 54 other wolf-like breeds in the care of the Dogs Trust.

Chilean pickpockets are the most successful thieves currently active in central London, according to undercover police teams. These groups, often consisting of 3-6 members, follow wealthy shoppers in the West End, specifically targeting tourists. Notably, two Chilean women were stopped by police after targeting rich Arab tourists in Park Lane and Mayfair. The Metropolitan Police are actively attempting to reduce pickpocket crimes in busy shopping areas like Oxford Street, with DC Darren Bond's team experiencing a 50% reduction in thefts over the past year. However, a significant number of arrested pickpockets have been Romanian or Bulgarian, with Chileans making up about 5% of the total. According to DC Bond, the crimes are part of an organized, international network, with thieves periodically moving to different European cities to avoid detection.

A driver in his 20s survived a severe car accident where his vehicle flipped over and he was trapped under it. Emergency services, including firefighters, spent 25 minutes using specialized equipment to free him. He was conscious throughout and suffered head, chest, and suspected leg fractures, as well as injuries to his pelvis and sternum. Despite the severe injuries and the nature of the crash, the man was praised for his survival and was taken to University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire by air ambulance.

A significant pile of 40 tonnes of industrial waste, estimated to have been transported by three tractors and trailers, was illegally dumped in a Suffolk village, Walsham-le-Willows. The waste, which is believed to originate from the carpet and veterinary industries, was described as "horrific" and the worst sighting in 28 years by PC Mark Bryant, a rural crime officer. The police, National Farmers' Union, and Country Land and Business Association are currently working on a campaign to prevent fly-tipping, with this incident, considered the worst, reported to have occurred recently.

A man at Toronto's Pearson International Airport was Tasered after he refused to comply with security protocol, attempted to enter a restricted area, and refused to board a Turkish Airlines flight. The incident was captured on video, and the man, who appeared to be mentally disturbed, could be seen holding a black briefcase tightly. He was later handcuffed and taken to a hospital under Canada's Mental Health Act. It is unclear whether authorities will pursue criminal charges against him.

A government jet carrying Serbia's President Tomislav Nikolic to Italy last week had to return to Belgrade due to a co-pilot spilling coffee on the instrument board, causing turbulence and the emergency slat button to be activated. An investigation found that this incident, resulting in a near crash, was due to the co-pilot's accidental activation of the emergency slat button after trying to wipe coffee off the instrument panel. The civil aviation authorities briefly suspended the co-pilot's license after the incident.

In South Africa, over 300 suspects have been arrested for deadly attacks on foreigners that have prompted thousands to flee, with the government denouncing these acts of violence. These incidents took place in Durban, resulting in the deaths of two immigrants and three South Africans. The government has praised law enforcement agencies for preventing further bloodshed, while stressing that these attacks are not representative of all South Africans. Efforts are being made to provide support and refuge for those affected, with the Gift of the Givers charity offering shelter in Johannesburg and President Jacob Zuma expressing his support for displaced foreign nationals. This latest wave of xenophobic attacks follows previous incidents in 2008, where many victims were Zimbabwean immigrants.

In Revelstoke, Canada, photographer Zach Birnie was filming the scenic mountainside when an unexpected avalanche occurred while he was skiing off-piste. The skier manages to survive with only a slight shoulder injury, but is submerged beneath the snow for a terrifying period. Cornelia Accola from the WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF theorizes the fresh snow and steep terrain might have caused the avalanche. She advises that in similar situations, individuals should let go of their ski poles, attempt to open bindings, pull knees to chest, and cover face with arms if caught in an avalanche.

On the hottest day of the year, two men robbed an Esso petrol station in Surrey's Caterham, stripping off their shirts before the robbery. Police have released CCTV footage of the incident and are requesting the public's help in identifying the men. A third individual, also in his 20s, was arrested and later released on bail as the investigation continues. The men are suspected of burgling the manager's office in search of cash, but they only managed to steal a mobile phone before fleeing when disturbed by a staff member. No one was injured during the incident.

The article discusses the Lada Niva 4x4, a rugged and affordable Russian-made 4x4 vehicle priced at £13,395 on the road. With the Land Rover Defender discontinued, there might be an increase in sales for the Lada Niva, which has gained international popularity due to its robust nature and distinctive appearance. The Lada Niva, available as a compact van for £10,590, is a no-frills vehicle with a plastic interior that's easy to clean after off-road adventures. Notably, despite being a Russian brand, the Niva driven by Vladimir Putin in 2009 was equipped with a German engine.

A lawsuit accuses the AIDS Healthcare Foundation, the nation's largest supplier of HIV/AIDS medical care, of a $20 million dollar scam involving kickbacks for patient referrals to boost funding from federal health programs. This alleged practice was key to the company's business model. The suit was filed by three former managers who were later fired after reporting the issue, which the foundation denies, stating they are not guilty of wrongdoing. The lawsuit has been supported by the federal government and the state of Florida, who declined to intervene.

A bearded dragon named Liz, owned by Shannen Hussein, has demonstrated an unusual ability to understand English commands, primarily responding "yes" when asked if she's hungry. This has been shown in a video taken at mealtime where she nods in response to "Are you hungry?" Liz appears to be fond of superworm treats and will often go to great lengths to get one. Shannen also has a popular social media following, with her pet sheep, Winter, famous for its antics on Vine and various other platforms. The farm where Liz resides also houses various other pets, such as cats, birds, a snake, ducklings, turtles, a llama, and what seems to be an emu.

Travis Hatfield, a 21-year-old aspiring country singer from West Virginia, posted a video of himself singing a George Jones hit to his uncle, Jamie Joe Cline, who has Down syndrome. The heartwarming performance, featuring the two singing He Stopped Loving Her Today, went viral with over 410,000 views. Hatfield asserts that his uncle, who lives with him, has been an influential figure in his life and inspires his music, which is a blend of George Jones, Jason Aldean, and Brantley Gilbert, among others. Hatfield, who dreams of becoming a country singer, has received offers from Nashville record labels and plans to audition for The Voice's 2016 season. He is currently working on a CD of original songs.

High-wire performer Nik Wallenda has announced his latest stunt, an untethered walk on the turning Orlando Eye observation wheel in Florida on April 29. The event takes place at the Orlando Eye, part of a new entertainment complex, which opens to the public on May 4. Nik Wallenda, a seventh-generation member of the Flying Wallenda family, known for death-defying feats like walking across the Grand Canyon and Niagara Falls, has previously walked on a Ferris wheel but considers the Orlando stunt unique due to its size and absence of a pole.

Bayern Munich's central defender Medhi Benatia could miss both legs of the Champions League quarter-final against Porto due to a muscle injury sustained in the German Cup last eight against Bayer Leverkusen. The defender is expected to be out for between two to four weeks, joining a list of injured players that includes Bastian Schweinsteiger, David Alaba, Javi Martinez, and reserve keeper Tom Starke. Bayern manager Pep Guardiola has a depleted squad as he prepares for domestic and European competition, with Franck Ribery and Thiago Alcantara recently returning from injuries. Despite the injuries and currently leading the Bundesliga by 10 points, Bayern is still aiming for three titles.

Bayern Munich, under the management of Pep Guardiola, secured a resounding 6-1 victory over Porto in the Champions League quarter-final second leg, bringing their season goal tally to an incredible 115. With five Bundesliga matches remaining, the German giants aim to reach a third consecutive title, the German Cup semi-final, and potentially multiple Champions League matches if they progress further. Top scorer Robert Lewandowski contributed three goals during the triumphant run.

Fernando Torres, a former player of Atletico Madrid, has credited manager Diego Simeone as the key to the team's success, which includes six consecutive victories over Real Madrid. Simeone's leadership has allowed Atletico to exceed expectations and compete with top European teams, while also emphasizing the importance of playing at their limit due to limited room for error. Additionally, Torres and several other Atletico players are one yellow card away from suspension in the upcoming Champions League quarter-final against Real Madrid.

A small aircraft carrying two passengers went missing and was later found crashed near Loch Etive in western Scotland, leading to a large-scale rescue operation involving helicopters, lifeboats, and police. The plane had been believed to be traveling from central Scotland to Tiree, and it is reported that the aircraft lost radar contact near Beinn Nan Lus. Authorities are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the crash, and the families of the victims are being contacted.

A bus collided with a Boeing 777 jet from Uzbekistan Airways at Tashkent airport, causing significant damage to the plane's engine. The incident resulted in potential flight delays as it occurred at one of the busiest airports in Central Asia. This event is similar to earlier incidents where Ryanair planes have collided at Dublin Airport, and a British Airways plane hit a hangar at Heathrow Airport. It's unclear if anyone was injured in these events, although they have caused significant disruptions for numerous passengers.

An off-duty Secret Service agent, identified as Arthur Baldwin, was arrested in south-eastern Washington D.C. early Friday morning on charges of attempted burglary and property damage. The incident occurred on the 3200 block of D Street SE. Baldwin, a member of the Foreign Missions Branch, has since been placed on leave, and his security clearance was revoked. This arrest follows close on the heels of a high-ranking supervisor also being put on leave for alleged misconduct, which is currently being investigated by the Homeland Security Department's inspector general. These incidents pose a further challenge to the Secret Service, whose role involves protecting the president and his family.

Israel is developing a new, high-tech system to accurately detect tunnel activity, initially focused on the Gaza-Israel border. The system, costing approximately £2.3 million ($3.5m) per mile to install, consists of sensors that are claimed to have no false alarms. This comes after more than 700 proposals were considered in response to a perceived tunnel threat. The aim is to provide additional security for residents, particularly in regions affected by ongoing conflicts between Israel and Gaza. Initial tests have shown success, with further results planned in the next few months.

A primary school headteacher has implemented a water-only policy during school hours to promote long-term health, banning all drinks except water. Some parents have launched a campaign, arguing that the rule is too strict as many children dislike water and might go without a drink all day. The school defends the decision, citing health benefits, while some parents believe it should be their choice what their child drinks.

Paul Smith has secured a highly challenging fight against Andre Ward on June 20, and although it won't involve Ward's WBA super-middleweight world title, it presents a significant opportunity for Smith, who has previously contested for Arthur Abraham's WBO belt. Smith, who is known for outclassing Carl Froch in 2011, is enthusiastic about facing Ward, who has been inactive since 2013. Ward, the top-ranked pound-for-pound fighter, has expressed his excitement about returning to the ring in Oakland, California, but acknowledges Smith as a formidable opponent.

Angela Merkel, the German Chancellor, and her husband Joachim Sauer are spending their annual Easter holiday on the Italian island of Ischia, traditionally at the luxurious Miramare Spa Hotel. Due to the weather not being as sunny as expected, Merkel has been focusing on her health, reportedly enjoying Pilates classes and vegetarian meals, with a private Pilates instructor hired for the holiday. Her husband, a professor of theoretical chemistry, is often private and avoids the limelight, as seen in his decision to watch Merkel's inauguration on TV rather than attend in person.

Ander Herrera, a Spanish midfielder playing for Manchester United, has an unusual shooting habit – he often scores goals with his eyes closed. This peculiarity was displayed again during a game against Aston Villa, as Herrera netted a brace without looking at the goal. Louis van Gaal, Manchester United's manager, has praised Herrera's shooting skill but has encouraged him to be more composed and control the ball before shooting. This unusual shooting style is not entirely new, as Herrera has been seen scoring goals with closed eyes even in previous games, such as for Spain's Under 20 side and during matches against Queens Park Rangers, Leicester, Preston, Swansea, and Yeovil Town.

A 23-month-old girl sadly passed away in North Las Vegas after being unintentionally hit by her father's pickup truck in the driveway. The family was unaware that the toddler had left the house and reached the driveway. Officials are treating the incident as an accident and no charges have been filed. The identities of the family members involved have not been disclosed.

The University of Connecticut baseball team has welcomed a new member, 5-year-old Grayson Hand who is battling leukemia, as part of a program by Team IMPACT. Grayson will have his own locker with the team and can attend as many games and practices as he likes. His sister, Sophie, has been named an honorary cheerleader, and the Hand family considers this partnership as a tangible representation of the emotional support they've received during this difficult time.

London Midland has committed to providing CCTV footage of a passenger who defecated in a train carriage during a service between Lichfield Trent Valley and Longbridge, leading to severe delays and cancellation of the Cross City line service. The incident forced the train operator to terminate the service at Birmingham New Street for cleaning. London Midland has stated that they will hand over CCTV images of the culprit to the police for investigation.

James Rodriguez, the Real Madrid midfielder, has been praised by Spanish newspaper Marca for his impressive form and significant impact since joining from Monaco last summer. The Colombian star, dubbed 'the jewel in Real Madrid's crown', has contributed 13 goals and 12 assists, with the team winning 80% of games when he's on the field compared to 58% when he's not. Marca credits him for living up to his £60million price-tag and becoming a fan favorite. In a separate report, AS is focusing on Real's appeal against Cristiano Ronaldo's yellow card for diving in a recent game, with the competition and appeals committee set to meet on Friday. In Italy, La Gazzetta dello Sport is reporting on Roberto Mancini's plans for a summer overhaul at Inter Milan, with the list including Yaya Toure, Filipe Luis, and Lucas Leiva from the Premier League, as well as Barcelona's Pedro and Palermo forward Paulo Dybala. Meanwhile, Tuttosport has an exclusive interview with Juventus striker Alvaro Morata, who has stated

A Florida man, identified as Kenneth Crowder, claimed to be God and was high on the designer drug Flakka, stronger than crystal meth. On Friday, he was seen running naked through a neighborhood and committing an undisclosed act on a tree. When police arrived, they used a Taser twice on him, but he violently resisted. He was eventually arrested and charged with battery on a law-enforcement officer, resisting with violence, and assault with a deadly weapon on a law-enforcement officer. Flakka, a dangerous drug usually made from alpha-PVP, causes euphoria, hallucinations, and sometimes psychosis or apparent superhuman strength. Its use has significantly increased in Florida, with more than 670 occurrences in 2014.

A Russian Premier League match between Arsenal Tula and Torpedo Moscow was suspended for seven minutes due to rival fans breaking barriers, causing chaos, and throwing chairs. The incident led to fights on the running track and prompted Torpedo to face heavy punishment for the hooliganism, which is not their first offense this season. Torpedo fans have been previously sanctioned for racist behavior, most recently abusing Zenit St Petersburg's Brazilian forward Hulk. They currently sit in 12th place in the league table with 19 points, one place ahead of Arsenal Tula, who sit just above the bottom with 14 points.

A Chinese high school in Huizhou is conducting military-style dagger drills for female students, utilizing fake knives with retractable blades, under the guidance of a former special forces soldier named Inspector Tan. The training is a form of self-defense education aimed at equipping these teenage girls to handle dangerous situations, with the intention of using any sharp object, such as chopsticks, should the need arise. The training session, which lasts five days, is reportedly well-received by the school's students who are learning the latest self-defense techniques.

AP McCoy, the champion jockey who has held the title since 1997, has announced plans to retire immediately if his mount, Shutthefrontdoor, wins the £1 million Crabbie’s Grand National on Saturday. With an avalanche of emotional support behind him, McCoy aims to end his record-breaking career with a victory in the famous race, but understands that nothing is guaranteed in jump racing. Despite the challenges, McCoy remains optimistic and is eager to see his script have a glorious finale.

John Isner, a 6-foot-10 American tennis player, reached the semifinals of the Miami Open by defeating Kei Nishikori 6-4, 6-3, marking the first time an American man has advanced this far in Miami since 2011. In the semifinals, Isner will face either Novak Djokovic or David Ferrer. Nishikori struggled against Isner's powerful play, failing to gain a break chance and not facing any break points in the tournament. In the other semi final, Andy Murray will face Tomas Berdych, his former teammate and friend. Their meeting is expected to be contentious due to past disagreements, with sparks flying between the two at the Australian Open this year.

In the first leg of the Champions League quarter-final, Bayern Munich suffered a 3-1 defeat against Porto, with Franz Beckenbauer criticizing defender Dante's performance, comparing it to someone wearing "ski boots." Bayern's head coach, Pep Guardiola, was also dissatisfied with their performance. Beckenbauer, speaking in New York as part of Bayern's media agreement with MSN, stated that if the team performed similarly in the next match, they would have no chance of advancing. He also acknowledged that Dante was Brazilian and expressed that his comments were not meant in a negative way, but rather a reaction to the team's poor performance. Beckenbauer admitted that with the current performance, Bayern is not close to winning the Champions League.

A 21-year-old man named Arnold Quintero from San Antonio, Texas has been arrested for allegedly imprisoning, brutally assaulting, sexually assaulting, and burning a 13-year-old girl. The incidents are said to have taken place between January 21 and February 8 in what was referred to as a 'trap house.' Quintero faces several charges, including aggravated sexual assault of a child and possession with intent to deliver drugs. The girl identified Quintero a month after being interviewed by the Bexar County Sheriff’s Office Criminal Investigations Division.

In Week 12 of the Betway Premier League, Michael van Gerwen (World No 1) had a mixed night, winning 7-0 against James Wade and booking a spot in the play-offs, but losing 7-5 to Gary Anderson in the finale. Gary Anderson, too, had a topsy-turvy night, losing 7-1 to Stephen Bunting in the opener but clinching a thrilling 7-5 win over Van Gerwen in the finale, averaging 105.94. Other notable matches included Raymond van Barneveld coming from behind to defeat Dave Chisnall and Phil Taylor drawing 6-6 with Adrian Lewis.

Jay Rutland, a 34-year-old training consultant and husband of billionaire heiress Tamara Ecclestone, earned £65 a week from his firm, Brigante Business Developments, last year, according to recently filed accounts. The company saw a decline in net assets from £18,131 in the previous year to £3,378 over the 12 months to July 2014. Despite the low earnings, Rutland lives with his wife and daughter in a £45 million house in London, and the couple has a lavish lifestyle, owning luxury vehicles and hosting expensive events such as Sophia's first birthday party, which estimatedly cost £70,000. Rutland's career in the City of London ended in disgrace in 2012 due to being banned from trading over 'market abuse'.

A leukaemia patient named Jia Binhui, formerly from Yunlong County in Yunnan Province, China, has resorted to an unconventional treatment, lying over hot coals in his garden, due to financial constraints that prevent him from affording hospital treatments. He claims this action was advised by experts, as temperatures over 42 degrees Celsius might destroy cancerous cells in his body. Jia built a rudimentary contraption for this purpose and hopes it will cure his disease. Despite his dire circumstances, Jia recently married and expresses determination to persevere.

Queens Park Rangers are hoping to boost their relegation fight by bringing back Dutch midfielder Leroy Fer from a knee injury, which he sustained in February. Since joining from Norwich in the summer, Fer has struggled with both form and fitness. Manager Chris Ramsey acknowledges reintroducing Fer carries some risk, but he could potentially feature on the bench for this weekend's home London derby against West Ham, with defender Richard Dunne and Korean left-back Yun Suk-Young also set to return from recent injuries. However, Rio Ferdinand remains unavailable.

Team Sky cyclists Sir Bradley Wiggins and Geraint Thomas narrowly avoided being involved in a major crash in the final kilometre of Scheldeprijs race on Wednesday. Their team-mate, Elia Viviani, was unfortunate and got caught up in the crash, resulting in him being sent to hospital for x-rays after hitting the barriers while vying for position ahead of the expected sprint finish. The crash involved around 50 riders, with Katusha's Alexander Kristoff taking the win, leaving only 14 riders to contest the sprint finish. Despite Viviani's injury, Team Sky remains optimistic about their performance in the upcoming Paris-Roubaix race on Sunday.

Aston Villa players received messages of encouragement from fans, displayed in their dressing room before the FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool. Jack Grealish, a 19-year-old player, thanked supporters on Twitter, encouraging the team to find the 'end of the rainbow' and prove they're the pride of the Midlands. Coach Tim Sherwood included Grealish in the starting line-up after his impressive performances, and other players like Brad Guzan also shared supportive messages prior to the match.

A 12-year-old named Hanghang in China was severely injured when his old phone exploded while charging, exposing part of his jawbone and embedding fragments in his arms and legs. He had used the phone as an alarm and played with it before it became hot and blew up. Experts speculate that improper charging might be the most common cause of such explosions, and advise against using the phone during charging, not overcharging, and replacing swollen batteries. Hanghang is currently hospitalized and is expected to undergo several operations for his injuries.

Mike Rowe, in an episode of "Somebody's Gotta Do It," met Chad Pregracke, the founder of Living Lands & Waters, a nonprofit dedicated to cleaning up U.S. rivers. Pregracke, who founded the organization at 23, has collected over 8.4 million pounds of trash with the help of thousands of volunteers, earning him the 2013 CNN Hero of the Year Award. Pregracke also showed Rowe his living and working barge, a recycled strip club, aimed at removing an additional 500,000 pounds of trash in 2015. To aid in this mission, visit LivingLandsAndWaters.org/Get-Involved/.

The drone-captured footage showcases the spooky, abandoned ghost town of Balestrino, a Tuscan settlement dating back to the 11th century, with a castle on the hill and depreciated buildings. The town, located 40 miles southeast of Genoa, was mostly abandoned due to seismic instability, with a major earthquake in 1887 causing severe damage. Today, Balestrino is considered the most famous abandoned location in Italy, with legends of hauntings adding to its mystique. The video concludes with a shot of the town from a distance, highlighting the town's eerie, empty windows and the grandeur of the castle on the hill.

The article discusses an event in Anaheim, California where director J.J. Abrams and the cast of "Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens" screened a trailer for the film, causing audience members to gasp, cheer, and applaud. Mark Hamill addressed the audience, calling them "family." The trailer reveals details such as Han Solo's return, a new planet called Jakku as a primary location, and hints of the involvement of Luke and Leia. Abrams also mentioned that less CGI was used in the film compared to the prequels, and the new droid BB-8 is not CGI. Additionally, the article mentions the unveiling of a Star Wars themed 787 Dreamliner, Star Wars emojis, new Stormtroopers, and the debut of a new droid BB-8 on stage.

Rob Ford, the former Toronto Mayor, has announced he will undergo a significant surgery to remove a cancerous tumor from his abdomen on May 11. The surgery, which will be performed by four surgeons, is expected to last eight to ten hours. Ford hopes to return to work as a city councilor in September, following a recovery period of 10 to 14 days. He was diagnosed with malignant liposarcoma, a rare soft tissue cancer, last year and underwent five rounds of chemotherapy and nearly a month of radiation.

The University of Cape Town has removed a statue of British colonialist Cecil Rhodes, a decision driven by student protests which claimed his legacy was steeped in racism. The statue, unveiled in 1934, was the center of a campaign, #RhodesMustFall, that initially received attention after activists threw excrement on the statue. The university has stated that the heritage authority granted it permission to remove the statue. Meanwhile, in Pretoria, a group of protesters disagreed, arguing the statue's removal is an attempt to erase history rather than confront it. Post-removal, students celebrated and marked the event with a march, signaling the ongoing nature of their campaign for change.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic gold-medalist, successfully returned to competitive swimming after a six-month ban due to a drink-driving conviction, winning the 100 meters butterfly race at the Arena Pro Swim Series in Arizona. With a time of 52.38 seconds, Phelps edged out Ryan Lochte. Despite missing this summer's World Championships in Kazan, Russia, following talks with USA Swimming, Phelps aims to compete in his fifth Olympics in 2016 at Rio de Janeiro.

A woman in Crown Heights, New York hung herself from a third-floor fire escape early Sunday morning. Her body was discovered at around 8:20 am and remained there for over an hour. Several witnesses were traumatized, with one initially believing it was a Halloween prank. The woman had known mental health issues. Her identity has not been released, pending notification of her family.

1. Lyon and Saint-Etienne played a stirring 2-2 draw in the Rhone derby, with Clinton N'Jie, Lindsay Rose's red card, Max Gradel's penalty, and Romain Hamouma scoring for the respective sides. The draw places Lyon at the top of the Ligue 1 table, level with Paris St Germain who have a game in hand.

2. Lille maintained their pursuit of the top four spots by defeating Bordeaux 2-0, with goals from Nolan Roux and Adama Traore. This win saw Lille moving just four points behind Bordeaux, marking their third consecutive victory.

3. Montpellier secured a crucial 1-0 win against Caen thanks to Hilton's early header, allowing them to elevate their position to seventh in the Ligue 1 standings. The defeat leaves Caen struggling in 13th with only four points from their last six league matches.

Arsene Wenger was surprised by the significant contributions of Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin in Arsenal's late push for the Premier League title, as he initially did not foresee them as key players. Bellerin, who scored Arsenal's opening goal against Liverpool, has been impressive with his defensive skills and offensive potential at just 20 years old. Despite beingbooked earlier in the match, Bellerin was fortunate not to receive a second yellow card for a slide tackle on Sterling that resulted in a penalty. Coquelin was previously sent on loan to Charlton before Christmas and Wenger had almost given up on him.

"The Hollywood Reporter" reports that Fox is developing a two-hour remake of the cult classic "The Rocky Horror Picture Show," with Kenneth Ortega (of "High School Musical" fame) set to direct, produce, and choreograph the project. Slated to celebrate the film's 40th anniversary, the special is tentatively titled "The Rocky Horror Picture Show Event." Previous attempts to adapt the film for television were made in 2002 and during Fox's "Glee," where several popular songs were covered. The special's production is contingent on casting, with no confirmed air date as yet. Other notable live musical productions include NBC's planned live version of "The Wiz."
