AS Roma has been ordered to close part of their stadium for an upcoming home game due to offensive banners displayed during their match against Napoli, which insulted the mother of a Napoli fan who was killed in violent clashes between supporters last year. The banners stirred outrage and were deemed provocative by a Serie A disciplinary tribunal. Roma's game against Atalanta on April 19 will see part of the Stadio Olimpico Stadium closed. The banners aimed at Antonella Leardi, the mother of the deceased Ciro Esposito, were met with condemnation by Roma's club president James Pallotta, who expressed the club's deep regret over such incidents. Leardi, expressing her personal pain, called for a change in the fans who displayed the offensive banners.

Ellen White, former Arsenal player, experienced a memorable night in the Women's Super League as she scored a stunning free-kick against her old club, Notts County. The goal came after a moment of confusion between Arsenal's Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood. However, White missed a penalty that could have sealed a 2-0 victory, and Arsenal eventually equalized late in the game with a debut goal from Chioma Ubogagu, salvaging a point.

Arsene Wenger acknowledges discussions with Eden Hazard's agent regarding a potential move to Arsenal in 2012, but ultimately, financial constraints prevented the deal from materializing. Chelsea signed Hazard for £32million, a price Arsenal could not match. Now, with a standout season under his belt, Hazard is a strong contender for the Player of the Year award, but Wenger believes his own player, Alexis Sanchez, also has a chance at the title due to Sanchez's comparatively younger experience level in the Premier League.

Stephen Akers-Belcher was dismissed from his care manager role with Newcastle City Council for gross misconduct, after he was found to have taken time off work under false pretenses for a funeral, but was instead photographed attending an event on historical warship HMS Warrior which is 323 miles away from his job. Akers-Belcher claims he was sacked for whistleblowing, but the council denies this, stating the allegations were examined following an investigation but no action was taken. Akers-Belcher has declined to comment on the matter beyond stating he has done nothing wrong.

A highly respected Australian doctor named John Parker, who had been working at an Ebola treatment center in Sierra Leone since November, was placed in isolation at Westmead Hospital in Sydney after experiencing flu-like symptoms. Tests taken at the hospital came back negative for Ebola, as confirmed by NSW Health. The aid organization Aspen Medical, which employs Dr. Parker, stated that he followed protocol and notified them as a precaution. Over 10,000 people have reportedly died from the Ebola virus, according to the World Health Organization, primarily in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

A nine-year-old footballer named Frankie Franz has replicated a trick shot performed by Barcelona's Martin Montoya, scoring a 27-yard goal directly into a basketball hoop positioned in his garden's goal-post setup. The boy expressed confidence in his ability to perform the shot after watching a viral video of Montoya pulling it off at Barcelona's Ciutat Esportiva training ground. The shot was performed similarly to Montoya's, with the ball bouncing off the backboard and going through the hoop. Frankie demonstrated shock and excitement upon scoring the goal, much like Montoya did in the original video. Despite not being captured on camera, Frankie is said to have attempted the shot again and successfully scored twice in quick succession. Frankie is an academy player for Dagenham and Redbridge Football Club and harbors aspirations of playing for Real Madrid or Barcelona in the future.

The Wisden–MCC Cricket Photograph of the Year 2014 showcases a wide array of cricket images, ranging from professional matches to children playing on a Bangladesh rubbish tip. The winning photograph by Matthew Lewis captures Dwayne Bravo taking a spectacular catch for the West Indies during last year's ICC World Twenty20 competition. Other notable images include an intrepid game of cricket on Mount Kilimanjaro, England bowler Broad getting hit in the face by a ball, and Bangladesh A's Nurul Hasan facing South African fast bowler Steyn. The competition also includes photographs highlighting the ordinary passion for cricket, such as a Bangladeshi game amidst parents foraging on a rubbish tip.

A New Jersey judge has ruled that a mother did not abuse her parental discretion by taking her 11-year-old daughter to a Pink concert in 2013, despite the father's protests. The father, who is the girl's ex-husband, claimed the performances were too sexually suggestive. However, the judge found that Pink's music, while sometimes suggestive, is not necessarily inappropriate for preteens. The judge also noted that the mother's decision was reasonable, as she took the girl's wishes into account and deemed the show age-appropriate after watching clips on YouTube.

The coastal town of Salcombe in Devon has recently been identified as the most expensive place to buy property in the UK, with an average property price of £671,759, surpassing London's average of £638,217. Notably, Salcombe's waterfront properties average over £2 million, followed by London's pricier neighborhoods like Notting Hill, Regent's Park, and Hampstead Heath. Salcombe's property market has seen a steep 10% increase in the last 12 months, coinciding with a decrease in prices for nearby seaside towns like Padstay. Salcombe's popularity as a yachting and sailing destination, along with its renowned fresh seafood and beaches, has contributed to its appeal and property demand. For those seeking to experience the millionaire lifestyle without the corresponding costs, the Salcombe Harbour Hotel & Spa offers waterfront rooms beginning at £425 this summer season.

1. Celtic have expressed disappointment with the ticket pricing for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness at Hampden, with prices set at £23 for some stands and £15 for adults in the East Stand.
2. The Scottish Football Association (SFA) has defended the pricing structure, stating that the prices have remained unchanged for four years and revenue from the semi-finals is shared equally among participating teams.
3. Despite the ticket pricing controversy, Celtic manager Ronny Deila is focusing on their Scottish Premier League (SPL) clash with St Mirren on Friday.

A 16-year-old student, Rebecca Rice, was allowed to bring her pet Labrador, Holly, into her GCSE French oral exam at Bodmin College in Cornwall due to her severe nerves. After trying various methods to calm down, only her dog was effective. Ms. Lorette Esteve, Rebecca's French teacher, facilitated this arrangement, stating it's part of the school's efforts to reduce students' stress during exams, including allowing drinks, a lucky charm, or a friend in the room. Rebecca found comfort in Holly's presence, stating it significantly helped manage her nervousness.

Anders Lindegaard, a Manchester United goalkeeper, is currently enjoying marital bliss with his Swedish model wife Misse Beqiri, whom he married last year in a beach wedding in Mauritius. Despite his struggles for playing time at United, having made only 19 league appearances in five seasons and being third-choice at the club since the arrival of David de Gea and Victor Valdes, Lindegaard has a successful life off the pitch, often sharing snippets of his personal life on Instagram. Misse Beqiri, who has Albanian roots, is a popular model with over 17,000 followers on Instagram and is not shy about showcasing her modelling work on the platform. The couple have been together since 2012.

Manchester United goalkeepers David de Gea and Victor Valdes took a break from football to visit a theme park, wearing sunglasses and relaxing after their impressive win against Manchester City. This victory is a part of Manchester United's recent resurgence in the Premier League, where they are now competing for second place after earlier struggle to secure a top-four spot. Their future with the team, however, remains uncertain, particularly for Valdes whose chances at Old Trafford have been limited since his free transfer.

A piano teacher, John Goodwin, awaiting trial for six counts of aggravated sexual assault against an underage student, shot himself outside a New Hampshire courthouse while jurors were deliberating. The former student testified he did not come forward until 2013 due to embarrassment. Goodwin was airlifted to a hospital with life-threatening injuries from the self-inflicted gunshot wound, and his health status remains undisclosed. The New Hampshire Attorney General's Office is expected to release more information about the incident later.

Amazon removed a controversial mobile game, titled "Rescue the Anorexia Girl," after it received numerous complaints for encouraging players to feed a cartoon character battling anorexia by throwing food at her. The game's design, which portrays anorexia as a villain that needs to be defeated, was criticized for reinforcing harmful stereotypes and stigmatizing those suffering from mental illnesses. The game's marketing description, which has also been withdrawn, encouraged players to act as "heroes" by saving the character, who would lose weight and eventually die if not fed.

Scientists are working on a project called the Green Brain Project, aimed at digitally recreating the cognitive abilities of honeybees to power drones. So far, researchers have managed to clone the part of the bee's brain responsible for sight, enabling a drone to fly similar to a bee. The project team, consisting of researchers from the Universities of Sheffield and Sussex, has developed several quadcopters and a ground robot each with unique abilities. Tests are currently being conducted at the University of Sheffield to enhance the drones' navigation and cognitive functions. This eventually aims to lead to the application of these drones in tasks such as pollinating crops and search-and-rescue missions.

A newly-wed Air Malta crew, comprising a pilot and a cabin crew member, arranged a romantic flight over the Mediterranean to celebrate their wedding. The Airbus A319 flew heart-shaped patterns and a sightseeing tour, with the wedding status displayed on the airport's arrivals board. Some aircraft enthusiasts speculated about it being a training flight or a publicity stunt, but the airline confirmed it was a personal initiative by the newlywed couple, attended by their family, friends, and colleagues.

A five-year-old giraffe named Melvin was gored to death by an eland antelope at Kristiansand zoo in Norway. Witnesses, including 30 children, saw the unprovoked attack, which occurred when Melvin got his head stuck in the fence. Veterinary efforts to save Melvin were unsuccessful. The incident has been described as traumatic by witnesses, and the zoo's chief executive expressed sadness over the event. The cause of the attack is unknown.

A restaurant in Belgium, Rubens eaterie, has been criticized for charging a mother 36p to heat up her baby's feeding bottle. The incident was shared on Twitter and caused public outrage. The manager was labeled the 'stingiest boss in Europe.' However, a spokesperson for the restaurant chain later stated that the service is charged only when explicitly told to the customer, but in most establishments under the chain, it is usually free.

North Korea is demanding the release of one of its cargo ships, the Mu Du Bong, which ran aground off the coast of Mexico in July and was subsequently detained due to the ship's owner, North Korea's Ocean Maritime Management company, circumventing United Nations sanctions. Mexico defends its actions as an international obligation and adherence to proper protocol. The 33 North Korean crew members, currently in a hotel in Tuxpan, are reportedly free and will soon be returned to North Korea with assistance from the country's embassy. Notably, this is a separate incident from the 2013 detention of the Chong Chon Gang by Panama, where the ship was found to be carrying undeclared weaponry from Cuba.

David Cameron is planning to offer an additional 600,000 childcare spaces for families a year to combat escalating childcare costs, with the aim of making work more financially beneficial. This will be funded by reducing tax relief on pension contributions for individuals earning over £150,000. The expansion of free childcare, offering up to 30 hours a week, is intended to stimulate employment, particularly among second earners, and help households save up to £5,000 per year. The initiative promotes the Conservative Party's goal of fostering a country where hard work is rewarded and poverty is reduced.

Manchester City's young team extended their 3-0 first-leg lead over Leicester City with two late goals from Isaac Buckley and Brandon Barker in the Youth Cup semi-final match. Leicester had momentarily reduced the deficit through a penalty by Layton Ndukwu, but City responded with quick-fire goals to eliminate any hope of a comeback. In the final, they will face Chelsea, with the first leg set to be held at the City Football Academy Stadium on April 20, followed by the second leg at Stamford Bridge on April 27.

Russian President Vladimir Putin dismissed Western sanctions against his country as an attempt to stymie Russian development, not just a response to the annexation of Crimea or the conflict in Ukraine's east. He also defended the sale of a sophisticated air defense system to Iran, calling it a defensive measure and dismissing concerns about Iran posing a threat to Israel. The Q&A session, where Putin often speaks for extended periods, is an annual spectacle in Russia, often criticized as a performance rather than an opportunity for the public to question their leader. Last year, NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden made a surprise appearance during the session.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood will evaluate Gary Gardner, who has displayed impressive form during a loan spell at Nottingham Forest, when Gardner returns for pre-season training. A former England Under-21 player, Gardner, who was born in Solihull and played for Villa's academy, expressed a desire to make an impact at his hometown club. He also mentioned that Forest would be his preferred destination if a loan move becomes necessary following his return to Villa. Gardner showcased his ability during a match against Watford, scoring a fine free-kick with Sherwood in attendance.

A stampede occurred at a nightclub in Santiago, Chile, during a performance by British punk band Doom, leading to the deaths of three people and the injuring of a dozen more, including seven who are in critical condition. The crush outside the Tsunami nightclub caused a structure inside to fall, as described by police general Hugo Insulza. The identities of the deceased have not been formally released, though they are believed to be in their 20s and 30s. Several arrests have been made in connection with the tragedy, and the band is known for playing Crust Punk songs such as Anti-Social and Raining Napalm.

Bayern Munich advanced to the German Cup semi-finals after a 5-3 penalty shoot-out win over Bayer Leverkusen, but manager Pep Guardiola expressed concern about the team's recent lack of scoring touch, particularly without Franck Ribery (ankle injury) and Arjen Robben (stomach muscle tear). Guardiola believes the team struggles in one-on-one situations without Ribery and Robben. The team will look to address these issues when they host Eintracht Frankfurt in the Bundesliga on Saturday. Robert Lewandowski scored the only goal in Bayern's last three matches, a 1-0 win against Borussia Dortmund, and the two teams will face each other again in the German Cup semi-final.

Derry Mathews' world title challenge is in uncertainty as Richar Abril withdrew for the second time, causing the potential second defense of Abril's WBA lightweight belt to be in question. The WBA may strip Abril of his title, allowing Mathews to fight for it in his home city of Liverpool. Mathews recently secured a fifth-round knockout victory against Gyorgy Mezei Jnr prior to this title bout.

The article describes a video featuring Hazel, an English Bulldog, who uses her playful energy to fall into a washing basket. In the video, Hazel jumps into the basket, causes it to fall over, and tries to chew on its side. After the unexpected fall, Hazel recoveries and continues her playful antics before sitting calmly next to the basket. The article highlights that these kinds of videos of Hazel exploring the world are frequently uploaded to her owner's YouTube and Instagram pages, where viewers can see Hazel playing on a skateboard, looking at her reflection in a mirror, and trying on a collar.

Catholic bishops in America have criticized the acclaimed BBC series "Wolf Hall" for portraying historical figures, particularly Thomas Cromwell and Thomas More, in a negative light, labeling it as a "prejudice-laden presentation of the past." The drama is said to distort historical facts and present a biased view, with the Catholic News Service characterizing Cromwell as a "monster" and More as an "evidence-flouting caricature." The series, which is based on the Hilary Mantel books and stars Damian Lewis as King Henry VIII, was generally anticipated by U.S. media, but the Catholic Church's critique raises concerns about the historical accuracy and potential ideological bias in the show.

Staff Sergeant Shawn Manning, a victim of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting that was ultimately classified as a terrorism act, claims he is being denied financial support despite being set to receive a Purple Heart medal today. The Army initially denied his claim that his injuries were sustained in the line of duty, citing a 2015 National Defense Authorization Act provision that does not offer combat benefits for service members permanently disabled in attacks inspired or motivated by foreign terrorist organizations. Manning, who suffers from PTSD, says this decision means his family will miss out on $800 a month in benefits. The Army contests that this decision is not final and that recipients of the Purple Heart will receive benefits to which they are legally entitled. It was revealed that army psychiatrist Major Nidal Hasan, the shooter, had exchanged emails with al-Qaeda spokesman Anwar al-Awlaki before the attack.

John Carver, the head coach of Newcastle United, faces the challenge of leading a struggling team, with fans planning to boycott a match against Spurs due to their dissatisfaction with owner Mike Ashley's management of the club. The supporters are protesting the perceived lack of investment and ambition, despite the club's record profits and significant cash reserves. Carver has urged fans to attend the match, expressing understanding for their concerns, but emphasizing the need for support for the team. Despite the ongoing challenges, Carver considers the job at Newcastle to be the toughest in football.

The 2015 Masters tournament saw a new American golf star rise as Jordan Spieth, aged 21, claimed victory, becoming the first competitor to reach 19 under par in the Masters. Spieth entered the final day with a four-shot lead and comfortably held onto this advantage to secure the title. Born in Dallas, Texas, Spieth gained attention as a teenager, becoming a double US Junior Amateur champion and the sixth youngest player to make the cut at a PGA event. After leaving college early, Spieth quickly rose through the professional ranks, winning the PGA Tour Rookie of the Year award and the John Deere Classic before his 20th birthday. Following his 2014 second-place finish at the Masters, Spieth has now achieved victory at the prestigious tournament.

Beatrice Tollman, a luxury hotel chain founder, donated £20,000 to the Conservative Party for their General Election campaign, but she had previously been charged with tax evasion, although the charges were later dismissed. Her husband, Stanley Tollman, pleaded guilty to tax evasion and had to repay over $100 million. The Tollmans' son also pleaded guilty to tax evasion and was sentenced to prison. These developments may be embarrassing for Conservative leader David Cameron, who has been critical of tax avoidance in the past. A Conservative spokesperson has stated that donations from the Tollmans were declared and in compliance with electoral law.

A 23-year-old marketing coordinator named Poppy Smart complained to police and a construction company after allegedly experiencing a month-long daily ritual of sexual harassment in the form of wolf-whistling and sexist comments from builders on a construction site in Worcester, England. The whistling and comments made her job commute an unpleasant experience, and she compared this treatment to racial discrimination. Although wolf-whistling is not a specific crime, repeat instances could be considered a breach of the peace. In 2012, then-Prime Minister David Cameron declined to make wolf-whistling illegal despite signing the UK up to a Council of Europe convention against violence against women.

Teenager Lily Sharp in the UK pranked her mother by simulating a kidnapping, referenceing the movie "Taken." Using text messages, she convinced her mother that a stranger had entered their home, taken her phone, and demanded a ransom of £4000. The mother was completely fooled and became increasingly frantic. After sending a picture of herself as proof, Lily revealed the prank, but her mother did not find it amusing. Despite this, the text exchange received significant attention on Twitter.

Bangladesh defeated Pakistan by 79 runs in the first one-day international in Dhaka, with Tamim Iqbal and Mushfiqur Rahim scoring centuries for the hosts. In reply, Pakistan could only manage 250, with Iqbal and Rahim taking four wickets each, leaving room for a possibility of leveling the series on Sunday. The second ODI is scheduled in Mirpur. In the match, Tamim Iqbal top-scored for Bangladesh with 132, while Azhar Ali led Pakistan with 72 before being dismissed.

Todd Kincannon, a 33-year-old attorney and former South Carolina Republican Party executive director, was arrested and charged with criminal domestic violence following an incident with his wife, Ashley Griffith, in March. Griffith reported that Kincannon grabbed her arm, prevented her from exiting the car, and threatened to harm her, himself, and her family. Kincannon claims he accidentally overdosed on prescription medication during the incident, but Griffith has evidence of past verbal abuse and threats from Kincannon. In addition to his professional background in politics, Kincannon has garnered attention for controversial and inflammatory tweets.

Jordan Spieth, fresh from his Masters victory, is participating in the RBC Heritage Classic this week after a whirlwind media tour in New York. Despite the lack of normal pre-tournament preparations, Spieth is confident and determined to overtake Rory McIlroy for the world No. 1 spot. He has had success at the RBC Heritage in the past, finishing ninth and 12th in his two previous appearances. This tournament holds special significance for Spieth, as it helped boost his confidence and standing on the PGA Tour when he finished in the top 10 two years ago.

Samantha Cameron, the wife of former British Prime Minister David Cameron, demonstrated her appreciation for the alternative group Poliça, known for their psychedelic rock and often violent, sexual imagery. The band's inspiration comes from Shulamith Firestone, a radical feminist who criticized traditional family structures. Poliça's latest album, Shulamith, pays tribute to Firestone, who is best known for her 1970 manifesto advocating for feminist revolution.

The Australian government plans to implement goods and services tax (GST) on movie and music downloads, potentially affecting streaming services like Netflix and Apple, as well as online purchases under $1,000 from overseas companies such as Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and eBay. This move is aimed at increasing GST revenue. However, consumer advocacy group Choice suggests tackling domestic costs and access issues for television shows, music, and movies instead. The new tax could lead to minor price increases for Netflix, iTunes, Google Play, Amazon, and Adobe Creative Cloud services. Tech-savvy consumers might circumvent the tax by using virtual private networks to change their location and appear outside the country.

Stephen A. Smith, a host on ESPN's First Take, is facing criticism for his stance on boxer Floyd Mayweather Jr. Smith suggested that Mayweather's domestic violence history should be considered separately from his boxing career. During a discussion about a forthcoming fight between Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao, Smith stated that Cari Champion, a fellow anchor, should feel a certain way about Mayweather's behavior towards women due to her gender. This controversial statement came nine months after Smith received a one-week suspension for blaming women for provoking domestic violence in a previous discussion. Champion responded by expressing concern about both Mayweather's domestic violence history and his overall treatment of women. Smith defended his position by stating that it was influenced by his love of boxing and not the broader context of Mayweather's actions. This is a recurring theme, as Smith previously faced criticism for victim-blaming in a July 2014 episode of First Take in the wake of the Ray Rice scandal.

A 12-year-old boy named Mahendra Ahirwar from Madhya Pradesh, India, suffers from a rare condition that causes his head to hang at a 180-degree angle and limits his ability to stand, walk, eat, or use the toilet independently. His parents, who work as laborers, have consulted over 50 doctors but have yet to find a diagnosis or treatment. Despite this, his mother Sumitra Ahirwar has expressed her desire for her son's suffering to end due to the devastating impact it has on their family's lives. The community, however, believes that Mahendra's condition is a punishment for the father's past sins. Despite their struggles, the family remains hopeful for a miracle and a cure for their son.

1. The World Happiness Report 2015 reveals that Switzerland is the world's happiest nation, with strong factors contributing to its citizens' contentment including healthy GDP figures, strong social bonds, and increasing life expectancy.
2. Iceland, thanks to factors such as its beautiful scenery and cultural history, made a significant jump in happiness rankings from number 9 in 2013 to number 2 in 2015.
3. The World Happiness Report uses a range of factors to determine a nation's happiness, including GDP, life expectancy, and the well-being of its citizens, and it finds that European nations, particularly Scandinavian ones, and those with less war and extreme poverty generally have higher happiness levels.

The upcoming Burnley vs Arsenal Premier League match at Turf Moor will be covered by Sportsmail, with previews including team news, provisional squads, betting odds, and Opta stats. Matt Taylor is expected to return from a long-term injury for Burnley, but both Dean Marney and Kevin Long remain out. Arsenal's Laurent Koscielny and Wojciech Szczesny could pass fitness tests, while Jack Wilshere, Mikel Arteta, Abou Diaby, and Mathieu Debuchy are back in contention following injuries. Key match stats show Arsenal have won their last seven league games, but Burnley have let in 10 goals in their last four meetings against the Gunnals. Notable players to watch include Danny Ings and Olivier Giroud.

The article previews the upcoming Premier League match between Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa at White Hart Lane. Tottenham will be without Kyle Walker and Hugo Lloris, with Jan Vertonghen a doubt due to injury and illness. Aston Villa boss Tim Sherwood could be without several players, including Alan Hutton, Ashley Westwood, and Scott Sinclair, but a few absentees could return. Key stats indicate Tottenham have won their last five league meetings with Aston Villa, who have struggled to score against them, while Tottenham have proven resilient at home, turning losing positions into wins. The match kicks off on Saturday at 3 pm, with Tottenham favored at 4/7, while Aston Villa are at 5/1, and the referee is Lee Probert.

The article previews the upcoming Liverpool vs Newcastle Premier League match at Anfield, providing team news, provisional squads, betting odds, and Opta stats. Mamadou Sakho is unavailable due to a hamstring injury for Liverpool, but Emre Can returns from suspension. Daniel Sturridge and Mario Balotelli may play, depending on their fitness. Newcastle's Daryl Janmaat should be fit to play despite an injury scare. Key stats include Newcastle's inability to perform a league double against Liverpool since 1993-94, their poor record at Anfield, and Liverpool's goal-scoring slump compared to last season. Jordan Henderson, Vurnon Anita, and Raheem Sterling have notable statistics related to this match. The kick-off is scheduled for Monday at 8pm on Sky Sports 1, and betting odds favor Liverpool.

Nick Clegg, the leader of the Liberal Democrats, has been criticized for blaming various groups instead of himself for the party's declining poll ratings. In an interview with The Economist, he attributed the loss of former supporters to protest voters who deserted the party after it formed a coalition, public sector workers whose pensions were affected and who faced job cuts, and areas that are traditionally anti-Conservative. Clegg claimed that these factors are more significant explanations for the party's decline than policy decisions, such as the increase in tuition fees. A Conservative source has described Clegg's comments as him blaming everyone but himself, and the Liberal Democrats are facing the prospect of losing dozens of seats in the upcoming election.

Chef Bobby Flay's divorce from actress Stephanie March has become more complicated with allegations of a three-year affair between Flay and his assistant Elyse Tirrell. Flay's business partner, however, has dismissed these claims, stating that any ongoing affair with an employee would be known to him. The divorce proceedings have become contentious, with March contesting the prenuptial agreement that stipulates Flay only has to pay her $5,000 per month in alimony. The situation is further complicated by claims of economic warfare and disputes over shared property.

A bus carrying Fenerbahce players and staff was shot at on a viaduct near Trabzon, resulting in the driver being injured. The incident occurred after Fenerbahce's 5-1 win over Caykur Rizespor in the Super Lig. Caykur Rizespor midfielder Ludovic Obraniak was later taken to a hospital for a suspected heart problem. Both incidents were strongly condemned by officials, with Fenerbahce expressing disappointment as they had been in Trabzon for a sports event.

TV presenter Lisa Oldfield underwent a liposuction procedure to lose weight after her son's unflattering portrait of her prompted her to address her weight concerns. She was motivated to make a change due to her regret of having few pictures with her children and her discomfort with her appearance. The surgery removed 5.5 liters of fat, a costly procedure that Oldfield, who still works on Channel 9, felt was necessary despite her efforts to maintain fitness through walking her dogs. She expects minimal fat to return, particularly in her arms.

A couple, Sarah and Mark Brennan, from south Wales, experienced ten miscarriages over a ten-year period yet never lost hope of becoming parents. Last September, Sarah found out she was pregnant, and after some worries, they discovered a strong heartbeat in their daughter Eryn Elisabeth. Eryn was born seven weeks early, weighing just 3lb 11oz. The couple struggled with Eryn's early water break and her prolonged stay in neonatal care but are now overjoyed and advise others struggling with infertility to never give up hope.

To commemorate the Football League Awards' 10th anniversary, a team featuring standout players from below England's top tier during the past decade has been assembled. Notable inclusions are Gareth Bale, Wes Morgan, Adam Lallana, Rickie Lambert, and Jordan Rhodes. The team is comprised of key positions and is headlined by goalkeeper Kasper Schmeichel, defenders Angel Rangel and Ashley Williams, midfielders Wes Hoolahan and Peter Whittingham, forwards Glenn Murray and Rickie Lambert, and manager Eddie Howe.

Moeen Ali, named as one of Wisden's Five Cricketers of the Year, has recovered from a rib injury faster than anticipated and will join the England squad ahead of the second Test in the Caribbean. He aims to build upon his performances during the World Cup, where he averaged 38 with a strike-rate of 105. Ali is confident about facing Australia's two left-arm Mitchells (Starc and Johnson) in the upcoming Ashes, having worked on countering the short ball since last year. He also discussed the challenge of facing the fast and swinging deliveries of Starc, who he believes might be more dangerous than Johnson due to his swing. Moeen is eager to further establish himself as England's primary spinner and has been working on perfecting his doosra.

Andy Lee, the current WBO middleweight world champion, is confident and ready for his title defense against Peter Quillin in New York on Saturday. Lee, who won the title last year against Matt Korobokov, has made significant improvements since then and is proud to defend his title in Quillin's hometown. Quillin, a former champion, is yet to taste defeat as a professional and poses a tough challenge for Lee. Both fighters have expressed self-assurance and are ready for a technical yet potentially explosive fight.

Usain Bolt is known for his joking and mentorship on the athletic circuit. In a memorable incident during a World Championships warm-up in Moscow, Bolt playfully made fun of Adam Gemili, a young British athlete, when Gemili was preparing for a 200m race despite being primarily known as a 100m runner. The exchange helped Gemili relax before the competition. Gemili appreciates Bolt's guidance, particularly his advice to enjoy the sport and not to put unnecessary pressure on oneself. Despite not being at Bolt's competitive level yet, Gemili looks forward to potentially challenging the sprint champions as he increases his own competitive rigor in the coming years. The British sprinter acknowledges that there is a void left by the retirement of sprinters like Tyson Gay and Justin Gatlin, but sees potential for British and European athletes to step into these vacated roles.

Two men, Wade Robson and James Safechuck, who were formerly defenders of Michael Jackson, are set to have their civil claims for sexual abuse heard in court on Tuesday. Robson, now claiming Jackson abused him as a child, and Safechuck, who alleges Jackson performed a secret wedding ceremony with him, missed a statutory deadline for filing their claims. If their case proceeds, more child molestation allegations against Jackson may be revealed. Robson and Safechuck allege Jackson molested them numerous times, with Safechuck claiming more than 100 instances.

A Virginia man, Mark Ward Faville, was convicted of voluntary manslaughter for suffocating his wife Anne in 2000. After the verdict, he took his own life in the courthouse. The couple's daughters testified that Faville exhibited strange behavior and grew suspicious of Anne, and Anne was preparing to leave him for her high school sweetheart. Investigations are ongoing into the details of Faville's death in the courthouse.

1. Memphis Grizzlies tied for second seed in the NBA's Southwest Division after a 100-92 win over Oklahoma City Thunder, with Jeff Green scoring 22 points and Marc Gasol adding 19.
2. Dallas Spurs extended their league record of consecutive 50-win seasons to 16 straight with a 123-93 win over Denver Nuggets, thanks to Danny Green's 6-for-6 shooting on 3-pointers, with Kawhi Leonard scoring 20 points.
3. In East playoff-shaping games, Brooklyn Nets won their sixth consecutive game against Toronto Raptors with Deron Williams scoring a season-high 31 points and Brook Lopez adding 30 points and 17 rebounds. Chicago Bulls beat Detroit Pistons 88-82 with Pau Gasol scoring 26 points and 10 rebounds, and Milwaukee Bucks beat Boston Celtics 110-101, placing a dent in Boston's playoff hopes.

Camellias, known for their polished evergreen foliage and regally beautiful, varied flowers, are easy to grow if soil is acid, free-draining, and nutritious. They can be easily propagated through root cuttings or bought during their blooming season. These plants are versatile, thriving in various environments including pots, walls, arches, and hedges. They are hardy, extending their flowering season, and resist frost damage. Notable varieties include Adolphe Audusson, Alba Simplex, Donation, and St Ewe. Problems such as premature bud drop, yellowing foliage, or magnesium deficiency can be addressed with proper watering, soil adjustments, and supplements.

The article discusses the majestic greater adjutant stork, which soars over the Boragaon landfill in Guwahati, India, a 94-acre site that attracts the endangered bird as it thrives on fresh waste. The landfill is home to approximately 100 families who eke out a living by searching through the trash for reusable items, such as metal and plastic, which they sell to make a meager $2 per day. Despite the difficult living conditions, photographer Timothy Bouldry found the residents to be content, using words like "love," "hope," and "spirituality" to describe them. Bouldry, who has a background in art from Boston, has dedicated himself to photographing and helping people living in landfills around the world, considering it the most fulfilling aspect of his work.

A rapist is being sought by West Yorkshire Police after brutally attacking an 18-year-old woman at a bus stop in Leeds last month. The man, described as Pakistani or Middle Eastern, in his early twenties, and slim with a receding hairline, was seen on CCTV stalking three other women in Leeds city center before the attack. The attacker hit the victim over the head with a rock, leaving her with serious head injuries and a broken hip, and then raped her. CCTV footage shows the man wearing a distinctive green Puma hooded jumper and jeans, and police believe he may have premeditated the assault. The victim survived the attack but is recovering in the hospital. Police are urging anyone with information to come forward.

A mother of six, named Lizzi Crawford, lost over seven stone after an unexpected comment from a child on a bus mistook her for being pregnant. This embarrassing moment led Crawford to reassess her unhealthy lifestyle, characterized by a diet of burgers, pizzas, kebabs, and frequent drinking. Despite being diagnosed with cervical cancer in October 2012, Crawford persevered and lost the weight by attending fitness and self-defense classes, cooking healthier meals, and following the Hourglass training program. Now addicted to fitness, Crawford credits her success to the supportive community at her gym. Her mother praises Crawford's dedication and states she is now "like the old Lizzi I used to know as a little girl."

Nigerian cities, notably Victoria Island in Lagos, have become hubs for luxury goods due to an influx of high-net-worth individuals, with a significant number of millionaires. This growth has also been observed in cities like Luanda, Dar es Salaam, and Accra. Africa's new wealthy class is driving the demand for luxury products, with regions like Nigeria seeing growth in sales of luxury items such as French Champagne and digital televisions. Luxury brands are entering African markets through distributors to leverage local knowledge, but the future growth of luxury in Africa depends on infrastructure and operating environment improvements. Despite the dominance of international brands, there is also potential for home-grown luxury labels to thrive in Africa.

Hotel owner Jennifer McGirr, 61, from Blackpool, claims to be living in fear after her hotel windows were smashed and she received intimidating phone calls, following her criticism of other local hotels on Channel 4's 'Four in a Bed'. The attack, which was caught on CCTV, involved a man throwing a brick at her hotel. Ms McGirr also received a series of abusive phone calls, including one during police investigation of the incident. The abuse started after she described other hotels in the area as 'grim' on the reality TV show.

Ronnie O'Sullivan, a five-time world champion, took off his shoes during a match at the Crucible on Tuesday, complaining about a painful big toe. Despite the breach of the snooker's strict dress code, he was allowed to continue playing and even borrowed shoes from a member of the audience. He maintained a 7-2 lead over debutant Craig Steadman before his lead was pegged back to 4-2. Ding Junhui had a chance to make a maximum break but missed it due to a concentration lapse while Ali Carter, a two-time Crucible finalist, looked in good form in his first match since being given the all-clear from lung cancer. Mark Allen, a Northern Irish player, won nine consecutive frames from a 3-1 deficit against Ryan Day.

A Sydney teenager, Marian Carole Rees, who went missing 40 years ago, may still be alive according to a coronial inquest. The inquest found that the teen likely ran away with the intention of permanently cutting ties with family and friends and that she may still want to avoid detection and not wish to make contact with her family. The case has been referred back to the Missing Person's Unit for further investigation as the Magistrate believes there were holes in the police investigation at the time. Marian was reportedly fed up with taking care of her younger siblings due to her mother's drinking problem and had spoken about running away on numerous occasions.

A mother employed as an assistant director at a childcare center, Michelle Schwab, has been charged with child endangerment after allegedly dangling her two-year-old son over a 10-foot-deep cheetah enclosure at Cleveland Metroparks Zoo, resulting in the child falling into the pit. Witnesses reported that the cheetahs did not approach the boy, and his parents leaped into the pit to rescue him. The child sustained minor injuries and is in stable condition. KinderCare, Schwab's employer, has confirmed that she has taken a leave of absence from her management role at one of their centers in Columbus, Ohio, while the incident is investigated.

A study conducted by researchers at the University of Reading found that chewing gum can help reduce the likelihood and intensity of earworms, or catchy songs that stuck in one's mind. Participants in the study reported thinking about and 'hearing' the catchy tunes less when chewing gum compared to not chewing or tapping their fingers. The study implies that this technique might also be useful for stopping other unwanted thoughts. However, more research is needed to determine the full effects on obsessive-compulsive disorder and similar conditions.

An Oregon couple, Jesse and Melissa Meek, announced their pregnancy in a creative rap video set to the theme song from '90s television sitcom 'The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air'. The video, featuring the couple rapping as they drive, has garnered over 1.7 million views on YouTube. In the video, Melissa reveals that they had been trying to conceive for two months, surprising everyone, including their family, who were eager for grandchildren. The video includes a sonogram of their unborn child, and the Meeks are planning a second video after learning the gender of the child. The video was created to share the happy news with relatives living far away. The Meeks are descendants of Oregon pioneer Joseph Lafayette Meek. Previously, a couple from Phoenixville, Pennsylvania, also used the 'The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air' theme for a pregnancy announcement video last year.

Josiah Duggar, a star from the reality show 19 Kids and Counting, has announced that he has entered into a courtship with 17-year-old Marjorie Jackson. They met while taking Spanish lessons and will follow strict courting rules set by the Duggar family, including chaperoned dates and no physical contact beyond 'side hugs'. The couple has known each other for a few years, with their relationship officially starting on April 6, the same day Josiah's older sister, Jill, gave birth to her first child. Their courtship is likely to be featured on the family's reality series, and it represents one of the Duggar family's major announcements in the past year, following Jessa and her husband Ben Seewald's engagement and marriage. Other recent events in the Duggar family include Jill and Derrick's pregnancy and the birth of their first child, with speculation that Jill may have undergone a cesarean section.

The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge are about to experience the emotional upheaval of parenthood for a second time. A US-based group of parents have created a viral video, titled 'Extra Storage Space,' providing advice to new parents. Tips include establishing a schedule, creating time for personal activities, cherishing moments, being grateful, letting children be themselves, being prepared for the unexpected, and knowing that love is an unforeseen aspect of parenthood. Viewers are also encouraged to share their own parenting advice using the hashtag #makeroomforlife.

Arsenal, currently Europe's top form team, is preparing for a Premier League game against Burnley with an unusual pre-match routine. Players have revealed their personalized playlists, with Giroud choosing Coldplay, Cazorla opting for Melendi, Monreal preferring David Guetta, and Walcott listening to LL Cool J. The eclectic playlists are part of a campaign by Arsenal's partner Europcar to bring fans closer to the players. Despite Burnley's struggle at the bottom of the table, Arsenal aims to keep their title hopes alive.

Ed Miliband's US advisor, David Axelrod, who masterminded two presidential election victories for Barack Obama, admitted he does not pay taxes in Britain on his reported £300,000 salary, despite frequent visits and calls to provide advice on Labour's cost-of-living and tax fairness policies. His employment contract is in dollars, and he resides and pays taxes in the US. Despite his high-profile role, concerns have been raised about his visibility ahead of the election, with some noting his absence from Labour's manifesto. Axelrod's political career includes triumphs in the US, such as helping oust a three-term Republican senator in Illinois and aiding the re-election of Chicago's first black mayor, but he has had less success in Europe, with Italian political advisement resulting in only 10.5% vote.

In December 2012, Texas Trooper Abraham Martinez followed a motorcyclist, Steven Gaydos, who was driving on a suspended license, engaged in a high-speed chase reaching speeds of 130 mph. During the pursuit Martinez leaped out of his car and karate-kicked Gaydos, knocking him off his motorcycle, and also fired four shots at him, hitting Gaydos once in the thigh. The unconventional moves led to a three-day, unpaid suspension for Martinez, but the incident was only recently revealed through an investigation by the Austin American Statesman. The shooting and kick, while not specifically violating Texas Department of Public Safety rules, is considered an area needing policy updates according to experts.

In North Charleston, South Carolina, a white police officer, Michael Slager, shot and killed an unarmed black man named Walter Scott, who was stopped for a broken taillight. Slager claimed he feared for his life, but a video later emerged showing him shooting Scott in the back multiple times. The community expressed outrage, as the incident was seen as an injustice. Despite the video evidence, Slager was ultimately exonerated initially, but was later arrested on murder charges. The racial makeup of the North Charleston police force, which is mostly white, is not representative of the city's predominantly black population. Some argue that racial profiling could have been a factor in the initial stop, and the incident's handling was different from that of Ferguson due to situational awareness or instructive fallout from previous incidents. The final outcome of Slager's trial remains uncertain.

The article describes a complaint made by Steve Ashton, the son of an 81-year-old woman living in Aneurin Bevan Court sheltered housing, about the quality of meals served to his mother. He was particularly upset about a serving of baked potato and corned beef that he found in his mother's fridge. The meal was reportedly unappetizing, and Mr. Ashton expressed concern about food standards for the elderly in care. He has since met with Newport City Homes to discuss potential changes to improve food quality. The spokesperson for Newport City Homes has acknowledged the concerns and agreed to make improvements.

A 71-year-old man named Richard Curry, a pensioner from Loveclough in Lancashire, underwent a unique procedure to receive a magnetic nose after his own was removed due to a rare cancer (malignant melanoma). He had magnetic implants inserted into his cheekbones and nasal cavity at the Royal Blackburn Hospital to hold his prosthetic nose in place. Mr. Curry has spoken positively about the procedure's success and highlighted its comfort and aesthetic appeal, as well as the preservation of his sense of smell. He now wears the nose during the day and removes it at night. Recent check-ups have shown no signs of the cancer returning. This was a rare case as specialists noted that cancers of the nose are not common, and this was the first time they had used magnets to attach a prosthetic nose.

Jimmy Graham, a new addition to the Seattle Seahawks' offense, is viewed by some as a significant acquisition, but defensive end Michael Bennett has previously criticized Graham, labeling him 'soft' and 'overrated.' Bennett expressed his continued dislike for Graham as a player and a person following their previous encounters, stating that he still feels the same way, but will be a better teammate to him due to Graham now being on his team. Bennett had also quashed rumors about asking for a trade to join former defensive coordinator Dan Quinn at the Atlanta Falcons. He explained that he never requested a trade, disputing a report that originated from Clarence Hill of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram. The two players will interact during the Seahawks' official off-season training program on April 20.

A woman named Lisa Courtney from Hertfordshire, UK, has the world's largest collection of Pokemon memorabilia, with over 25,000 items amassed over a 17-year period. Her obsession with Pokemon started at the age of nine when she saw a picture of Pikachu in a Nintendo magazine. This collection has become so large that her mother had to move to the smallest room in their house to make room for the vast array of toys, clothing, badges, flannels, and posters. Despite the size of her collection, Lisa's family is very supportive of her passion for Pokemon. The Guinness World Record for the largest Pokemon collection was clinched by Lisa in 2009, but she continues to collect. She particularly enjoys traveling to Japan to obtain exclusive merchandise. Pokemon has proven to be a source of comfort to Lisa during difficult periods in her life, including when she was being bullied at school.

Raheem Sterling, after rejecting a £100,000-week deal at Liverpool, has been cautioned by Michael Owen, who had a similar journey starting at Liverpool before moving to Real Madrid. Owen believes Sterling, despite his development at Liverpool, may not be ready for Madrid due to the competition with players like Cristiano Ronaldo. Current interest in Sterling includes Chelsea, Arsenal, and Manchester City, but Liverpool are determined to keep him. Owen emphasizes that although Sterling has benefited from his time at Liverpool, he is not obligated to stay out of loyalty.

A 26-year-old woman named Natalie Swindells consumes almost exclusively Rice Krispies, avoiding other food items for nearly two decades. Despite her limited diet, she believes it fosters better health than overeating. The cereal provides her with a balanced diet that includes protein, calcium, and various vitamins due to fortification. However, consulting dietician Sian Porter notes that while Natalie appears healthy, her diet lacks essential minerals and nutrients compared to dietary recommendations.

George and Amal Clooney are hosting a three-day birthday celebration at their Lake Como mansion for Amal's 37th birthday, which was in February. Notable guests include Matt Damon and Brad Pitt. The event is being heavily guarded to ensure privacy, with strict rules in place to avoid unwanted attention. Amal is known for her designer wardrobe, and one of her recent fashion choices, a Stella McCartney dress, is highlighted in the article. The dress features a see-through mesh design and is no longer available, but similar styles are available at Neiman Marcus and other retailers. Amal works as a human rights lawyer, and she has recently accepted a lecturer position at Columbia University in New York City. George is currently filming a new movie, Money Monster, in New York.

Creflo Dollar, a prosperity gospel pastor, defended his campaign to raise $300 from 200,000 people globally to buy a Gulfstream G650, stating that critics and allegations about his request were attempts by the devil to discredit him. In the face of criticism, Dollar asserted that his followers, not fundraising, paid for his previous aircraft, and that the need for a new, luxurious jet was necessitated by two accidents involving his older plane. The purchase of the jet, which is expected to cost around $65 million, is not limited to member donations, but also involves partners and supporters of his ministry. Critics have expressed concerns about the expenditure, given the theology associated with the prosperity gospel, which promises wealth and health to those who tithe, and its emphasis on material wealth.

In an article for the Independent Association of Prep Schools magazine, Sherborne Preparatory School headmaster Peter Tait urges parents to step back and trust schools and teachers instead of becoming overly involved in their children's education. He argues that modern parenting trends stem from being bombarded with information and that such interference can hinder a child's natural development. He encourages parents to focus on their child's happiness, challenges, purpose, and values. The article also mentions a rising trend of parents using social media to bully and intimidate teachers, with nearly 60% of teachers reporting this form of abuse.

An Irish tourist, Barry Lyttle, has pleaded guilty to recklessly causing grievous bodily harm to his brother, Patrick Lyttle, in Sydney, Australia. The incident occurred in January, leaving Patrick in a coma for six days. Despite the initial charge carrying a possible maximum term of 10 years in a district court, the case will be heard in a local court where the maximum sentence is two years. The hearing is expected to include CCTV footage of the attack and evidence from a criminologist specializing in restorative justice. The Lyttle family has requested the charges against Barry be dropped, and Patrick has made a "fantastic recovery." The matter will return to court on April 16.

The Ventura County prosecutors have refiled charges against Jane Laut, a woman accused of killing her Olympic medalist husband David Laut in 2009, after a judge denied for the third time a request to delay her trial. This move appears to be an attempt to prolong the trial. Jane Laut claims she acted in self-defense, alleging that her abusive husband, who won a bronze medal in the 1984 Olympics, threatened to kill their son and dogs before she took the gun from him. Her attorney criticized the prosecution's decision to refile the charges in a murder case.

A British nuclear submarine, HMS Talent, sustained £500,000 worth of damage in a collision while tracking Russian vessels in the North Sea, potentially in the Arctic Circle, as both countries have increased submarine activity in these areas. The Navy claims the damage was caused by striking 'floating ice', but the incident is under investigation. This incident recalls similar Cold War collisions that were initially attributed to ice but were later revealed to be caused by enemy vessels. HMS Talent, a "hunter-killer" submarine, will be out of action for several months while repairs are made to the acoustic tiles on its conning tower.

The study found that two cups of coffee daily could potentially reduce by half the risk of breast cancer returning in women undergoing treatment with the drug tamoxifen. This effect is due to coffee's ability to inhibit breast cancer cell growth, especially in combination with tamoxifen. Researchers believe substances like caffeine and caffeic acid in coffee might be responsible for this interaction. Moreover, coffee consumption has been linked to improved cancer prognosis in other studies, with potential risk reductions for liver and skin cancers.

Wild rabbits in greater Sydney are being targeted again for population reduction using carrots laced with a viral disease called Calicivirus, also known as Rabbit haemorrhagic disease (RHD), due to their significant growth this year. The virus causes severe damage to the animal's liver and gut, resulting in haemorrhaging and death in mostly all rabbits. Local Land Services implemented a similar program last year and will again distribute the infected carrots in May across 10 areas and the Central Coast, aiming to combat the pest that causes agricultural and environmental damage. Pet rabbits should be vaccinated to protect them from the virus, which does not harm cats, dogs, or humans.

The article discusses the optimism among many Iranians regarding the continuation of nuclear negotiations between Tehran and six world powers, which is seen as a potential indicator of a favorable Persian New Year (Norouz). This preliminary agreement, part of a joint comprehensive plan of action, aims to guarantee the peaceful nature of Tehran's nuclear activities in exchange for the lifting of sanctions. President Hassan Rouhani and his "moderate" administration view this deal as strengthening their position, particularly in upcoming elections, as they seek to improve the living conditions of ordinary Iranians. The agreement is considered a significant step towards rapprochement between Tehran and Washington.

A Sudanese refugee, Mohamed Hamdin, is facing indecent assault charges after allegedly groping a 15-year-old girl at a rap concert in Sydney. The incident occurred during the concert of U.S. rappers YG and Ty Dolla $ign at the Enmore Theatre on Australia Day. Hamdin will reappear in court on April 28. Noteable is the rap artists YG and Ty Dolla $ign's history of violence and alleged gang affiliations, with YG being a controversial figure due to incidents such as shootings, crowd violence, and gang-related incidents at previous concerts.

1. Arsene Wenger is optimistic about Arsenal's title challenge, but emphasizes the importance of maintaining perfection for the rest of the season while waiting for potential slip-ups from Chelsea.

2. Arsenal achieved a strong 4-1 victory over Liverpool at home, with goals from Hector Bellerin, Mesut Ozil, Alexis Sanchez, and Olivier Giroud. Despite this win, they remain seven points behind Chelsea, who will visit The Emirates in two weeks.

3. Wenger believes that if the opportunity arises, Arsenal will be ready to challenge Chelsea. He also believes that the performance against Liverpool demonstrates that had they not been affected by injuries and the late return of players like Ozil and Per Mertesacker, they would be closer to Chelsea in the table.

The article discusses the worrying trend of one in three General Practitioner (GP) training places remaining vacant, causing concerns about patients' access to family doctors. This outcome is attributed to junior doctors shying away from becoming GPs due to fears of overwork, making GP a less attractive specialty. The GP shortage has become more pressing, as revealed by recent statistics showing that 10% of patients failed to book a GP appointment in 2013/14. The empty GP training posts equate to nearly 34 million unsuccessful attempts to book appointments in 2019. Regions like the East Midlands, North East of England, West Midlands, and several coastal areas show vacancy rates above 40%. The shortage is already causing issues in many regions, with some practices being forced to close or reduce service levels. Efforts to recruit 50% of junior doctors as GP trainees by 2016, set by Health Education England, have not been met with success.

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian forward Dane Tilse, a 6ft 7in prop with 200 NRL appearances, on a 2.5-year contract to replace the front row pair Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey, who left due to injury and personal reasons respectively. Tilse is set to join the team once he receives necessary paperwork from his previous team, the Canberra Raiders. Hull KR head coach Chris Chester expressed excitement about Tilse's arrival and believes he will be a valuable addition to the squad. Tilse is looking forward to the new challenge and the fresh start in the Super League.

A 6-year-old girl's teeth were in a dangerous, potentially fatal condition due to her father's negligence, leading to Kenneth Wanamaker Jr's guilty plea for reckless endangerment. He also pleaded guilty to false swearing and faces a two-month to a year prison sentence. The investigation continues into Wanamaker and his partner's connection to the death of other children, including a 7-month-old baby boy in 2011 and two stillborn deliveries since 2007. Despite the ongoing investigation and charges, Wanamaker maintains that he and his partner are raising a healthy, active family.

A 16-year-old transgender boy who has experienced distress due to gender incongruence has been granted court-approval to undergo male puberty hormone treatment after demonstrating a consistent desire to transition. The approval process involves psychiatric evaluations, medical assessments, and legal consideration of the adolescent's ability to make informed decisions about their treatment. The Family Court's involvement in these matters has been a topic of discussion regarding its necessity, as some argue that the decisions can be made by parents and medical professionals alone.

A light aircraft, a Piper PA-32, crashed in the Punta Cana region of the Dominican Republic, killing seven people. The foreign office is investigating reports that two British citizens were among the passengers, although this has not been definitively confirmed. The plane, which was en route to the Samana Peninsula, was owned by private firm Sky High Aviation Services. The accident occurred at around 8.15am in the eastern part of the island, where it is a popular tourist destination, and took place in the grounds of Cocotal Golf and Country Club.

Cynthia Lennon, who was married to John Lennon during his rise to fame with the Beatles, passed away on Wednesday at the age of 75 following a battle with cancer. The couple met at art school, where Cynthia was an illustrator and John was a struggling musician. Their relationship was marked by John's brittle personality and his rising fame, which at times proved challenging for Cynthia. They were married from 1962 to 1968, and their son, Julian, was born in 1963. After the divorce, Cynthia wrote two books about her marriage to John and continued to write and marry three more times. She is survived by her son Julian.

The stepchildren of Kim Howe, who died in a car crash involving Bruce Jenner, are considering suing Jenner for wrongful death, despite having a virtually non-existent relationship with him. The crash occurred on the Pacific Coast Highway in February, with Jenner's vehicle rear-ending Howe's car, which then collided with another vehicle. If a lawsuit is filed, Jenner, who was not injured in the incident, may have to pay from his personal finances due to his insurance coverage being limited to $250,000. Sources close to the investigation suggest Jenner may not be prosecuted for manslaughter, but this does not preclude a wrongful death suit by Howe's stepchildren. Additionally, Howe, who was childless and had no other close living blood relatives, was known to be socially active and philanthropic in her community.

Neil MacGregor, the Director of the British Museum, is stepping down after 13 years in the role, having previously worked at the National Gallery and as a broadcaster. In his time at the museum, he helped complete a new building and build partnerships with other museums, expanding the museum's program of loans and training worldwide. He is known for his Radio 4 series A History of the World in 100 Objects, inspired by the museum's collection. The museum is now poised to embark on a new phase, with the new Islamic galleries and plans for the future of the Old Reading Room. The museum's chairman, Sir Richard Lambert, praised MacGregor's work and expressed gratitude for his contributions. The museum received 6.7 million visitors in 2014/15 and has hosted recent exhibitions on topics such as life in China, Afghanistan, and ancient Rome.

The Augusta National Golf Club has enforced a cell phone ban, leading fans to use old cameras for capturing images of golfers like Tiger Woods. Many fans, some of whom had not used their cameras in years, adapted, with some re-learning how to use their equipment. This new method generated humorous moments, such as attempts to take selfies with point-and-shoot cameras not designed for such use. Some fans planned to commemorate the experience with photo albums or high-quality prints.

Allie Davis, a 21-year-old Beyonce fan, made her boyfriend take a ten-question exam about Beyonce and other pop stars to stay in the relationship. He scored 80%. Allie posted the results and a copy of the exam on Twitter, and one commentator took the stunt seriously, while Allie defended it as a bored and playful jab at her boyfriend. Some people found it excessive and psychotic.

Ocean photographer Lloyd Meudell, based on the south coast of New South Wales, Australia, captures the surreal moment when ocean foam explodes into the air and creeps over the sand. His unique photographs, reminiscent of works by surrealist artists like Salvador Dali, have drawn interest from buyers worldwide, including a surprisingly large number of elderly women. Meudell, who uses an EOS 5D Mark III DSLR and various lenses, advises aspiring photographers to first understand the ocean's dynamics before diving into photography, suggesting a GoPro as a starting point.

Bayern Munich suffered a 3-1 defeat in the first leg of their Champions League quarter-final against Porto, with Ricardo Quaresma and Jackson Martinez scoring two early goals and a second-half effort, respectively. Bayern manager Pep Guardiola attributed the loss to the team's current injury woes, while Porto manager Julen Lopetegui expressed optimism about reaching the semi-finals, emphasizing the need for a 'perfect' performance in the return leg. Jackson Martinez, who returned from injury, was a constant thorn for Bayern's defense and scored Porto's third goal, while Ricardo Quaresma stood out for his hard work and team ethic.

The Curiosity Rover has discovered unique, multi-colored veins on Mars, specifically at a site called 'Garden City' on Mount Sharp. These veins, which contain both bright and dark materials, are believed to be remnants of Mars' watery past, formed in ancient fluid flows above eroded bedrock. The veins suggest that at least two secondary fluids were present, with the dark material reflecting an earlier fluid flow episode. The study estimates that Mars once contained at least 12.4 million cubic miles of water, more than the Arctic Ocean, for over 1.5 billion years. This discovery suggests ample time and water for life to thrive on Mars in its past, although 87% of its water has since been lost, leaving it barren and dry.

A 25-year-old man named Carl Bradey is being hailed as a hero for rescuing a three-year-old girl from a house fire that destroyed his rental property in Palmerston North last month. The fire, caused by a candle, left Bradey with extensive burns across his body, causing nerve damage in his right arm, and he lost his belongings in the blaze. Bradey is currently undergoing multiple surgeries and recovering at his mother's house, where he is receiving support from his loved ones. A crowdfunding page has been set up to help him rebuild his life. Fire experts advise using candles with caution, and the house has been demolished due to asbestos found in the property.

The article reports that thousands of olive trees in the Puglia region of Italy are being destroyed due to a bacterial infection, a move which has alarmed the European Union and led to France boycotting Puglian fruit and vegetables. This action is predicted to lead to olive oil shortages globally, including in Britain, and potentially push prices higher. The bacteria, called xylella fastidiosa, has caused widespread devastation in the region, with many ancient olive groves affected. The Italian government's plan to remove affected trees and stop the spread of the disease has been met with opposition from Puglian growers.

In Yemen, a border guard was killed and 10 others were injured in a cross-border fire exchange with militants in Saudi Arabia's Asir region, marking Saudi Arabia's first military death since it began airstrikes against rebels. Meanwhile, Houthi rebels seized the presidential palace in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden. Additionally, reports indicate that Yemeni special forces loyal to former President Ali Abdullah Saleh have arrived in Aden to secure the city.

Muhammed Tahir, 53, from Leytonstone, east London, was convicted of sexual assault after he intentionally targeted a young woman on the London Underground, rubbing his crotch and pot belly on her bottom. The incident, which was witnessed by undercover police officers, occurred on a hot summer's day in July 2020. Despite being found guilty, Judge Rebecca Poulet QC decided not to immediately imprison Tahir, instead giving him a six-month prison sentence suspended for two years, a 12-month supervision order, 150 hours of unpaid work, an £80 victim surcharge, and a five-year ban from using the London Underground during rush hours.

A Californian man named Robin Barton, who was abandoned as a baby and rescued by retired Santa Ana police officer Michael Buelna from a dumpster 25 years ago, recently met Buelna for the first time. Barton was adopted by Elizabeth Barton and Daniel Fernandez of Orange County and stated he felt blessed with a great family. Buelna, who was also abandoned by his mother as a child, shared a special bond with Barton and hopes to aid Barton in his search for his biological mother. Barton expressed a desire to meet his biological mother for closure, while Buelna was glad to see the grown man he saved.

A 16-year-old student, Courtney Brain, visited her GP for a water infection and was given a detention for half an hour of missed lessons. Her mother, Jane Burnham, criticized the school for penalizing Courtney, who has a high academic record and rarely misses school. The school claimed the detention was to give Courtney the best chance at performing well in her exams, but Mrs. Burnham believed the extra half-hour of revision wouldn't significantly impact her overall grades. The school's claim of a 91.2% attendance rate for Courtney was contested by her mother, who stated her daughter's attendance is 98%. The principal claims letters were sent out addressing concerns about students missing lessons for medical appointments.

A 53-year-old former naval serviceman, Graeme Finlay, was acquitted by a jury at Teesside Crown Court of beating two elderly holidaymakers in a dispute over perceived rudeness at a dinner table on a cruise ship, Thomson Celebration. The incident allegedly involved Finlay violently assaulting the retired engineer Ron Phillips, 70, and his wife June, 69, who suffered a gash to the forehead and fractured vertebrae, respectively. However, Finlay claimed self-defense, stating he was attacked by Phillips who wielded a crutch. He expressed relief and gratitude towards the jury's verdict, stating it had been a stressful period for him. The trial revealed that Finlay felt snubbed during dinner and alleged that the couple was rude to him, which led to the disagreement.

American Hayley Carney, a transgender woman, plans to move to the UK to marry a yet-unnamed partner and become a British citizen. She has dreamed of living in Britain since childhood, finding it more accepting of her identity. Hayley will undergo surgery, move to Plymouth, find employment, and follow proper procedures to earn British citizenship, with the vision of spending the rest of her life in the UK.

Diego Simeone, manager of Atletico Madrid, has expressed surprise at the absence of English clubs in the Champions League quarter-finals, as Chelsea, Arsenal, Manchester City, and Everton have all been eliminated. Simeone believes this situation is a wake-up call for the Premier League to reevaluate its performance. Despite his surprise, Simeone still believes Spain hosts the two best teams in Europe, with Real Madrid and Barcelona being amongst the last eight in Europe every season. In the upcoming quarter-final second leg, Atletico Madrid will face local rivals Real Madrid, without the injured players Karim Benzema, Gareth Bale, Luka Modric, and suspended player Marcelo.

David Cameron and Boris Johnson, known as a dream team for the upcoming election, faced a challenge while trying to complete a toddler-level jigsaw puzzle at a children's day nursery in Surbiton. Struggling with the puzzle, they were stumped and found finger painting to be a more manageable task. The visit was intended to promote a Tory pledge to double free childcare for working parents. The difficulties with the puzzle added an element of stress and humour to their campaign.

In a speech at the University of Queensland, Justice Diana Bryant advocated for a reform of Australian surrogacy laws to prevent cases of child abandonment, proposing that commercial surrogacy should be legalized to ensure ethical practices. This suggestion comes in light of international surrogacy cases like that of baby Gammy, where the surrogate mother was left with the child while the parents, who learned of the child's disability, brought home the healthy sibling. Justice Bryant believes that legalizing surrogacy in Australia would allow for better regulation and the chance for children born to surrogates overseas to know their biological parents, particularly in cases where their biological mothers will never meet them due to abandonment.

A kitten named Seven, who miraculously survived a seven-story fall in Zetland, inner-east of Sydney, is on the road to recovery. Initially found in a 'terrible state' with severe injuries, including a broken jaw, broken leg, broken hard palate, and bruised lungs, the cat was taken to My Vet Animal Hospital. The clinic shared Seven's story on social media, which led to a massive outpouring of support from the public. Hundredies of people donated funds to cover Seven's hefty medical bills, surgeries, and treatments, totaling over $3000. Having undergone two surgeries, Seven is currently learning to walk again at the vet clinic and is expected to be ready for a new home in about six weeks.

The TV show MasterChef crowned Simon Wood as its champion, a 38-year-old data manager from Oldham in Greater Manchester. During the final, he impressed judges with a three-course meal, marking the end of the eleventh series of the popular UK competition. Simon's win was especially significant as he had nurtured a dream of becoming a chef since he was eight. In other news, Kim Woodward made history as the first female head chef at the Savoy Grill, a prestigious London restaurant with a 126-year history. Previously a sous chef at the Savoy Grill between 2010 and 2012, Kim Woodward will now lead a team of about 35 chefs at the five-star venue, which is part of the Gordon Ramsay stable.

1. Hull City manager Steve Bruce acknowledges the need for "crazy results" to secure Premier League survival, with only a two-point cushion above the relegation zone after five games without a win.
2. Goalkeeper Allan McGregor is under pressure to retain his starting spot following a pair of costly errors in recent matches, with veteran Steve Harper pushing for a spot in the lineup.
3. Hull face a tough test against high-flying Southampton in the upcoming fixture, with manager Bruce expressing respect for Ronald Koeman's side and the club's overall organization.

Celebrity chef Bobby Flay, worth over $20 million, is reportedly offering his soon-to-be ex-wife, Law & Order: SVU actress Stephanie March, $5,000 a month according to the terms of their prenup. TMZ reports that she is 'mighty unhappy' with this arrangement, and the prenup also includes a clause allowing Flay to buy their $8 million marital home for $1 million, with an additional $50,000 for moving expenses. The marriage is said to have ended due to several incidents over the past year and a half, including Flay not visiting March in the hospital when her appendix burst. This is March's first divorce, while it will be Flay's third, following two previous divorces. There have been rumors of romantic liaisons involving Flay, including with fellow chef Giada De Laurentiis in 2014.

Australian modelling agencies are now prioritizing models with a strong social media presence, referred to as 'influencers' or 'bloggers', alongside traditional beauty and fitness requirements. This shift is due to the increasing client demand for models with impressive social media following. Agencies are creating separate 'influencer' and 'blogger' divisions in their portfolios to accommodate this new trend. Models with a significant number of followers, ranging from 10,000 to 300,000, are being considered for jobs, and some agencies, such as Vivien's Models and Chic Management, are even offering social media training to help models self-promote and increase their followers. This strategy is seen as a lucrative method for brands seeking rapid and organic promotions, particularly the 'cool girl' appeal associated with influencers. Notable examples include models like Gigi Hadid and Alexis Ren, who are in demand not just for their looks, but also their considerable online followings.

Hungarian architect Matyas Gutai, in collaboration with Milan Berenyi, has developed a prototype house using water as a primary material for temperature regulation. The house, built in Kecskemet, features a water-filled panel system that self-reheats, is energy efficient, and reduces carbon emissions. Gutai's vision aims to redefine permanence in architecture by creating adaptable structures instead of resistant ones. The project has addressed several potential issues such as freezing temperatures and panel breakage through inventive solutions like natural solvents and special joint units.
