The goal is to construct energy-efficient homes using this technology, though the initial cost may be higher than traditional designs.

Cardiff City has decided to forgo the attendance of supporters at their Championship game against Leeds United at Elland Road due to a perceived lack of reciprocity in ticket allocations. The decision follows a fan-led boycott campaign, which Cardiff City CEO Ken Choo supports. The reverse fixture in November saw Cardiff welcome 2,200 Leeds fans, and Cardiff is frustrated by the minimal ticket allocation for their fans in the return match. Leeds United has yet to comment on the matter, and the West Yorkshire Police have been criticized for restrictive ticket allocations in the past. Cardiff City requested to hold a 'beam back' of the game at their stadium, but this request was denied by Leeds United, further frustrating the Welsh club.

The article discusses Utah photographer Alan Lawrence and his 18-month-old son Wil, who has Down Syndrome. Initially, Lawrence felt negative emotions upon learning about Wil's condition. However, he now acknowledges that Wil brings a joyous energy to the family. Lawrence created a photo series titled 'Wil Can Fly,' where his son appears to be flying, using photography techniques to leave himself out of the images. The series, showcased on his blog and Instagram, has sparked a Kickstarter campaign to donate to Down Syndrome foundations. Lawrence aims to foster awareness about Down Syndrome, photographing Wil 'flying' in various destinations and sharing therapy tutorials on his YouTube channel for those without easy access to care.

The death sentences of 11 football fans were upheld following a retrial in Egypt over a 2012 stadium riot between Al-Masry and Al-Ahly fans, which resulted in 74 fatalities. The riot erupted after a league match between the two clubs, leading to widespread protests in Cairo which caused an additional 16 deaths. The final decision on their sentences will be made by the Grand Mufti on May 30. The riots, which were the deadliest in Egypt's football history, have been followed by violence, including a stampede this year that resulted in 22 deaths.

In the heart of Nima, a slum in Accra, Ghana, tech entrepreneur Regina Agyare teaches coding to local teenage girls every week at a mosque. She started this coding class in January 2014 as part of her mentorship initiative "Tech Needs Girls" and has since established a mentor scheme to recruit and train university women as role models. Agyare's classes aim to empower girls, break social barriers, and provide them with opportunities to shape their future. Her goal is not just to develop software developers but to enable girls to use technology to reach their full potential and bring change to their community.

A Wisconsin church's four-decade tradition of mud-wrestling pigs at a summer fundraiser, called the Original Pig Rassle, has been canceled due to complaints about animal abuse, including punching, body slamming, and throwing the pigs onto a barrel. The church has announced it will replace the tournament with a human mud foosball tournament during its 45th annual Roundup. The Global Conservation Group, an animal advocacy group, successfully launched a petition with over 81,000 signatures to end the event, claiming it was inhumane. The church has offered a statement recognizing the controversy and agreeing that the parish's talents would be better spent in less controversial areas.

Maria Sharapova has withdrawn from this weekend's Fed Cup semi-final against Germany due to a leg injury, and her last appearance was in the Miami Open at the end of March. Anastasia Myskina, Russia's Fed Cup captain, has to find a replacement for Sharapova, who had been looking forward to playing in the city where she grew up. Venus Williams has withdrawn from the USA's World Group play-off against Italy due to personal reasons, with Lauren Davis set to replace her.

A 36-year-old woman in police custody is suspected of kidnapping and murdering a 23-year-old mother, Samantha Fleming, in a plot to steal Fleming's newborn baby, Serenity. The suspect posed as a Child Protective Services employee and convinced Fleming to come to Gary, Indiana, where her body was later found wrapped in plastic and doused with bleach. police located Fleming's cell phone signal in Gary, leading them to the suspect's home, where they found Fleming's body. Remarkably, Serenity has been found safe and is now in the care of Fleming's boyfriend and other relatives. The suspect is currently under mental health care in a Texas hospital, with no charges filed as of yet. The suspect was reportedly preparing a nursery at her home in Gary and had claimed to be pregnant with twins.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered through newly released birth records that her biological mother, Francine Simmons, works at the same call-center company as she does and lives only six minutes away. After connecting on social media, the two women spoke for the first time, and Mitchell-Clark learned she has three younger biological sisters. The reunion was described as a relief and amazing by Mitchell-Clark's newly found sisters. Her adoptive parents have been supportive of her search for her biological parents.

The Icelandic duo, Búi Bjarmar Aðalsteinsson and Stefán Atli Thoroddsen, are seeking funding on Kickstarter for their new product, the Jungle Bar. Made with common ingredients such as dates, seeds, and chocolate, the unique aspect of the Jungle Bar is the inclusion of cricket flour. Claimed to be a rich source of protein and other nutrients, the cricket flour is sent in, farm-raised and ground down, to make the bars. The duo aims to promote eating insects as a dietary change in the Western world, highlighting the nutritional benefits of using edible insects. The Jungle Bar is free from common allergens like gluten, peanuts, dairy, and soy, and a box of six can be pre-ordered on Kickstarter. The duo previously gained attention for their Fly Factory, which breeds insect larvae for human consumption, with the aim of addressing global food shortages.

A 73-year-old reserve deputy, Robert Charles Bates, accidentally shot and killed Eric Courtney Harris during an undercover drug operation. Bates, who was monitoring the operation from a distance, believed he had a stun gun but instead pulled out his service weapon. Harris was allegedly meeting with undercover deputies to buy a 9 mm semi-automatic pistol and was killed after officers believed he was reaching for a weapon, causing concern for their safety. Harris has a history of criminal convictions, including escape from prison, robbery with a dangerous weapon, and making threatening phone calls. Bates, classified as an advanced deputy, has the same powers as paid deputies and can conduct investigations, make arrests, and work on task forces.

A Russian unmanned spacecraft, Progress 59, lost contact with flight controllers during a resupply mission to the International Space Station and is now expected to re-enter Earth's atmosphere between May 5 and May 7, carrying non-critical trash and wastewater. The vehicle's issues will not affect the six crew members on the ISS, nor will it pose a threat to the space station due to differences in their orbits. Russian flight controllers continue efforts to make contact with Progress 59, and Roscosmos plans to launch a new resupply ship by the third quarter of this year.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce has revealed that players' salaries will be significantly reduced if the team is relegated, with the team currently struggling in 17th place and facing a challenging run-in to avoid relegation. Bruce has emphasized that this financial measure is in place to protect the club from financial hardship in the event of relegation, as Hull has one of the lowest wage bills in the Premier League. Bruce is hopeful that key player Mo Diame will recover from a knee injury in time for important upcoming matches, but he remains doubtful due to the length of the injury and his underperformance since rejoining the team. Bruce has praised the job done by managers at Crystal Palace, the team Hull will play next, and is cautious about the potential for a surprising result despite Palace having little left to play for.

Leo Schofield, a 79-year-old restaurant critic and festival curator, expressed his unhappiest life experience was spent in Tasmania, where he settled to establish a Baroque music festival. He found the state's government unsupportive and cut the festival funding by 25%, which led to its discontinuation. Luke Martin, from the Tourism Industry Council of Tasmania, offered a contrasting view, labeling Schofield's comments about Tasmania as "blatant mistruths." Despite his struggle and grudge, Schofield has planned to dedicate a chapter in his memoirs to his Tasmanian experience, titled 'Revenge of the Bogans.'

The annual photography competition held by the Northern Territory Cattlemen's Association showcases the unique lifestyle and people of Australia's remote regions, providing an insight into rural living. The competition encourages participants to submit images that illustrate the region's distinct landscapes and outback lifestyle. In 2021, Marie Muldoon's touching photo "True Love" of her daughter cuddling a horse was the overall winner, taking home both the competition prize and the People's Choice award. Previously, in 2014, Jacynta Coffey won the competition with her image "Trucking," depicting typical station life, and also won the People’s Choice award with "Feeding the Bulls" and the NT Landscape category with "Sunset Storm." The competition emphasizes the recurring theme of the bond between humans and animals in rural Australia.

The book "Sex by Numbers: What statistics can tell us about sexual behavior" highlights various researches led by David Spielgalhalter, a Cambridge University professor. These studies aim to separate sexual myths from reality. Some findings include the average penis size when erect being around 5.2 inches in length and 4.6 inches in circumference, most men having 7 erections a day with 5 occurring during sleep, and an average ejaculation speed of 28 miles per hour. The book also debunks the idea that a larger penis equates to better sexual experiences.

Barnet secured promotion back to the Football League after a 2-0 victory over Gateshead, with Mauro Vilhete scoring two goals. Barnet manager Martin Allen, known as "Mad Dog", was involved in the intense game, with John Akinde missing an early chance. Despite some pressure from Gateshead, Allen's team maintained their dominance throughout the game, clinching the Conference title and ensuring Allen's fourth spell as manager would be his most successful. The play-off spots were finalized with Bristol Rovers, Grimsby Town, Eastleigh, and Forest Green Rovers qualifying, while Alfreton, Telford United, Dartford, and Nuneaton were relegated.

A missing college freshoman, Anjelica 'AJ' Hadsell, has been confirmed dead, with human remains found in Franklin, Virginia, around 40 miles from her home. The remains were sent to the Chief Medical Examiner's Office for identification and cause of death determination. Police have been investigating Hadsell's disappearance, with the FBI now involved, but there has been no evidence of foul play. Hadsell's stepfather, Wesley Hadsell, was arrested for breaking into a home, allegedly to search for Hadsell.

The article discusses Apple's rumored plans to use stronger materials, specifically a 7000 series aluminum, for the construction of its next generation smartphones, potentially the iPhone 6S and iPhone 6S Plus, in an attempt to avoid another 'bend gate' issue. This material is also used in the Apple Watch Sport edition and in competition bicycles. The stronger material is reported to make the next iPhone 60% harder than the iPhone 6. The article also mentions that the bend issue was observed in previous iPhones due to the phone's aluminum construction, with areas like the volume buttons and SIM card slot being particularly susceptible to bending. To prevent this issue, users are advised to avoid storing the phone in their back or side pockets, and consider using a case to maintain the phone's rigidity.

The article discusses the current state of European rugby, with Irish and French teams dominating the Heineken Cup since 2007, while no English club has managed to win it since. This season, English sides Northampton, Saracens, Bath, and Wasps find themselves in the last eight of the Champions Cup, but bookmakers favor holders Toulon and Clermont for the title, with Racing and Leinster as secondary contenders. The article highlights several challenges facing English teams, including smaller budgets and superior international talent in French clubs, as well as strong recent European pedigree and rested top players for Leinster. The article suggests that Bath and Saracens are the most likely English teams to progress, with Bath facing a tough challenge at the Aviva Stadium and Saracens expected to challenge Racing in Paris. If two English teams reach the semifinals, it would be a significant boost to national morale ahead of the World Cup.

Sam Pearce, a 24-year-old English teacher from Milton, Massachusetts, was discovered on a New York subway and signed with a modeling agency, RED NYC. While juggling his career as an eighth-grade English teacher in Brooklyn, he has modeled for top designers such as Alexander McQueen, Diesel Black Gold, and DKNY under the pseudonym Sam Worthen. Pearce maintains his teaching is his top priority and works with his agents to minimize conflicts between his two jobs. He has recently launched a fundraising campaign to buy new books for his students, using the attention his modeling career has brought to benefit his pupils.

An amateur astronomer, Gordon Ewen, captured a photograph of a sunspot that resembles a chick sitting on the sun's surface. Sunspots are common, occurring when a concentration of magnetic fields causes a reduction in surface temperature, making them visible. They range in size from 10 to 100,000 miles in diameter and can be seen from Earth without a telescope. Gordon Ewen, who previously worked in chemistry, set up an observatory in his garden after retiring and used a telescope to capture the photograph. Sunspots have a temperature of 2,700 to 4,200°C and are the source of solar eruptions such as solar flares and coronal mass ejections. The sun's activity goes through a periodic change known as a solar cycle, and the frequency of sunspots is affected by this cycle. Sunspots should not be confused with coronal holes.

Vladimir Putin is alleged to be preparing to employ nuclear threats and potential actions, including cyber attacks and ethnic tension exacerbation, to maintain control of the Crimean peninsula and deter NATO from intervening in nations bordering Russia. The reportedly secret meeting between US and Russian intelligence officials in Germany suggested Russia will respond forcefully, including with military force and nuclear weapons, to perceived encroachments on its territory, such as NATO's arming of Ukrainian forces and any attempt to reclaim Crimea. The immediate threat appears to be towards the Baltic states, especially Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania, due to their concern about Russian ambitions in the former Soviet territories.

Virgin Galactic hopes to test a new version of SpaceShipTwo by the end of the year, with the aim of improving on the previous craft that was destroyed in a crash in 2014. The new spacecraft is nearly ready, and could begin test flights this year. The crash, which resulted in the death of co-pilot Michael Alsbury and injury to pilot Peter Siebold, was due to human error, and the National Transportation Safety Board is yet to release a report on the incident. Celebrities among the 700 customers who have tickets for space travel include Ashton Kutcher and Leonardo DiCaprio. The previous White Knight II plane carrying SpaceShipTwo will likely be used again for the successor.

A refugee couple in Cloverdale, Perth, alleges that a neighbor launched a racially charged attack on their property, which led their children to question their identity. The incident, captured on video, shows the neighbor, a 51-year-old woman, verbally abusing the men, using racist slurs, and swinging a crowbar. The woman was charged with several offenses after the violent encounter went viral, but she maintains she was the victim of the altercation. The incident has left the refugee family, especially their children, traumatized.

Walmart is under scrutiny after a stolen rifle from one of its stores in Tuscon, Arizona was used in a shooting spree by Mario Valencia. This incident occurred on February 19, and despite protocols requiring weapons to be locked, Valencia was able to start firing the rifle shortly after he left the store. Police pursuing Valencia were informed that the gun was locked, but it was later discovered that the wire securing the weapon was only wrapped once, allowing it to be discharged. The gun was eventually recovered after Valencia was apprehended. Valencia, who had allegedly been on a crime spree, is facing several felony charges. Meanwhile, the pursuing officer, Officer Michael Rapiejko, was put on leave but was soon reinstated after the incident was deemed not to involve any wrongdoing.

A Wisconsin father-of-five, Peter Kelly, was stabbed to death during an argument with three other fishermen at the St Croix River. The argument started when Kelly and a friend asked the other fishermen to quieten down, which escalated into a heated verbal exchange over three hours. The stabbing occurred on the Wisconsin side of the river, and the attackers, believed to be in their late teens or early 20s, fled the scene in two vehicles with Minnesota license plates. Authorities are still searching for the attackers and are asking for public assistance. The loss is deeply felt in the small community of St Croix Falls where Peter Kelly actively volunteered as a coach for the high school's football, baseball, and wrestling teams. His wife, Christie, stayed at home to care for their four sons and a daughter, all under nine years old. The family is mourning the loss of this dedicated family man.

Holly Willoughby and Davina McCall have teamed up for their first campaign together, endorsing Garnier Nutrisse hair dye. In the campaign, they emphasize finding the perfect shade and show off their glossy hair in a playful photoshoot. Holly has launched a vintage-inspired clothing line for babies, spending 18 months in development. Meanwhile, Davina renewed her wedding vows with her spouse of 15 years, Matthew Robertson, in Las Vegas and embarked on a road trip with their three children.

1. The retirement and subsequent deaths of the Baby Boomer generation will lead to a rise in funeral debt due to increased death rates and rising funeral costs in Britain, as predicted by a report by the International Longevity Centre-UK.

2. The report suggests that younger generations, already struggling financially, will find it difficult to cover funeral costs, with funeral expenses having already risen by 80% over the past 10 years, and further increases expected.

3. Increasing funeral costs are attributed to a variety of factors, including the removal of mercury from cremated remains, rising undertaker bills due to bad debts and Church fees, and the added costs of extra services requested by families, such as memorial stones, flowers, and wakes.

The TSA's Aviation Security Advisory Committee found that full screening of airport employees nationwide would not significantly enhance overall system-wide protection. The report recommended strengthening employee vetting, expanding national intelligence collection, and increasing surveillance of employees working in sensitive areas. In response to a December incident at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, TSA Secretary Jeh Johnson announced immediate actions including increased random and unpredictable screening, strengthening employee background checks, and reducing access points to secure areas at all airports.

Raheem Sterling and Jordon Ibe were pictured smoking a shisha pipe together, joining other Premier League stars who have found themselves in controversy off the field. Jack Wilshere has been involved in multiple smoking incidents and a spitting altercation, including being photographed with a shisha pipe. Diego Maradona was suspended for 15 months in 1991 after a positive drug test and a subsequent heart attack was attributed to years of alcohol and drug abuse. Saido Berahino faced a drink-driving charge and was banned from driving for a year, while Kyle Walker apologized for inhaling a legal high during a night out. Robin Friday, a former Reading forward, was known for drug-taking, womanizing, fighting, and smoking, and retired from football at age 25 due to health issues.

The Ask Reddit thread invited members of the disabled community to share their experiences about well-intended actions by able-bodied individuals that unintentionally offended or belittled them. Common grievances include being labeled an inspiration, being praised for doing normal activities like going to university, insistence on 'help' without asking first, taking charge of their mobility equipment, accusations of faking disabilities, and unsolicited advice about diets, remedies, or cures. Additionally, bringing religion into discussions was deemed particularly offensive.

A team of German engineers led by DFKI Robotics Centre has developed the EOssc2, an innovative micro-car designed for mega cities. It can transform its size, turn on the spot, and move sideways like a crab to navigate tight parking spaces. The vehicle is planned to be semi-autonomous, allowing it to park itself. Currently, it has a top speed of 40mph and semiautonomous features such as a LIDAR sensor and cameras. The EOssc2 is being tested in both Bremen, Germany, and Dalian, China. Future plans include making it fully autonomous.

Middlesbrough secured a 2-0 home victory over Rotherham United, with goals from Lee Tomlin and Patrick Bamford in the second half. Tomlin opened the scoring with a clinical finish in the 50th minute, while Bamford doubled the lead six minutes later. Despite the win, Boro remained fourth in the Sky Bet Championship table due to other teams also securing victories. Late in the game, Bamford missed a penalty, preventing him from adding to his 16-goal tally for the season.

A Massachusetts police department, Tewksbury Police Department, was targeted by hackers who encrypted vital records on their computer network, forcing them to pay a $500 Bitcoin ransom to decrypt the files. The malware used was a variant of CryptoLocker, which infected the network through a phishing email. The department lost access to files including arrest logs, motor vehicle records, and calls for service. This is not the first case of a U.S. police department being a victim of ransomware, with similar incidents occurring in Swansea Police Department and Midlothian, Illinois. The Tewksbury Police Department chief expressed that the incident was an eye-opening experience and paying the ransom was the last resort.

A Chinese woman, Zhu Diandian, has garnered internet fame for sharing a close bond with her 187lb pet pig, Five Flowers. She often posts pictures of them sleeping together, and while her husband is said to be tolerant, her dog seems enviously watching from outside the bedroom. Zhu works at a publishing company in Beijing and cares for the pig, along with a dog and a rabbit. Her latest post of Five Flowers in bed has received high engagement, with comments ranging from appreciation to disapproval of keeping a pig as a pet.

A diner, Louise Smith, 38, has been convicted of fraud after secretly pulling hair from a young girl in a pub restaurant and planting it in her food in an attempt to get the meal for free. The incident occurred at the Crown and Thistle pub near Carlisle, Cumbria, last May, when Smith was eating dinner with the child and a man. The court heard that Smith did not have enough money to pay for the £21 dinner, and upon finding a hair in her food, she complained to staff, leading to the incident being investigated under Health and Safety rules. The hair did not match any of the staff's hair, and an arrest warrant has been issued for Smith, who is now on the run. The pub's licensees stated that their primary concern was the welfare of the child and the health and safety of their customers.

Thailand's Kiradech Aphibarnrat clinched his second European Tour title at the inaugural Shenzhen International, edging out Chinese teen prodigy Li Hao-tong in a playoff. Despite a late charge by Li, Aphibarnrat exhibited a remarkable finish, holing an eagle on the 17th, and though missing a birdie putt on the last in regulation, he returned to the 18th for the playoff where he sealed the win with another birdie. Aphibarnrat, who struggled for form over the past year, expressed his gratification following the win, acknowledging the support of his caddie.

The article discusses two of the most significant fights in boxing history: Floyd Mayweather vs Manny Pacquiao, which is expected to be the most significant fight this century financially and culturally, and Joe Louis vs Max Schmeling, a political war between America and Germany during World War II. The Louis vs Schmeling fight was notable for its racial and political undertones, as black America saw Louis as a high-profile campaigner for Civil Rights, and Schmeling, though originally a hero of the Third Reich, was anti-Nazi and even refused to sack his Jewish manager. Louis won the rematch by knocking out Schmeling in the first round, fracturing his spine with body attacks. The social picture was clouded further by the political tension between the two countries, with President Franklin D Roosevelt urging Louis to "beat the Germans." The fight was a turning point for both athletes, with Louis becoming a symbol of hope for a struggling America and Schmeling eventually becoming a hero in his own country for his resistance to Hitler.

The article discusses a newly released mobile game named None*, which presents users with a single clue and a keyboard, with no additional aids like images, music, or hints. The game is intentionally mysterious, with clues ranging from simple math problems to more complex riddles, such as name associations and coordinates. Despite its relative simplicity at the beginning, the game becomes progressively harder. Around 10% of users have completed the 50 levels in Episode One, and the creator, Dimitris Chassapakis, plans to release Episode Two in the summer. Feedback for the game is mixed, with some praising its challenge and others finding it frustratingly vague and without a clear answer.

The latest GCSE reform for foreign languages aims to make the learning process more contemporary and engaging by incorporating topics such as tattoos, music festivals, YouTube, and rap music. The new syllabus will include examining a gritty foreign film, analyzing Spanish tweets about the Olympic Games, and discussing radio broadcasts on rap music. The new approach is designed to improve students' linguistic ability and enjoyment, and will dispense with conventional topics like describing a family or holiday. The new content proposes drawing inspiration from methods used in teaching English as a foreign language, and may also include literature extracts, foreign food, and events like the Cannes Film Festival.

Danielle Davies, a mother from Morecambe, Lancs, gave birth to Harley, one of Britain's biggest babies, weighing 11lb 5oz, after an eight-hour natural labor without pain relief. Shocked midwives needed to weigh him multiple times because he was too large for their scales. Danielle had a blood clot on her brain a month before the birth, which required an induced delivery, but she managed the process without any drugs, surprising the staff. Harley is now already in size 2 diapers and fits into clothes intended for three to six-month-old babies.

A couple, Linda and George Hunter, who paid off their mortgage over decades, find themselves in a 'ghetto' due to a council regeneration scheme that offers neighboring homes for £1. Their home is now estimated to be worth significantly less than its market value, making it difficult to sell. Frustrated with being unable to sell or move, they want the council to honor their original offer from eight years ago. The council argues that the scheme to sell derelict properties at £1 is for their renovation and to revitalize the area, which will make it a more desirable place to live.

Celebrities celebrated Easter in a relatable manner, involving their families andfollowing traditional activities such as egg hunts, decorating baskets, and bakingtreats. Notable examples include Kim Kardashian preparing Easter baskets(possibly for her daughter North, niece Penelope, and nephews Mason and Reign),Mariah Carey baking Easter cupcakes for her twins Moroccan and Monroe, andMyleene Klass hosting an Easter egg hunt for her daughters Ava and Hero. Othercelebrities indulged in non-traditional Easter activities, with Sam Baileyadmitting to forgetting Easter eggs for her trip, Poppy Delevingne sharing afamily photo of her niece and nephew's excited Easter morning, and LaurenLaverne's son enjoying an Easter celebration with a Star Wars Darth Vadermask. Fearne Cotton received a flower arrangement from her mother-in-law JoWood.

A convicted fraudster named Gabrielle Yinka Saunders, who had previously been convicted of fraud twice, embezzled £17,000 from her employers, Insight Investments, where she worked as a personal assistant, using her colleagues' credit cards for expenses like her wedding, honeymoon, and personal items. Despite her history, she was spared jail, receiving a 15-month suspended sentence and 200 hours of unpaid work, after it was revealed she had repaid the stolen money and was now retraining as a teacher.

A man named PJ Spraggins lost 70lbs in a year to donate his kidney to his wife Tracy, who battles Lupus and was on a seven-year-long kidney transplant waitlist. However, initial blood pressure issues halted the operation. Determined to donate, PJ underwent a rigorous fitness regime, eventually passing the necessary health evaluations in December 2014. In February 2015, they underwent the transplant together at Vanderbilt hospital. Tracy is now enjoying a 100% functional kidney, while the couple recovers at home in Birmingham, Alabama. Friends have since established a fund to support them during the two-month recovery period.

A kind-hearted animal lover, Pauline Kidner, is caring for three abandoned badger cubs that were rescued by finding them food that includes custard creams, after one was saved from a Jack Russell. The cubs, named Little Star, Vogue, and Scrumpy, were underweight when they arrived but are growing at an astonishing rate thanks to Pauline's care. The cubs will be released back into the wild once they are strong enough, vaccinated against Bovine TB, and have adapted to nocturnal behavior.

Kimi Raikkonen, race-winner in 2007, believes Ferrari has a genuine chance to win the 2015 Formula One world title, thanks to a car that he finds satisfactory for the first time since 2014. Currently fourth, he has been improving on his podium-less stretch of 19 months, with two top-four finishes in the last two races. However, Raikkonen is aware that better qualifying performances are essential if he intends to challenge for the championship. In the recent Chinese Grand Prix, he could not catch team-mate Sebastian Vettel, who won a podium place, but Raikkonen remains optimistic about Ferrari's potential to consistently outperform Mercedes.

In the article, Stuart McCall, Rangers boss, urges his team to secure a win against Dumbarton this Saturday to maintain their push for second place in the Championship. The team recently drew 1-1 against bottom side Livingston, with Myles Hippolyte and Marius Zaliukas scoring the goals. The draw could prove crucial in the team's pursuit of second place, as Hibs face Falkirk in the Scottish Cup semis. McCall emphasizes the importance of a victory, aiming to go four points clear in second place. Meanwhile, Livingston manager Mark Burchill was disappointed with his team's defending, particularly after taking the lead through Hippolyte's freekick, which was later equaled by Zaliukas for Rangers.

Nigel Farage, the Ukip leader, plans to state in the European Parliament that allowing refugees into Europe might enable half a million Islamic extremists to pose a threat to Western civilization. He reasons that the high number of migrants attempting to reach Europe from North Africa could serve as a cover for potential terrorists. Farage's speech aims to highlight the potential issue of jihadis entering Europe, securing EU passports, and easily moving to Britain due to the current open-border policy, which he considers damaging and potentially more threatening than the eurozone crisis. If the EU approves refuge for North African migrants, this could lead to millions being given passports to move to Britain, according to Farage. His speech may be his final address in the European Parliament if he is elected as an MP for Thanet South. Additionally, Farage has been critical of the SNP, labeling them 'openly racist.'

Kai Windsor, a 10-year-old boy, was born as a girl and, from a young age, exhibited a strong preference for male-associated toys and activities. At the age of 3, Kai expressed feelings of not being in the right body, and by 6, he started to adopt traditionally male behaviors. Kai's mother, Rachel, initially found it difficult to accept her child's gender identity, but after observing his behavior and understanding his persisting discomfort, she supported him in accepting himself as a boy. Currently, Kai is set to undergo hormone treatment to halt puberty and avoid developing female characteristics. He is receiving support from his primary school, which is also making efforts to accommodate other children with similar circumstances.

A Hawaiian fisherman, Ron Ingraham, aged 67, is missing after his boat ran aground on rocks near Hawaii's Lanai island following a severe storm, just a few months after he survived 12 days lost at sea. Ingraham's son, Zakary, was notified by the U.S. Coast Guard. Earlier in December, Ingraham was rescued after drifting at sea following a storm on Thanksgiving. His sailing mate, Kenny Corder, survived and was rescued. Ingraham's disappearance follows a period of reconciliation between him and his son, after nearly 15 years of estrangement.

A father and son, Nicholas Pence (25) and David Pence (56), were shot dead in an apparent execution-style murder in their home in Metairie, New Orleans, after celebrating a victorious football game. The police have arrested two suspects, Dexter Allen (17) and Haraqyon Degruy (18), who reportedly have no significant criminal history. The motive and connection between the suspects and victims remain unknown. The community is shocked and saddened by the incident, describing the victims as outgoing and lively neighbors. The investigation is ongoing.

June Whitfield, known for her role as the eccentric grandmother in Absolutely Fabulous, is set to play the character Sister Ruth in EastEnders, offering encouragement to Kat Moon (Jessie Wallace) who is dealing with past sexual abuse. Whitfield expressed delight at working with Wallace. Timothy West, who previously criticized soaps for not valuing older characters, made his final appearance as Stan Carter last month. In recent months, EastEnders has been making an effort to include more older characters, with Linda Marlow joining as Sylvie Carter. Marlow indicated that this could be part of the reason for increased ratings, suggesting the show's core audience may be older viewers.

Lewis Hamilton, a Formula One racer, tops the 2015 Sunday Times Sport Rich List with a fortune of £88 million. Wayne Rooney, a Manchester United and England football captain, has moved up to second place with a wealth of £72 million, a significant increase of £12 million from the previous year. Jenson Button, another Formula One driver, is just behind Rooney with a fortune of £71 million.

Researchers at Yahoo Labs have developed a sensor technology called Bodyprint, which can identify users based on the unique shape of body parts like ears, hands, or fingers, turning a standard touchscreen into a biometric scanner. This obviates the need for specialist hardware such as fingerprint readers or infrared cameras. The technology aims to simplify device access, reducing the need for manual phone unlocking, and could potentially be integrated into device manufacturers' products in the future. During tests with 12 participants, Bodyprint classified body parts with 99.98% accuracy and identified users with 99.52% accuracy.

Belinda, a woman from Essex, experienced regret after a botched Turkish facelift left her with unsightly scars around her ears. She initially sought the cheaper procedure to address jowls, but the operation resulted in earlobes being sewn to the sides of her face due to incorrect stitching. Her subsequent corrective surgery, performed by plastic surgeon consultant Vik Vijh, requires another full face and neck lift to address ongoing scarring and potential nerve damage. Despite the challenges, Belinda expresses renewed happiness following the intervention, stating her scars have significantly reduced and she no longer worries about public appearances.

Chuka Umunna, the shadow business secretary, accused UKIP leader Nigel Farage of having a "problem with race" due to his remarks about "fully black" and "half black" UKIP supporters and the presence of far-right supporters at a UKIP event in South Thanet. Umunna claims UKIP whips up anti-immigration sentiment, is infected with the "virus of racism," and does not like "modern Britain." The row started after a group of far-right supporters called the East Kent English Patriots campaigned for Farage, with one of its leaders, Gary Field, having a criminal record for assault. Farage distanced himself from the group, stating they were not invited.

Model Maggie Rizer, 37, has returned to her fit physique just nine weeks after giving birth to her third child, daughter Cecilia Kathryn. She showcased her toned figure while playing on the beach with her two-year-old son Quinnlann Clancy, as evidenced in a shared Instagram post titled 'Boogie boarding with my baby.' Many online commenters expressed awe over her quick weight loss. Prior to the family vacation, she had shared a picture of herself working out on a Pilates reformer. Maggie and her husband Alex Mehran are currently enjoying a family vacation in an unidentified tropical destination with their children. Despite stepping away from modeling in 2004 due to financial mismanagement, Maggie continues to advocate for AIDS awareness, a cause driven by her late father's death from AIDS when she was 14 years old.

The article presents a survey revealing that British people eat an average of four servings of cheese a week, with cheddar being the favorite variety. The survey also found that many Brits enjoy cheese sandwiches frequently, with some even consuming whole blocks of cheese in one sitting. Additionally, it was noted that a significant number of office workers have identical lunches each day for over four years. To encourage experimentation with new tastes, food psychologist Greg Tucker suggests recipes for chicken and mango sandwich with mint raita, smoked ham and egg with capers, gherkins, and mustard mayo, and feta with avocado and roasted red pepper. These recipes were provided by Lurpak Spreadable.

A dress worn by Vivien Leigh in the 1939 movie Gone With the Wind, featuring a black zigzag applique, fetched $137,000 at auction. The dress, originally a slate blue-gray, has faded to light gray over the years. The dress, one of more than 150 items from the film, was part of the private collection of James Tumblin, a former hair and makeup department head at Universal Studios. The auction also saw a straw hat worn by Leigh sell for $52,500, a suit worn by Clark Gable sell for $55,000, and a black bonnet worn by Leigh and Olivia De Havilland sell for $30,000.

A Turkish Airlines flight from Milan to Istanbul made an emergency landing at Ataturk Airport today due to its engine catching fire, and passengers were evacuated safely. This incident follows a series of similar incidents recently involving Turkish Airlines flights. While attempting the first landing, the right side landing gear collapsed, causing the pilot to abort. The necessary investigation has been initiated to determine the causes of this incident. Additionally, on March 30, another Turkish Airlines flight made an emergency landing in Casablanca, Morocco due to a bomb threat, and on March 29, a flight to Tokyo was also the subject of a bomb threat.

Adam Leheup, a 34-year-old architect, was acquitted of rape and sexual assault charges at Blackfriars Crown Court. He had been accused of forcing himself on a woman he met on a dating app, with the alleged incident taking place hours after their first meeting. During the trial, Leheup claimed the woman 'freaked out' when he tried to comfort her about her saggy breasts, and he maintained that she had not explicitly objected to his advances. After a week-long trial, the jury found Leheup not guilty of the charges. He had been communicating with 35 women at the time and was regularly having sex with six of them, but the alleged victim was not among them.

Italian activist and artist AleXsandro Palombo has launched a campaign, #briefmessage, encouraging women to write their thoughts on gender violence on their underwear and share them via social media in a bid to challenge machismo. The responses have been diverse, ranging from defiant statements to simple affirmations about self-worth. The campaign has also seen some men participate, expressing solidarity and initiating a discussion about the importance of fighting gender violence and machismo. Palombo's work often addresses controversial issues with his vibrant and colorful art style.

Nick Clegg faced opposition from tuition fee protesters in Surbiton, London, as he criticized George Osborne's budget plans. Clegg warned that Osborne is "a very dangerous man" whose ideological approach would cause significant damage to the economy, particularly affecting the working poor. In a separate incident, Clegg also described David Cameron as a "classic traditional shire Tory" and expressed concern over Ed Miliband and Ed Balls' approach to public spending. During the same visit, a senior Treasury official, Danny Alexander, accused the Tories of hypocrisy for advocating tax cuts for the well-off while claiming credit for raising the tax threshold.

Sharon Edwards, a 55-year-old teacher, has been missing since March 14 in Grafton, NSW. Her car was found parked in her driveway, and her clothes were in the washing basket, suggesting a mysterious disappearance. Her family, including her husband John and sons Eli, Zac, and Josh, are struggling with this sudden loss and lack of information about her whereabouts. The police are treating the investigation as a homicide due to her absence of known enemies and lack of a history of mental illness. Essential clues, such as her wallet and handbag, are missing. The family has made an emotional appeal for information and holds grave concerns for her welfare, as it is out of character for her to disappear. The police are investigating the case and have asked for community assistance to find her.

A husband named Steven Nelms penned an essay celebrating his stay-at-home wife, Glorianna, for her work in raising their two-year-old son. He estimates the value of her contributions to their family, including childcare, cooking, cleaning, errands, and financial management, at around $73,960 per year. Despite this, he feels he "can't afford" her staying at home due to high childcare costs and that her income doesn't cover her worth, causing him a sense of guilt and shame. The essay concludes with a heartfelt expression of appreciation for his wife, calling her "more precious than rubies."

Prime Minister David Cameron on Thursday defended his election campaign, vowing to continue emphasizing Labour's economic threat and focusing on issues like jobs, business, and childcare. Tory donors and figures have criticized the campaign for a lackluster message and failing to pull ahead in the polls. A potential leadership change with Boris Johnson as the next leader has been speculated among senior Tory figures, with some planning a coup against Cameron if the Tories lose the election.

Two former Parma, Missouri police officials, Trish Cohen and Rich Medley, resigned from their positions following the election of Tyus Byrd, a black woman, as the town's mayor. Cohen and Medley allege that their home addresses were shared online by Byrd's family members, causing them to fear for their safety. Byrd, who denies any knowledge of these safety issues, also expressed confusion about why the city officials resigned. Both sides have stated that they did not wish to discuss the reasons behind the resignations and have not responded to requests for comment.

Johan Bavman, a photographer from Sweden, undertook a project to document fathers utilizing their country's offered parental leave, which includes 480 days of leave with 80% income compensation. He aimed to show the genuine experience of involved and devoted fathers, capturing the balancing act of parenting and career in realistic imagery. In his search for subjects, Bavman discovered that while many fathers take advantage of the program, a majority of Swedish couples still have women primarily staying at home. Bavman hopes to find 60 such fathers to feature in an exhibition and book.

The article discusses the tragic drowning of twin 18-month-old boys, Eli and Silas Keslar, in a canal in Yuma, Arizona. Their mother, Alexis Keslar, was attempting to swat away a bee and lost grip of their stroller, which rolled into the canal. Despite her efforts to rescue them, she was unable to reach the boys due to the steep banks and strong current of the canal. The boys were later found and rushed to a hospital where they were pronounced dead. A GoFundMe page has been set up to cover memorial and medical costs for the boys' parents, Mark and Alexis Keslar. The incident has highlighted the potentially dangerous nature of the canal, prompting authorities to caution others about the swift current and difficulty of climbing the canal embankments.

Arsene Wenger has not definitively decided whether to offer a new contract to injury-prone midfielder Abou Diaby, suggesting a potential future at Arsenal could be on a pay-as-you-play basis. Diaby made a recent comeback from injury but has made only 22 appearances in the last five seasons due to extended spells on the sidelines. Wenger also expressed hopes for contract extensions for captain Mikel Arteta and midfielder Tomas Rosicky, who have also been sidelined with injuries. During his career at Arsenal, Diaby has suffered 42 injuries and spent a total of 226 weeks on the sidelines.

1. Eden Hazard, considered the linchpin of Chelsea's impending Premier League title victory, showcased his growth as a player by scoring the crucial first-half goal against Manchester United, exhibiting improved finishing and defensive work.
2. Hazard's performance on Saturday, marked by a goal and a strong defensive showing, underscored his importance to the team in difficult situations and his evolution from a creator to a goal-scorer.
3. As Chelsea edges closer to the league title despite not playing at their best, manager Jose Mourinho may find it necessary to rest key players such as Cesc Fabregas and Nemanja Matic in the coming weeks, with United, despite dominating possession, lacking clear-cut chances and proving unable to match Chelsea's resolve. Wayne Rooney, who played in midfield due to injuries to the center-forward position, demonstrated his ability in that role, but his team, despite a commendable passing performance, struggled to provide the necessary impetus in challenging games.

1. At the Summit of the Americas in Panama City, U.S. President Obama and Cuban President Raul Castro had a historic, brief meeting on Friday night. This marked the first notable interaction between the two leaders in over 50 years.

2. The meeting was a significant step forward in the ongoing process of re-establishing diplomatic ties between the U.S. and Cuba. Both leaders have been commending progress towards normalizing relations.

3. The U.S. is expected to remove Cuba from its list of countries that sponsor terrorism, a major advance towards rebuilding diplomatic ties. However, the move has not been universally popular within the U.S., with some lawmakers expressing discontent towards engaging with what they perceive as a corrupt Cuban government.

A woman, Latisha Fisher, has been charged with second-degree murder after allegedly smothering her 20-month-old son Gavriel Ortiz in a bathroom at a Manhattan restaurant. Fisher reportedly told police she did so to protect him from being eaten by someone, stating she put him to sleep. Previously, Fisher had a history of psychiatric problems, including a diagnosis of schizophrenia following a 2011 stabbing incident. Despite this, she was evaluated as mentally fit as recently as last year and received positive evaluations for alternative sentencing program participation. Witnesses reported seeing Fisher with her hand over the baby's mouth in the bathroom before finding him unconscious and foaming from the mouth.

The panel for Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens was held at California's Anaheim Convention Center, where Carrie Fisher and Mark Hamill were present. Harrison Ford, the franchise's Han Solo, was absent due to recovery from a plane crash, while Peter Mayhew, who plays Chewbacca, was also there. The second trailer for the film was rolled out, and it was announced that Ford will be back for the movie. The newcomers John Boyega and Daisy Ridley were introduced, with Boyega possibly playing a Stormtrooper. A desert planet called Jaku was revealed in the trailer, and the film opens on December 18, 2015.

Bill Nye, the television personality and author known as 'the Science Guy,' joined President Barack Obama on Earth Day for a visit to the Florida Everglades aboard Air Force One. In a statement beforehand, Nye said he loves the smell of jet fuel. During the 1,836-mile round-trip flight, Nye, who designed an anti-vibration tube for Boeing's 747 planes, will have ample opportunity to experience the carbon emissions from the president's jet. The trip aimed to promote Obama's administration's commitment to reducing carbon pollution and preserving Florida's wetlands. However, some questioned the environmental sincerity of the trip due to the high carbon footprint of jet travel. GOP Governor Rick Scott also criticized Obama and Congress for not providing adequate resources to protect the Everglades.

Floyd Mayweather Jnr, the boxer, recounts how he told his friends about his ambition to make $100 million in one night, which they considered crazy. This becomes a reality as he breaks away from promoter Bob Arum and prepares for a fight with Manny Pacquiao, set to earn each over $100 million in Las Vegas on May 2. Mayweather takes pride in being his own boss during this most lucrative boxing fight. During a media workout at his Las Vegas gym, Mayweather and his team express confidence in their preparation for the epic collaboration. Despite the hype and anticipation, Mayweather remains calm and businesslike, understanding that his legacy is not solely defined by one fight. He has also noted that for Pacquiao, being smaller may lead to height-related neuroses, such as wearing shoe lifts. The fight is predicted to be exciting due to the stature of the two boxers and their respective careers.

Elderflower Fields is a family-oriented festival held in Pippingford Park, offering a mix of outdoor activities, luxury experiences, and emphasis on children's development in various areas such as music, sports, arts, and environment. The festival includes performances by various independent artists, workshops, and free activities like sports camps, storytelling, and rafting for children. A highlight is the So Sussex Sunday picnic featuring local produce. The festival also offers luxurious pampering services like spa treatments and hot tub experiences. Adult weekend tickets cost £95, child weekend tickets cost £45, and children under 5 go free. For more information and ticket purchasing, visit elderflowerfields.co.uk.

The Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Premier League team of the year for the 2014-15 season was announced, with Chelsea having six players selected. The team includes Jose Mourinho's men's entire back four, with center-backs John Terry and Gary Cahill joined by Branislav Ivanovic and Ryan Bertrand. In midfield, Eden Hazard, Nemanja Matic, Philippe Coutinho, and Alexis Sanchez were chosen. Up front, Tottenham's Harry Kane and Chelsea's Diego Costa were selected as strikers. Chelsea fans may feel aggrieved that not seven players were included, with Cesc Fabregas being a notable exception despite making 16 league assists this season, 12 more than Coutinho. The team also includes David de Gea, who has overcome a difficult start in English football to become Manchester United's most outstanding performer this season.

A 21-year-old father named Michael Owen, who had recently received a job offer and was preparing for his daughter's fifth birthday, tragically died along with his friend Kyle Careford in a road accident in East Sussex. The men's Renault Clio crashed into a church wall in Crowborough, leaving skid marks and a significant gap in the sandstone wall. Tributes and condolences have been shared for the two young men, with family and friends expressing their love and grief for the losses. Michael Owen, a father to a 5-year-old girl named Lily-Rose Iris, was remembered for his love and devotion to his daughter. Kyle Careford was thought to have died just before his 21st birthday, and one of the men is believed to have lost control of the car as it came round a bend. The incident has prompted an investigation by Sussex Police, appealing for witness information.

The article discusses the ongoing concerns about Manchester City's performance and direction, as reflected by their fanbase, celebrities such as Ricky Hatton, and music icon Noel Gallagher. The team's fans are seen as not fully embracing the idea of City being European giants. Manuel Pellegrini's management is being questioned, with critics arguing he lacks the necessary character and gravitas to galvanize the team during tough times. Notable losses, such as the one against Manchester United, have led to speculations about Pellegrini's future. The article also criticizes the team's recent signings as being small-time, with players like Jesus Navas not living up to the expectations of a team aiming for Champions League domination. The article suggests that City needs to think bigger, make significant signings, and consider managers with a proven track record of greatness, such as Diego Simeone, Jurgen Klopp, or even Carlo Ancelotti. The ultimate goal is for City to push beyond their current level and compete for European glory.

A 39-year-old Irish mother of two, Kim Callaghan, lost over ten stone after feeling her size was causing her to look masculine. Worried about her shape and losing her femininity, she adopted a diet and exercise routine that led to a decrease in her weight from 20st 3lb to 9st 10lb. As a result, Kim, who is now a size eight, feels confident enough to wear dresses and has a more feminine appearance compared to her previous wardrobe of masculine-styled clothes. Kim, who initially hid her body in baggy clothing after her children's births, has since thrown out her double deep-fat fryer, replaced greasy foods with healthier options, and takes part in regular exercise.

In Miami, a police investigation revealed baggage handlers at Miami International Airport have been going on shopping sprees with passengers' luggage, unknowingly being recorded by hidden cameras. This is part of an ongoing issue of insider theft at the airport. The Miami-Dade Police Department is taking proactive measures to combat the problem, and the airport's Aviation Director emphasizes that such thefts are the exception among employees. However, this issue is not unique to Miami, with significant claims of missing valuables from checked luggage reported at other major U.S. airports, such as John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York. The problem of luggage theft extends beyond airport workers, with incidents reported of outsiders stealing luggage from carousels in various cities.

Marla McCants, a woman who weighed 800lbs due to a spiraling weight gain triggered by a past kidnapping event, stood for the first time in years on the season finale of My 600lb Life. After a lengthy hospital stay and gastric bypass surgery, she initially refused to cooperate with medical professionals, who saw it as a crucial step towards saving her life. However, realizing it was her last chance, Marla managed to stand for a few seconds with the help of a walker, a life-changing moment that kickstarted her recovery. This milestone was made possible by the support of her daughter Sierra, who had pleaded with Dr Younan Nowzaradan, Marla's weight loss expert, to help her mother. Marla, a mother of three, had previously depended on her daughters for constant care due to her morbid obesity and the associated health issues.

1. New findings suggest that Mars may still have liquid water close to its surface, with salts like perchlorate potentially allowing water to remain as a briny liquid.
2. Researchers are investigating evidence, including sediment deposits, found by NASA's Mars rover Curiosity, which indicates that Gale Crater may once have been a huge lake on Mars.
3. The presence of calcium perchlorate in Mars' soil, discovered by Curiosity, is essential to the theory that water can exist on the surface of the red planet, but the challenging conditions on Mars currently make it inhospitable for life.

Efforts are ongoing to find 11-year-old Luke Shambrook, who has been missing since Good Friday from a campsite in Victoria, with searches focused in the thick bushland areas around Lake Eildon. Luke, who is autistic and was last seen wearing a beanie and warm jacket, is believed to still be alive after four days missing. Searches involve a variety of rescue teams, campers, and volunteers, with hopes that Luke has managed to stay warm amidst dropping temperatures. The family expressed gratitude for the search efforts and suggest that Luke may not be aware he is lost. The police are confident that he could still be found in the significant bushland area.

Nicola Sturgeon, Scotland's First Minister, has voiced her support for transferring all tax powers to Holyrood, a move that could result in a potential £7.6 billion budget shortfall for Scotland due to reduced North Sea oil revenues. This could lead to higher taxes, deeper spending cuts, or unsustainable borrowing levels. Sturgeon's call for fiscal autonomy was met with concern from Labour leader Jim Murphy, who argued that such a move would create a catastrophic hole in Scotland's budget. The debate took place in Aberdeen, and participants included leaders from various political parties, such as Ruth Davidson (Conservative), Willie Rennie (Lib Dem), and Patrick Harvie (Green). The conversation revolved around the concept of 'full fiscal autonomy,' with critics claiming it is similar to independence by another means.

The Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sex Abuse in Rockhampton, Queensland, has heard harrowing accounts of victims who suffered physical and sexual abuse while they were at Neerkol orphanage near Rockhampton, ran by nuns and priests. Allegations include being raped with a broom handle, gang raped, and forced to drink their own urine. A former nurse claimed she was punched, slapped, and flogged, while a victim identified as AYL stated she was raped more than 100 times by Reginald Durham. The commission is investigating historical allegations of child abuse at the Neerkol St Joseph's Orphanage, which operated between 1885 and 1978. Many former residents have struggled to erase the horrible memories.

The Kentucky Derby at Churchill Downs on May 2 has banned selfie sticks due to safety concerns, particularly for the horses and large crowd. This is a growing trend among cultural institutions and sporting events worldwide, including the Coachella and Lollapalooza music festivals, Premier League stadiums, and the Smithsonian museums. Churchill Downs still encourages selfies but asks attendees to find alternative means to capture their photos without the use of selfie sticks.

The Mercedes-Benz Fashion Week Australia concluded on Thursday with Johanna Johnson's Hollywood-inspired Sirens' Call presentation. The event showcased a mix of trends, from wearable designs to peculiar ones, with dominant themes being metallics, voluminous silhouettes, and slouchy comfort. Couture creations by designers such as Galanni, Steven Khalil, and Johanna Johnson dazzled spectators with intricate details and show-stopping designs. Notable beauty trends included face bling, revealing designs, and eccentric headwear. Unusual accessories sometimes overshadowed the designs, with headpieces, masks, and atypical hair styles generating head-scratching reactions. The event also saw a few quirks, such as the theft of tablets intended for front row guests. Some designs were deemed too daring, while others were hailed as must-haves for the upcoming season. Overall, the week was a display of fashion's creativity, extravagance, and willingness to push boundaries.

Prince William, who recently began working as a pilot for East Anglian Air Ambulance, plans to take two weeks of paternity leave when his second child is born later in April. The Duchess of Cambridge, on the other hand, will spend her maternity leave primarily at Kensington Palace and will give birth at the Lindo Wing of St. Mary's Hospital, as planned. Contingency plans are in place should the Duchess go into labor outside of London. Meanwhile, the couple is grateful for the public's warm wishes and anticipation for the birth of their second child, who will be fourth in line to the throne.

Leanne Kenny, a 23-year-old woman from Northwich, Cheshire, lost seven stone after realizing her unhealthy habit of taking home discounted junk food from her job at a supermarket was contributing to her weight gain. Leanne, who began working at the Co-op as a checkout girl at age 16, ballooned to almost 20 stone and was unable to fit into the largest size in stores. A turning point came when she couldn't fit into a size 24 dress in a store, which led her to join Weight Watchers, start walking, and make a drastic change to her lifestyle. Leanne has now shrunk down to 13 stone, dropped four dress sizes, and regularly visits the gym.

Ed Balls, a Labour shadow chancellor, has faced criticism for dismissing as a joke the infamous 2010 note left by Liam Byrne in the Treasury saying "I'm afraid there is no money," which has been seen as a symbol of Labour's fiscal irresponsibility. Balls argued the note was merely a joke and maintains Labour will reduce the annual deficit of £90 billion. He has also accused David Laws, a Lib Dem minister, of leaking the note, saying it was intended as a private, humorous remark. The Tories have condemned Balls for his comments, seeing it as evidence of Labour's disregard for public trust and lack of understanding of the need for economic reform.

The pursuit of journalists for allegedly paying public officials to secure information was discontinued in a string of cases due to lack of public support. The Old Bailey case against nine reporters was dropped after another jury acquittal, with Director of Public Prosecutions Alison Saunders admitting the public has little appetite for jailing journalists who expose public interest matters. This decision sparked a blame game between prosecutors, police, and politicians, with some pointing fingers at the Leveson inquiry and MPs for whipping up a storm against the Press. The CPS is still pursuing three journalists from The Sun, while 23 have been cleared, had their cases dropped, or had their convictions quashed or foundered at the Court of Appeal. The accused public officials, including police, prison officers, and Ministry of Defence staff, have seen 21 convictions.

The district attorney in Nashville has banned the practice of offering female sterilization as part of plea deals, a controversial practice that has occurred four times in the past five years. While critics have labeled this practice as "evoking a dark corner of American history," the use of sterilization in plea deals involves a voluntary choice by defendants and is different from the forced sterilization of the mentally ill or "deficient" that occurred in the past. The constitutionality of sterilization as a punishment is unclear, but it may be permissible in plea deals if defendants willingly choose it, even if it could be deemed cruel and unusual. The current outrage may be due to the fact that these sterilization plea deals primarily involve female defendants, unlike the historical practice of sterilizing men.

A federal judge has sentenced former Blackwater security guard Nicholas Slatten to life in prison for his role in a 2007 shooting that resulted in the death of 14 Iraqi civilians. Three other guards, Paul Slough, Evan Liberty, and Dustin Heard, were each sentenced to 30 years and one day in prison for charges including manslaughter, attempted manslaughter, and using firearms while committing a felony. The judge rejected arguments for leniency from defense lawyers and rejected a prosecution motion to increase the sentences. The guards were convicted in October for their involvement in the killings that caused an international outcry in Nisoor Square, Baghdad. The legal fight over the case has spanned years, and the sentencing is unlikely to end the legal wrangling.

Islamic State militants in Mosul, Iraq, brutally beheaded four men accused of theft in a public square. The men, who may have been ISIS members, were first interviewed and photographed before their execution. The punishment was significantly harsher than the usual punishment for theft, which involves having one's right hand chopped off. The executions were carried out in front of a bloodthirsty crowd including children, and the decapitated bodies were later put on public display. U.S.-led forces conducted airstrikes against ISIS targets in Iraq and Syria. Iraqi forces have recently liberated key cities from ISIS control, but there are concerns about potential retribution and rights violations against local residents when these areas are retaken by the government. Government forces, along with Shiite militias, are now expected to target either Anbar province or Ninevah province, home to Iraq's second-largest city, Mosul.

The Labour party is experiencing internal divisions over its proposed 50p top rate of income tax, with Shadow Business Secretary Chuka Umunna advocating for it to be a temporary measure rather than a permanent one. This contrasts with Ed Miliband's more ideological stance to maintain the rate. The disagreement arises from concerns about the impact on businesses and the overall tax burden, as well as the need to present a more confident and positive case for deficit reduction. Ed Balls, Labour's Shadow Chancellor, also emphasizes the need for the new top rate to be temporary. Meanwhile, the Scottish National Party has pledged to support the 50p rate. Additionally, Ed Balls has criticized the Conservative Party's manifesto for making unfunded promises amounting to £25 billion annually, which he claims is equivalent to £1,439 per working household in Britain. George Osborne, the Chancellor, has dismissed these criticisms and has not ruled out reducing the top tax rate back down to 40p.

Bristol City, currently leading Sky Bet League One, have mathematically secured promotion to the Championship, having defeated Bradford City 6-0 at Valley Parade. The season has seen them achieve a third aim set at the start of the season, which was to win the Johnstone's Paint Trophy. Aden Flint, a key player in the team's success, has been central to their defense and scoring set-pieces, netting 11 goals this season. They still have a chance to become champions if they win against Coventry City this weekend. The team's success this season has been a result of a collective effort, with a strong team spirit, and the club's owner, Steve Lansdown, is planning to expand the Ashton Gate home to make it Premier League-ready, aiming to elevate the club to a higher league in the near future.

The article discusses the historical marginalization and erasure of Armenians, often reduced to jokes or footnotes, and their attempts to gain recognition for their plight during the Ottoman Empire's mass killings, which is considered the first genocide of the 20th century. Recently, the Kardashian family, particularly Kim Kardashian, visited Armenia and brought attention to the tragedy, with Kim Kardashian's family background highlighted in the media. This renewed attention has brought some pride to Armenians, but the community continues to push for acknowledgment of the genocide, particularly from the U.S. government and President Obama. Despite setbacks, the Armenian community vows to continue speaking out and seeking justice.

The article discusses a social media controversy that occurred when Janet Street-Porter, a British journalist, posted a tweet joking about a Nicola Sturgeon lookalike. The Tweet prompted backlash from Sturgeon's supporters who criticized Street-Porter with numerous insults. Street-Porter argues that the response indicates a culture in Scotland where Sturgeon is idolized without criticism, akin to a leader in a repressive communist state. The author laments the lack of civility and free speech in political discourse, particularly in relation to the SNP and their handling of criticism, as well as their hypocrisy in accepting donations while advocating for progressive values.

The article discusses England fans' singing of anti-IRA songs during a friendly match against Italy in Turin, noting a sizeable number spilled on to the street outside to sing it. This behavior is a concern for the FA, who are dealing with the fallout and debating how to handle the issue. The anti-IRA chanting is a tradition that dates back to football trips overseas and has been a source of embarrassment and strained relations with Ireland. The article also touches upon the FA's loyalty scheme for traveling fans, which has been met with criticism for rewarding those who attend home games instead.

Arkansas Governor Asa Hutchinson, a former US Congress member, announced he won't sign a religious freedom bill, citing influence from his politically liberal son Seth. Seth, who works for the Texas State Employees Union, communicated his opposition to the bill, urging his father to veto it. The bill, which was passed by both houses of the Arkansas legislature, was criticized for potentially allowing discrimination against the LGBT community. The White House also expressed concerns about the bill, stating that it could be used to justify discriminating against individuals because of their sexual orientation. Governor Hutchinson sent the bill back to lawmakers for amendments that would bring it more in line with the 1993 federal Religious Freedom Restoration Act, which better protected the rights of gays and lesbians.

Hillary Clinton has officially announced her candidacy for the 2016 U.S. presidential election, signifying a significant milestone in the pursuit of gender equality. If Clinton wins, her victory will mark a vital step forward for women's political inclusion. However, if she loses, the perceived failure could perpetuate the myth that women cannot win major elections and potentially discourage other female aspirants from pursuing political leadership. The author argues that while Clinton's candidacy doesn't necessarily determine the status of gender equality in the U.S., she has unwillingly taken on the role of a litmus test for true gender equality, a burden no female candidate ought to bear.

1. The Clinton Foundation, led by Hillary Clinton who is now running for president, has announced it will continue to accept donations from foreign governments, but will limit these donors to six nations: Australia, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, and the United Kingdom.
2. The foundation will stop holding CGI meetings abroad and most foreign governments will no longer be allowed to sponsor programs. Donations will now be disclosed every quarter instead of annually.
3. Despite the change in policy, concerns persist about potential conflicts of interest, particularly with longtime U.S. allies such as Saudi Arabia, which has donated to the foundation in the past, yet suppresses dissent and women's rights, and could still participate in the Clinton Global Initiative. Additionally, one of the six nations, Canada, has pushed for the approval of the Keystone XL pipeline, a contentious domestic issue.

The article discusses the trend of major brands shrinking their product sizes, with examples including Cadbury's Fingers, Creme Eggs, PG Tips tea bags, and John West tuna. This practice, known as "shrinkflation," allows manufacturers to increase profits without raising prices. However, consumers may feel frustrated as they are receiving less product for the same price. Critics argue that this is a deceptive strategy, particularly when manufacturers claim that size reductions are guided by health or efficiency concerns. The consumer watchdog Which? has highlighted many shrunken products, including Surf washing powder, Cif spray, Hovis bread, and Mars Bars.

On April 23rd, celebrations marking St George's Day took place across England, with participants donning traditional attire and waving flags. Events included Morris dance performances, veteran parades, and a Royal St George Society parade in Nottingham. 200 people attended the Nottingham parade, which kicked off with Morris dancers. In Emsworth, Hampshire, the 12th Regiment Royal Artillery led a parade, which also celebrated the 70th anniversary of the end of World War II. The festivities were enjoyed in modest temperatures, which were slightly warmer than last year, but are expected to drop towards the weekend.

Manchester City rebounded from their recent derby loss by defeating West Ham 2-0 at the Etihad Stadium, with an own goal by James Collins and Sergio Aguero's 20th Barclays Premier League goal of the season securing the victory. Notable performances included Jesus Navas, who had an improved display, and Eliaquim Mangala, who performed well in his first game back from injury. West Ham's Adrian was their best player but the visitors struggled to create chances and were outplayed by the home team.

1. Wedding preparations are underway for tennis champion Andy Murray and his fiancée Kim Sears, with a choice of decor inspired by that of Prince William and Kate Middleton's royal wedding, as trees are being used to decorate Dunblane Cathedral for their nuptials this weekend.
2. The town of Dunblane, Scotland, is eagerly anticipating Sears and Murray's wedding, with bunting adorning the streets and special-themed produce being created to celebrate the occasion.
3. Local businesses and friends have contributed thoughtful gifts for the couple, with Kim Sears expressing gratitude for a hand-embroidered and crystal-covered garter sent by shop owner Lesley Anderson.

Andy Murray lost to Novak Djokovic in the Miami Open final, marking Murray's seventh consecutive defeat to his rival. Murray pushed Djokovic hard, taking the match to a third set, but ultimately lost 7-6 4-6 6-0. The match was notable for Djokovic's aggressive play and Murray's struggles against the fierce sun. Despite his defeat, Murray has had a successful week and is currently ranked No. 3 in the world. Djokovic, on the other hand, extended his stretch as world No. 1 to 141 weeks, tying Rafael Nadal for sixth place on the all-time list.

The Siezen family, a New Zealand-based couple, have transformed a truck into a mobile castle-home complete with a rooftop bathtub, ensuring it meets minimum road requirements. The truck-home, equipped with a functioning shower, composting toilet, and a spacious kitchen, is a project merging art and engineering for the family, particularly useful for their traveling lifestyle due to Jola's job as an acrobat. The family continues to develop and add features to their unique home over time.

A 26-year-old Mexican woman named Elizabeth Elena Laguna Salgado, who recently moved to Provo, Utah to study English, has been missing since April 16. Despite no evidence of kidnapping, her absence for over a week is concerning to Provo Police Chief John King. Elizabeth's family, including her uncle Rosemberg Salgado, have pleaded for public help in finding her. Notably, Elizabeth is a former Mormon missionary who recently finished a mission in Mexico. Elizabeth Smart, a kidnapping survivor and advocate, along with her father, have joined the search efforts to raise awareness. Anyone with information regarding Elizabeth's whereabouts is encouraged to contact the Provo Police Department. A Facebook page has been created to share updates on the missing person case.

World heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, preparing for a title defense against American challenger Bryant Jennings, expresses deep concerns about the ongoing crisis in Ukraine, where he sees his homeland suffering from war with Russia. Klitschko is upset and shocked about the violence, particularly as it has divided Ukrainians and Russians. Despite this, he remains hopeful that Ukraine can establish a democratic future with the support of the international community, and does not want to return to a Soviet-era dictatorship. Klitschko's personal life has also experienced a significant change with the birth of his daughter with actress Hayden Panettiere. His plans for retirement are unclear, but he is determined to continue advocating for peace in the world.

A 21-year-old woman, Jamyra Gallmon, has been charged with first-degree felony murder over the stabbing death of David Messerschmitt, a 30-year-old Washington D.C. lawyer, in an upscale hotel. Gallmon, a former student at Forestville Military Academy in Maryland, was caught on surveillance video entering the hotel shortly after Messerschmitt texted his wife that he would be home in an hour on February 9. Police believe that the death was motivated by a robbery. Messerschmitt's wife, Kim Vuong, has publicly appealed for help in finding her husband's killer.

The article discusses the opinion of a female businesswoman, Cheryl Rios, who believes a woman's hormones make her unfit to be president, citing potential irrationality that could lead to unnecessary wars.
