Three British men, Conrad Clitheroe, Gary Cooper, and Neil Munro, were arrested in Dubai for plane spotting at Fujairah Airport and imprisoned for two months. They were accused of espionage but were later released after their attorney argued that their actions were harmless hobbyism. Conrad Clitheroe, who suffers from a heart condition, will now be able to return home to celebrate his first wedding anniversary. The case gained attention with the aid of the charity 'Detained in Dubai'.

The article discusses the high-tech F-35 Lightning II jet, which is equipped with a $400,000 helmet that provides pilots with a 360-degree view and the ability to 'look through' the aircraft. This is achieved through six infrared cameras mounted around the plane. However, issues with the helmet's development led to its price tag being significantly higher than the original budget. The helmet, like the jet itself, is part of one of the most complex weapons systems ever, with up to 8 million lines of software code compared to the F-22 Raptor's 1.7 million. Despite these challenges, the helmet, and the F-35 more broadly, is considered a game-changer in airborne warfare due to its stealth capabilities, versatility, and advanced electronic warfare functions.

The Conservatives have gained a four-point lead over Labour in the latest ComRes poll, with 36% of the vote, while Labour trails behind with 32%. Millions of voters are yet to decide on their choice, making the election race the tightest since 1992. The Liberal Democrats are experiencing a significant drop in support, with 8% of the vote, whereas Ukip has 10% and the Greens have 5%. A majority of Britons (57%) and 70% specifically disagree that having smaller parties in government is undemocratic or that a hung parliament gives too much power to smaller parties. However, there is a significant number of Conservative voters (46%) who believe another hung parliament would give smaller parties too much sway.

James Holmes, a former neuroscience doctoral student, is on trial for a mass shooting at a Colorado cinema in 2012, where he killed 12 people and injured 70 others after opening fire during a midnight showing of "The Dark Knight Rises." He is accused of wearing body armor and using multiple guns, including an AR-15 rifle, while wearing a gas mask. Holmes claims he was mentally ill at the time of the shooting and is pleading not guilty by reason of insanity. The trial is scheduled to begin Monday, and the jury consists of 12 jurors and 12 alternates, mostly white, middle-aged adults. The trial could last until the autumn. Holmes' family describes him as a clean-cut, well-behaved boy from a normal upbringing who seemed destined for academic success, but they also report concerns about his mental health in the months leading up to the shooting.

The Premier League leaders Chelsea host Manchester United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, with the title bid for Jose Mourinho's side relying on late interventions in recent matches. Louis van Gaal's United, meanwhile, are on a roll and aiming for the Champions League. Key questions regarding player form and motivation, such as Juan Mata's impact on United against Chelsea, Angel di Maria's chances of a comeback, and the performance of the Colombian duo Falcao and Cuadrado, are major talking points. The game could significantly impact the title race if United win, leaving Chelsea seven points clear of Arsenal ahead of their meeting, and United missing out on Champions League qualification. The confrontation between Mourinho and Van Gaal, two of the biggest personalities in football, adds an extra layer of excitement to the weekend's big match.

Glenn Mason, a former NatWest bank manager, was jailed for 15 months for stealing £185,000 from nine elderly customers to fund his internet gambling addiction. He has pledged to pay back the entire amount from his RBS pension pot. The stolen money was used for late-night poker and online gambling. The bank has already refunded the customers and will receive the money as compensation. Mason's actions had a significant impact on the community and caused personal tragedy, but his good character and previous personal hardships were considered during sentencing.

The article reveals the results of a survey conducted by Ripley's Believe It or Not! where participants voted their preferred celebrity choices for various family roles. David Beckham was chosen as the preferred celebrity father, Holly Willoughby as the preferred mother, Ed Sheeran and Channing Tatum as the preferred brothers, Adele and Rihanna as the preferred sisters, while Helena Bonham Carter and David Walliams were selected as the preferred aunts and uncles, respectively. Rhianna was also a popular choice for a celebrity sister. The survey also found that participants value characteristics like trust, kindness, and unconventionality in their ideal celebrity family members.

In South Africa, violent attacks against immigrants have resulted in at least five deaths and forced over 2,000 people to flee their homes. This wave of violence began in Durban two weeks ago and has since spread to Johannesburg. Immigrants, weaponized with machetes, have clashed with police, while vigilantes have targeted shops owned by immigrants. Many immigrants feel unprotected by authorities and are arming themselves in response. The government and others have condemned the attacks and expressed concerns about the country's high unemployment rate, widespread poverty, and porous borders potentially fueling such incidents. In response, Malawi and Zimbabwe have started efforts to repatriate affected citizens. Peace marches and calls for an end to the violence have been held in several cities.

Royal Dutch Shell Plc has filed a complaint in a federal court in Alaska seeking an order to remove Greenpeace activists who climbed and occupied the Polar Pioneer oil drill rig, bound for the Arctic, in a protest against Arctic drilling. The six activists, from various countries, boarded the rig, 750 miles northwest of Hawaii, and plan to stay for several days, unfurling a banner with names of millions opposed to Arctic drilling. Shell accused Greenpeace of illegally and dangerously boarding the rig, endangering both the crew and activists.

A fashion photographer, Ian Pettigrew, is creating a photography book, titled Salty Girls, featuring portraits of 56 women with cystic fibrosis (CF) to bring awareness to the life-threatening disorder and inspire children and teens with the condition. Pettigrew, himself a CF patient, was inspired to start the project after realizing he had more female subjects in his previous book. The women in the project, aged between 20 and 40, share their struggles and triumphs, hoping to inspire others with the disease. The project's name, Salty Girls, was inspired by the fact that individuals with CF produce more salt in their sweat.

Bruce Jenner, who won the Olympic gold in the 1980s, started a gender transition process in the mid-1980s which included hormone therapy, electrolysis, and plastic surgery to make his features more feminine. However, after meeting Kris Kardashian, he stopped the transition due to fear of publicity and shame. Jenner postponed his gender transformation plans and married Kris, with whom he had two children. This story was highlighted in a two-hour ABC special with Diane Sawyer on Friday night, where Jenner publicly addressed his personal journey and transition to living as a woman.

Jamelia, a Loose Women panellist, has faced criticism for suggesting that high street stores should not cater to larger sizes, specifically beyond size 20. She clarifies that she was referring to "extreme sizing" and was advocating for healthier lifestyles for young people. Her co-panellists defended her, with Ruth Langsford stating they were not discussing sizes smaller than 18. Jamelia later apologized for any offense caused and stands by her remarks, emphasizing that she supports inclusivity and the right for people to feel beautiful. Overall, she reiterates her concern for promoting unhealthy lifestyles on a broader scale.

England dominated a farcical tour match against St Kitts Invitational XI, with Alastair Cook scoring a century and England declaring with a massive 320-run lead. The match was drawn, but the performance of St Kitts highlighted the steep decline of Caribbean cricket. The match served as a warm-up for England's upcoming Test series, but its meaninglessness raises questions about the value of such fixtures. The only concern for England was the form of batsman Gary Ballance.

Jordan Spieth, a 21-year-old golfer, showcased an exceptional performance at the 79th Masters by scoring a 64 in the opening round, making him the youngest first-round leader in Masters history. Justin Rose, 34, and Ernie Els, 45, put up a strong fight with scores of 67, but Spieth managed to maintain a three-shot lead for the second round. Notable golfers like Rory McIlroy, defending champion Bubba Watson, Dustin Johnson, and Phil Mickelson had less stellar appearances, leaving them several strokes behind the leading Texas talent. Spieth's round was characterized by sustained accuracy, numerous holed putts from various distances, and a touch of good fortune.

An axe-wielding robber identified as Shaun Andrew McKerry, known as "Boomerang Boy" for his history of repeated offenses since the age of 11, was subdued by a shopkeeper and his wife during an attempted robbery at a post office in County Durham. McKerry, who has committed over 1,000 offenses, was foiled when the shopkeeper, Sab Dhillon, rugby tackled him and his wife followed with a baseball bat after hearing McKerry's demands. CCTV footage shows the incident, and McKerry faces sentencing on April 24. His criminal history includes various offenses such as burglary, assaulting a police officer, attempted robbery, shoplifting, and countless breaches of curfew.

The article describes an incident where Ryanair steward Fernando Miguel Andrade Viseu stole a £499 Nikon camera left on a flight and listed it on eBay. The camera's owner, primary school teacher Aaron Galloway, discovered the listing while searching for a replacement camera and messaged Viseu, who confessed to the theft and admitted working for Ryanair. Aaron contacted the police, and Viseu was arrested and charged with theft. The court ordered Viseu to attend a drug rehabilitation program, impose a community order, and do 100 hours of unpaid work, and Ryanair has since terminated his employment. Aaron was upset about the loss and destruction of personal photos on the camera.

Julie Creffield, a size 18 runner, was once discouraged by her doctor and heckled while training for a marathon. Despite this, she completed a marathon in 2012 and has since done numerous races. Now, she encourages other women through her website, The Fat Girl's Guide To Running, to take up running regardless of their size and ability.

A survey found that two thirds of women believe they can't run, yet 88% would like to be fitter. To combat this, the ITV show This Morning launched the Run For Your Life campaign in collaboration with Julie and marathon runner Nell McAndrew. The campaign aims to show women they can run regardless of their fitness level or body size, and encourages them to improve their physical and mental health through running.

This Morning will follow three novice runners as they train for five weeks to run 5K, and the show encourages viewers to join them on the journey by taking up running themselves. Many women believe their size is holding them back from running, but by taking up the sport, they could potentially lose weight and improve their health.

Cruise ship passengers experienced a two-day ordeal at sea on the Carnival Spirit as they were trapped during Sydney's storm of the century. The ship, carrying 2,500 holidaymakers and 1,500 crew, faced huge waves as high as 40 feet, leaving many seasick and traumatized. Finally, this morning, a Sydney harbour pilot boarded, and the ship safely docked at the Overseas Passenger Terminal around 10am.

Jessa Duggar, a 22-year-old star of the TLC show "19 Kids & Counting," announced that she is pregnant with her first child with husband Ben Seewald. The couple is expecting a baby on their wedding anniversary in November. The announcement doesn't come as a surprise, as fans had suspected the couple might be expecting due to a Facebook photo that was uploaded in late March showing Ben holding Jessa's stomach. The baby will be the sixth grandchild for the Duggars. The family is famously pro-life and shuns birth control; Michelle stopped taking birth control after she miscarried early in her marriage and has not used it since. The Seewalds, who live on the Duggar property, are planning to be parents, and are still considering adoption. Despite the pregnancy, their plans to adopt have not changed. The couple went on a honeymoon to Venice and Paris, which will be featured in an upcoming episode of "19 Kids & Counting."

A team of students at Rice University has developed a device named Comfortably Numb, which rapidly numbs the skin to ease the pain of an injection. The device is a 3D-printed device containing the chemicals ammonium nitrate and water, producing a rapid endothermic reaction within 60 seconds to numb the skin. The team aims to offer relief for people who fear needles and have previously avoided medical care. The device is inexpensive, single-use, and has potential applications beyond medical injections, including tattoos and ear piercings. The students are in the process of applying for a patent and plan to continue working on the project in their second year.

The article discusses the media's tendency to refer to Hillary Clinton as "Hillary" rather than by her full name or official titles, a practice that has continued despite her distinguished career in politics. This trend is contrasted with the formal manner in which candidates like Rand Paul and Marco Rubio have been addressed when announcing their presidential bids. The piece argues that this casual approach reinforces gender stereotypes and risks infantilizing Clinton, undermining the formality and respect required for the role of U.S. President. The article suggests that calling Clinton by her first name could hinder rather than help her election, as it prevents the American public from imagining a female leader without focusing on her gender.

Madonna kissed Drake onstage during her Coachella performance, but the 28-year-old musician appeared horrified and wiped his mouth afterward. The kiss was a last-minute decision by Madonna, and while sources later claimed that Drake enjoyed the kiss, it was reportedly his discomfort with her lipstick that turned him off. The kiss occurred while Madonna sang Human Nature to Drake, and was followed by her sauntering offstage without acknowledging his reaction. The age difference between the two, with Madonna being twice Drake's age, may have contributed to the unexpected and controversial kiss.

The grand National race at Aintree was won by Leighton Aspell on Many Clouds, making him the first rider since 1953 to win the race in consecutive years on different horses. Previously disillusioned with the sport, Aspell expressed gratitude for his 18-month hiatus that recharged his batteries. Many Clouds was owned by Trevor Hemmings, who also won the race in 2005 and 2011. AP McCoy, a popular favorite, finished the race in fifth place on Shutthefrontdoor. The defeat spared the bookmakers an estimated £50 million in bets on McCoy and Shutthefrontdoor. The race saw various early exits, with the unluckiest horse being The Druids Nephew, who was leading powerfully before falling at the 26th fence.

1. A leaked email from Hollywood PR Peggy Siegal suggests that the Academy Awards judges did not want to give the Best Picture Award to the film "12 Years A Slave" because it was not patriotic enough towards America, with concerns about a British director portraying the US negatively.

2. The email also reveals that plans for a Hollywood adaptation of the television series "Doctor Who" are in the works, but not for several years.

3. The emails were part of a larger database of documents and emails hacked from Sony Pictures Entertainment and later uploaded to WikiLeaks, causing controversy and damage to Sony's reputation.

Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has demanded that all sanctions on Iran be lifted simultaneously with any final agreement on curbing Tehran's nuclear program. He made his first comments since the interim deal reached in Lausanne, suggesting a cautionary approach towards the U.S., alluding to 'deceptive' intentions. Khamenei did not express a formal stance on a deal, claiming that details and potential restrictions could present issues. President Hassan Rouhani also reiterated that all economic sanctions must be lifted on the first day of the agreement implementation. Some officials have expressed concern over the immediate lifting of sanctions, fearing an influx of funds for Iran to arm regional proxies. The U.S. State Department maintains that sanctions will be lifted gradually as commitments are met.

A woman, Ranette Afonso, is set to marry Marko Conte, whom she met after he accidentally crashed into her car while she was parked, waiting for her husband to return. The fateful encounter led to a romantic connection and the pair began regularly texting shortly after the accident, which occurred in August 2013. Ranette, a lawyer, was going through a divorce at the time but found herself drifting closer to Marko. On their third date, just two months after the accident, Marko proposed and she accepted. They are planning to marry this October.

A remote Iron Age fort built by the Picts on a 20-foot-high sea stack in Scotland has been uncovered. The fort, featuring Pictish designs, appeared to have been used for extended periods and may have played a role in the Pictish dominance of the sea. Researchers believe it could be a precursor to Dunnottar Castle and part of a series of forts along the coast. The fort can only be accessed by climbing the cliff face with ropes, and evidence suggests it may have had a wooden bridge for easier access. The team plans to examine artifacts found at the site to learn more about its inhabitants.

A Texas A&M, Galveston professor, Irwin Horwitz, announced he would fail his entire strategic management class due to alleged cheating, disruptive behavior, and rudeness. Horwitz's emails to students and administrators detailed these issues, including personal insults, unfounded rumors, and fights among students. University officials have stated that across-the-board failing grades will be re-evaluated, and students who pass academically will not be failed. Horwitz, who has taught for 20 years, called the class behavior "disgraceful" but will not teach the class again at the Galveston campus. The department head will teach the rest of the semester, and grades will be based on academics.

Laura Everley, a 36-year-old mother, was diagnosed with ovarian cancer after recognizing her symptoms listed in a Facebook post. She had been experiencing bloating, back pain, constipation, and frequent urination, which she initially attributed to irritable bowel syndrome and endometriosis. After seeing a similar post about ovarian cancer, she realized her symptoms could be indicative of cancer. A hysterectomy revealed the cancer had already begun to spread, and she is now undergoing chemotherapy. Mrs. Everley hopes her story will raise awareness of ovarian cancer symptoms, particularly since they can be difficult to recognize in the early stages due to their similarity to less serious conditions.

A waitress named Agnese Klavina has gone missing following a night out at a celebrity club in Puerto Banus, Spain. Her disappearance is believed to be linked to Westley Capper, the son of a multi-millionaire property developer, who allegedly drove her away from the club. A court summons was issued for Capper on suspicion of her illegal detention, however, he refused to answer questions during a hearing yesterday. Both Capper and his co-accused, Craig Porter, have been questioned over the case but neither has been formally charged. Evidence includes a blonde hair found in the boot of the car, CCTV footage, and a possible connection to a motorboat belonging to Capper's family. The investigation is ongoing, and new DNA tests are expected to be ordered.

The article discusses the sentencing of Gavin Thorman, a drugs kingpin who operated his empire from prison, HMP Altcourse. Thorman was jailed for 12 years after being caught speaking about his drug trafficking operation in Welsh. His plans included spending money on cosmetic surgeries and taking over the town of Wrexham. The conspiracy involved the supply of cocaine and cannabis from Liverpool and Manchester, with drugs worth nearly £200,000 being seized during a five-year investigation. The 26-member gang was one of the largest to operate in North Wales, and the sentencing was the most significant in the region, with the participants receiving a total of 127 years imprisonment.

A 21-year-old man named Chris Ball made a heartbreaking final goodbye video to his family before taking his own life, expressing love and asking them not to blame themselves. Chris was suffering from depression and had been hospitalized twice, but was sent home on a shortage of beds. His family is calling for more beds for suicidal youths in hospitals and is raising awareness to prevent similar tragedies. Chris's mother, Kerrie Keepa, has lost four family members to depression and is advocating for emergency suicide training and more mental health resources in hospitals.

The individual claiming responsibility for the Gone Girl-like kidnapping of Denise Huskins in California has stated they will surrender upon immunity for their co-conspirators. This offer comes after the group expressed displeasure with the police labeling the incident a hoax. The kidnappers, who are linked to a series of burglaries and car thefts, allege the abduction was a training exercise, not targeted at Huskins. They have denied any intention to cause harm and claim it was a case of mistaken identity. Their attorneys have provided evidence to support their claims, although police and the FBI have not yet commented on the emails.
